    # Implementer rules �?" read before touching code
    
    ## Order of authority
    
    1. Measured physical-hardware behavior > independent hardware trace > documented specification > existing emulator behavior > hypothesis.
    2. User's explicit decisions: native Azahar integration (**not Libretro**), Rust + GPUI, multiple isolated workers, two Azahar branches (`integration`, `experimental`).
    3. Preserve compatibility and successful baselines before speculative accuracy changes.
    
    ## Attribution
    
    Agents never insert their own branding as a commit attribution or co-attribution. All commits are authored solely by the git identity already set on the authors computer. For example, the project owner's git identity should always be `terezi <jules@foxtails.me>`.
    
    ## Documentation
    
    Agents should keep documentation and comments as brief as possible. This does not mean spare on technical details. Explain what it is, what it's doing, how it works, what it isn't, and the relevant necessary information.
    
    Agents must keep documentation consistent.
    
    Agents must always be able to refer back to primary sources (such as 3DBrew, the citra wiki, source code citations from azahar) to justify changes or decisions. Agents are encouraged to use secondary sources, such as Coffeepot, for easy lookup of information - coffeepot, however, should not be your citation.
    
    ## Branch discipline
    
    - `integration`: only smallest viable native worker/front-end hooks, configurable build target, deterministic control queue, frame/audio/input adapters, and proven bug fixes required for integration. No GPU timing redesign or pervasive tracing. Regular upstream merges.
    - `experimental`: based on `integration`; structured tracing, debugger controls, snapshot experiments, timing models, hardware-fidelity experiments. Never merge `experimental` wholesale into `integration`.
    - Any item that seems essential to integration but introduces accuracy behavior changes needs an ADR and separate two-step PR.
    - Freeze upstream baseline SHA and CMake options in each test report. One independent worktree/build directory per branch. Never build both using one configured CMake cache.
    
    ## Evidence and debugging
    
    - Never confuse host milliseconds, virtual 3DS ticks, and empirically inferred hardware cycles.
    - Never claim a new accuracy feature without a hardware witness, an independent reference, and a counterexample where the old behavior differed.
    - Any cross-thread mutable emulated-state read MUST run at a defined safe point or return a labeled approximate telemetry snapshot.
    - Instrument with bounded buffers, severity filters and loss counters. Avoid `printf` in hot paths. Measure instrumentation-on/off overhead.
    - A GPU draw capture must describe the actual command/state at the draw, not a post-frame memory reconstruction. Pre-draw hashes must be computed by the draw or use frozen memory snapshots; never hash unrelated time-dependent registers as image identity.
    - Label examples explicitly: **verified compiled**, **verified hardware**, **verified emulator**, **source inspected**, or **proposed**. No unverifiable green check marks.
    
    ## Implementation quality
    
    - Prefer a narrow PR with a runnable acceptance test over a broad refactor.
    - Keep the C++ worker free of GPUI, MCP, and agent concepts.
    - Keep FFI structs plain, fixed-width and versioned; do not expose `std::string`, `std::vector`, `Core::System*` or internal layouts across IPC.
    - No unsandboxed remote RPC listener by default. MCP/control access local-only and scoped to explicitly created workers.
    - Treat ROMs, firmware, save data, logs and captures as sensitive user assets. Do not upload them, bundle them, or include them in bug reports without consent.
    - On worker crash, retain logs and metadata, invalidate frame-buffer leases, terminate child descendants and release per-instance locks.
    - Do not implement experimental multi-instance support by embedding two Azahar `Core::System`s in one process: globals and lifetime assumptions are not cleared.
    - Avoid speculative architectural abstractions that lack a second backend or a concrete test.
    
    ## Definition of done for every PR
    
    1. Explain touched subsystem, expected change, and branch rationale.
    2. Enumerate upstream source revision and build flags; tests and known untested platforms.
    3. Include a test that would fail without the change (or justify an instrumentation-only PR).
    4. Record guest output hash/checkpoints and host overhead for performance-relevant changes.
    5. Confirm clean shutdown, second launch, and two parallel workers if shared process/storage infrastructure changed.
    6. Update docs/source-map and protocol schema for altered interfaces.
    7. Make limitations explicit; retain rollback flag for risk-bearing work.

    # 29 �?" Wave 3 plan: comprehensive agentic debugger
    
    Status: **proposed**, 2026-11-15. Tickets and their Deliver/Check/Avoid terms
    are in [15](15-implementation-tickets.md); this document holds the goal,
    decisions, Azahar parity matrix and milestone order. No item here is
    implemented; source facts below are **source inspected** at the native pin in
    `config/pins.toml`.
    
    ## Goal
    
    LOTUS + CITnLO must meet or exceed every debugging, configuration and
    inspection capability of Azahar, exposed uniformly through the worker
    protocol, CLI, MCP and desktop, so that an agent can find and explain guest
    bugs without the Qt frontend. "Exceed" means capabilities Azahar lacks:
    rewind, session forking, predicate stops, symbol-aware debugging, matrix
    runs, and a single arbitrated control model across GDB, MCP and desktop.
    
    ## Decisions (owner, 2026-11-15)
    
    | ADR | Decision | Consequence |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | ADR-008 | **GDB server is written in Rust** (`crates/gdb`) on top of the Lotus debug API; Azahar's stub is not used | CITnLO workers build with `ENABLE_GDBSTUB=OFF`; HIO is rerouted to the worker debug channel. Multi-session, non-stop and reverse execution become possible |
    | ADR-009 | **Offscreen Vulkan worker from the start of Wave 3**; software renderer stays as default-safe fallback and oracle | New headless presentation path; `graphics_api`, `resolution_factor`, `physical_device` and hardware-renderer GPU debugging become real |
    | ADR-006 (unchanged) | **Old 3DS is the default profile**; New 3DS is a fully supported, explicitly labeled profile | Every test that touches CPU, scheduling or memory layout runs on both profiles |
    | ADR-010 | **Settings schema and transport live in `integration`**; debugger and accuracy toggles that change behavior are exposed but not altered there | Both AZAHAR and CITnLO accept profiles; default profile reproduces today's behavior byte for byte (proven by T24 check) |
    | ADR-011 | **Audio is in Wave 3**: audible output, capture, HLE/LLE DSP and mic injection | Supersedes the muted-only profile in [25](25-wave-status.md) |
    
    ADR-010 rationale: a settings channel is a frontend adapter (allowed in
    `integration` by [03](03-azahar-branches.md)); keeping it there means the
    AZAHAR backend can serve as a control in matrix runs (T41) with identical
    profiles. Any setting whose *default* would differ from stock still needs its
    own ADR.
    
    ## Source facts that constrain the design
    
    | Fact | Source | Effect |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Azahar GDB stub binds `INADDR_ANY` | `src/core/gdbstub/gdbstub.cpp:2125` | Violates local-only rule; another reason for ADR-008. Build-flag test must prove the stub is absent |
    | HIO request enters via `svcBreak`-family path into `GDBStub::SetHioRequest` | `src/core/hle/kernel/svc.cpp:1178`, `gdbstub/hio.h` (152-byte `PackedGdbHioRequest`, libctru layout) | CITnLO patch forwards the request address to the debug channel; Rust server implements the `F` reply |
    | Worker forces software renderer, Old 3DS, stub off | `src/ctr_worker/frontend.h:61-64` | Defaults move into the T24 default profile instead of hard-coded writes |
    | `is_new_3ds` read at boot (memory mode, cores) | `src/core/core.cpp:401,461` | Apply class `boot` |
    | `cpu_clock_percentage` applied live | `System::ApplySettings`, `core.cpp:876` | Apply class `live` |
    | Vulkan instance accepts `WindowSystemType::Headless`, but `PresentWindow` always creates a surface | `vk_instance.cpp:136`, `vk_present_window.cpp:104` | T45 adds an offscreen presenter with readback into the frame ring |
    | LLE DSP selected from `audio_emulation` at system init | `core.cpp:661-662` | Apply class `boot`; firmware is a user asset in the session root, never bundled |
    | CFG values (username, birthday, language, country, sound mode, play coins) live in CFG save data, not `Settings::values` | `configure_system.ui`, `hle/service/cfg` | Apply class `cfg-savedata`; written through the CFG module before boot |
    
    Every other setting's apply class is determined in T24 by reading where it is
    consumed; none is assumed.
    
    ## Parity matrix
    
    Azahar column names its frontend action, setting or interface. Each row must
    be reachable from worker protocol, CLI and MCP (T44 enforces this);
    desktop coverage follows in T17.
    
    ### Execution and CPU
    
    | Azahar | LOTUS | Ticket |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Pause / Resume / Stop / Restart | Existing, plus typed stop reasons and debug lease | T25 |
    | Debug Step, Advance Frame | Instruction step, step over/out, run-to, frame advance; per-core semantics stated | T14c |
    | GDB `Z0/Z1` breakpoints | Execute breakpoints with conditions, hit counts, logpoints | T14a |
    | GDB `Z2/Z3/Z4` watchpoints | Read/write/access watchpoints with cost estimate and cap | T14b |
    | GDB `g/G/p/P/m/M`, RPC Read/WriteMemory | Register and memory read/write, JIT invalidation | T14d |
    | Registers widget | Snapshot including CPSR/SPSR, VFP, mode, thread | T14d |
    | (none) disassembly | ARM/Thumb disassembly with raw bytes and symbols | T14d, T14h |
    | GDB stub (whole) incl. HIO, `qXfer:threads`, `osdata`, `vCont`, attach next process | Rust RSP server, loopback only, per-session port | T26 |
    | `use_cpu_jit`, `use_fastinterp` | Profile settings (JIT / fast interpreter / interpreter) | T24 |
    | `cpu_clock_percentage` | Live setting, labeled as virtual-clock scaling | T24 |
    | `is_new_3ds` | Boot profile; Old 3DS default | T24 |
    | `enable_exception_handler` | Crash/exception reports with backtrace | T14g |
    
    ### Kernel, services and system

    | `deterministic_async_operations`, `async_fs_operations` | Determinism profile | T29 |

    | Install CIA, Setup System Files, Boot HOME Menu, NAND/SDMC folders | Content tools confined to session roots | T31 |
    | Cheats (Gateway) | List/add/enable cheats | T31 |
    | Load/Remove Amiibo | NFC injection | T30 |
    | Compress/Decompress ROM, ROM bundles | Content tools | T31 |
    | Log filter, regex filter, instant log, console | Per-session structured log stream, `svcOutputDebugString`, HIO stdout | T27 |
    | Profiler (microprofile), `record_frame_times`, RPC GetPerfStats | Perf stats, frame times, scopes; host and guest time separate | T32 |
    
    ### State, replay and input
    
    | Azahar | LOTUS | Ticket |

    | Quick Save/Load, slots, RPC Save/LoadState | Named savestates keyed by pin + profile hash | T28 |
    | Record/Play/Close Movie, read-only mode | Movies integrated with scenarios; determinism check | T29 |

    ## Wave 0 - pin sources and reduce integration risk
    
    ### T00 [RUST] Repository skeleton and toolchain lock
    
    **Deliver:** Cargo workspace, empty crates, `rust-toolchain.toml`, source-version manifest, CI format/check. **Check:** `cargo test --workspace` passes; no network downloads at runtime. **Avoid:** implementing service APIs before machine boundary is known.
    
    ### T01 [INT] Fork/worktree policy and stock baseline
    
    **Deliver:** `integration` branch from selected upstream SHA, `experimental` from integration, immutable stock checkout; patch inventory; build matrix. **Check:** stock Azahar builds and launches homebrew fixture; revisions recorded. **Avoid:** moving branches as build inputs without pinned hashes.
    
    ### T02 [RUST] GPUI screen spike, no emulator
    
    **Deliver:** standalone GPUI app with generated native-resolution top/bottom images, scaling, touch coordinate tests, memory/perf observation. **Check:** 10-minute continuous updates, 4 simulated sessions, two high-DPI scale factors. **Avoid:** native Vulkan interop in this ticket.
    
    ### T03 [RUST] Protocol scaffold and supervisor stubs
    
    **Deliver:** envelope schema, handshake, typed status codes, local pipe/socket transport, mock worker, process lifecycle state machine and unit tests. **Check:** invalid messages rejected; worker crash detected; stale epoch rejected; GUI-independent CLI can query mock. **Avoid:** encoding C++ pointer values into protocol.

    **Files:** root `CMakeLists.txt`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`, new `src/ctr_worker`. **Deliver:** `ENABLE_CTR_WORKER=OFF` default; executable linked to native libs. **Check:** Qt-off/Libretro-off build; stock build behavior unchanged. **Avoid:** modifying `citra_libretro`.

    ### 3.1 CPU, kernel and system
    
    ### T14 [EXP] CPU, kernel and thread debugger
    
    Split into separately reviewable PRs; one fixture per PR.
    
    - **T14a execute breakpoints:** exact address, process, ARM/Thumb; JIT halt/invalidate; conditions, hit counts, non-stopping logpoints; invalidated on reset/load.
    - **T14b watchpoints:** read/write/access ranges through the memory path; range cap, overhead estimate, loss accounting.
    - **T14c stepping:** step, step over/out, run-to, frame advance; documented per-core behavior (New 3DS cores).
    - **T14d state editing and disassembly:** register (GPR, CPSR, VFP) and memory writes with JIT invalidation; ARM/Thumb disassembly with raw bytes.
    - **T14e kernel inspection:** processes, threads, wait objects, handle tables, memory map, deadlock graph; per-thread and all-thread suspend/resume.
    - **T14f SVC/IPC trace:** schema-decoded service commands, raw fallback, guest-tick durations; parity with the IPC recorder.
    - **T14g exceptions:** guest exceptions, aborts, `svcBreak`; report bundle with registers, nearby memory, recent IPC/GPU events and backtrace; guest and host failures labeled separately.
    - **T14h symbols:** ELF/DWARF from the user's build; symbolized disassembly/backtraces; file:line breakpoints.
    
    **Check:** deterministic crash fixture yields the same stop reason/context on each run and both profiles; robustness list in [07](07-debugger-core.md); perf A/B with debugger idle. **Avoid:** global instruction-by-instruction logging; fabricated source lines.

    ## Architectural decisions still to research
    
    - Exact worker ownership of separate renderer/audio threads; benchmark best race-free safe-point boundary.
    - Whether real renderer exports native screen buffers conveniently without render-to-surface changes.
    - Whether a shared immutable shader cache is safe across worker processes.
    - GPUI texture import API viability; postpone until native-frame pipeline has measured limitations.
    - Complete save-state fidelity across worker revisions; scripted checkpoint remains fallback.
    - Independent native firmware boot path and distribution constraints.

    /# lotus
    
    powered by CITnLO (CITra n LOtus), an experimental azahar fork
    
    lotus is a 3DS emulator for writing and debugging homebrew with agents
    
    currently, this is more of a debugging and MCP wrapper around azahar.
    
    eventual goal is to replace azahar/CITnLO with a more hardware-accurate emulator.
    
    documentation lives in [docs/index.md](docs/index.md); terms are defined once in [docs/glossary.md](docs/glossary.md).
    [workspace]
    resolver = "2"
    members = [
        "crates/protocol",
        "crates/session",
        "crates/trace",
        "crates/debugger",
        "crates/runner",
        "crates/hardware",
        "crates/accuracy",
        "crates/mcp",
        "crates/cli",
        "crates/desktop",
    ]
    
    [workspace.package]
    version = "0.0.1"
    edition = "2021"
    rust-version = "1.98"
    license = "GPL-3.0-or-later"
    authors = ["terezi <jules@foxtails.me>"]
    repository = "https://github.com/estyseesghosts/lotus"
    
    [workspace.dependencies]
    # Internal crates.
    lotus-protocol = { path = "crates/protocol", version = "0.0.1" }
    lotus-session = { path = "crates/session", version = "0.0.1" }
    lotus-trace = { path = "crates/trace", version = "0.0.1" }
    lotus-debugger = { path = "crates/debugger", version = "0.0.1" }
    lotus-runner = { path = "crates/runner", version = "0.0.1" }
    lotus-hardware = { path = "crates/hardware", version = "0.0.1" }
    lotus-accuracy = { path = "crates/accuracy", version = "0.0.1" }
    lotus-mcp = { path = "crates/mcp", version = "0.0.1" }
    
    # External crates.
    serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
    serde_json = "1"
    sha2 = "0.10"
    serde_yaml = "0.9"
    thiserror = "2"
    anyhow = "1"
    tracing = "0.1"
    tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }
    tokio = { version = "1", features = [
        "rt-multi-thread",
        "macros",
        "io-util",
        "net",
        "sync",
        "time",
        "process",
    ] }
    rmcp = { version = "3", features = ["server", "macros", "schemars", "transport-io"] }
    schemars = "1.0"
    toml = "0.9"
    
    # GPUI is pinned to an exact upstream commit. See config/pins.toml and
    # docs/17-scaffold-and-pins.md. Never move this to a branch or tag.
    gpui = { git = "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed", rev = "6b720973027999bae402df23d469026f4cced988", default-features = false }
    gpui_platform = { git = "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed", rev = "6b720973027999bae402df23d469026f4cced988", default-features = false }
    
    [profile.release]
    opt-level = 3
    lto = "thin"
    codegen-units = 1
    panic = "abort"
    # Pinned dependency revisions for Lotus.
    #
    # Every external source this project builds against is pinned to an exact
    # commit. Moving a pin is a deliberate act: update the file, update
    # Cargo.lock or the submodule pointer in the same commit, and record why.
    #
    # Verified by scripts/verify-pins.ps1.
    
    [azahar]
    # Upstream project.
    repository = "https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar.git"
    # Single fork that carries the two long lived branches.
    fork = "https://github.com/estyseesghosts/azahar.git"
    # Upstream commit the fork is based on.
    upstream_commit = "11eceda5e0e682a1f44e396bf954a1b9137097ca"
    # Branch with upstream minimal native worker hooks.
    integration_branch = "integration"
    integration_commit = "05773bbb5380bc5094fcd8eacf189fdc5d6360bb"
    # Branch with tracing, debugger and accuracy experiments.
    experimental_branch = "experimental"
    experimental_commit = "05773bbb5380bc5094fcd8eacf189fdc5d6360bb"
    # Vendored checkout of the pinned Azahar source.
    vendor_path = "vendor/azahar"
    
    [gpui]
    # GPUI lives in the Zed repository.
    repository = "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed.git"
    # Exact commit the GPUI crates are taken from.
    rev = "6b720973027999bae402df23d469026f4cced988"
    # Version of the gpui crate at that commit.
    crate_version = "0.2.2"
    
    [rust]
    # Toolchain used by every crate in the workspace.
    channel = "1.98.1"
    # Host triple the toolchain was installed for.
    host = "x86_64-pc-windows-gnu"

    # Lotus - documentation index
    
    Start here. Terms are defined once in the [glossary](glossary.md); documents
    link to it instead of redefining them. Each topic below points at exactly one
    canonical document - when writing or updating docs, link rather than duplicate.
    
    ## What Lotus is
    
    A **developer-first 3DS emulator platform** for writing and debugging homebrew
    with agents. Today it is an instrumentation, debugging and MCP wrapper around
    modified Azahar: a Rust product (GPUI desktop, CLI, MCP, scenario runner,
    session supervisor) that launches isolated native worker processes, each an
    emulated Old 3DS. The eventual goal is to replace the Azahar-derived workers
    with a more hardware-accurate in-house emulator. Contract, users and success
    metrics: [01 - product contract](01-product-contract.md).
    
    ## What Lotus is not
    
    Not "the most accurate 3DS emulator", not a Citra reskin, not a new hardware
    model yet. Bootstrap non-goals (no full HLE rewrite, no custom JIT, no
    in-process multi-instance, no LAN listeners, no synchronized multiplayer):
    [01, non-goals](01-product-contract.md). Why an independent UI does not make it
    accurate: [11, the critical distinction](11-accuracy-research.md). Current
    build makes no accuracy claim: [20](20-native-baseline.md).
    
    ## Lotus and Azahar
    
    Azahar supplies the initial machine; Lotus selectively modifies it through
    **one fork with two branches** - `integration` (minimal native worker hooks)
    and `experimental` (tracing, debugger, accuracy experiments) - plus a detached
    `stock` checkout as a control. Branch policy and invariants:
    [03](03-azahar-branches.md). Planned source edits:
    [16 - patch blueprint](16-azahar-patch-blueprint.md). Currently applied
    patches and baselines: [20](20-native-baseline.md).
    
    ## What is CITnLO
    
    CITnLO (CITra n LOtus) is the **backend name for the `experimental` branch**,
    the future home of tracing/debugger/accuracy work; AZAHAR is the `integration`
    backend name. Today both branches share one pin, so the two builds are
    identical and carry no accuracy experiments. See
    [glossary  CITnLO](glossary.md), [03](03-azahar-branches.md),
    [20](20-native-baseline.md).
    
    ## How it works internally
    
    - **Process graph and ownership boundaries** - desktop/CLI/MCP  Rust session
      supervisor  per-instance workers; shared-memory frames, artifact store:
      [02](02-system-architecture.md).
    - **Native Azahar worker** - headless `EmuWindow`, emulation thread, control
      queue: [04](04-azahar-native-worker.md); what's actually merged:
      [21](21-native-control.md).
    - **IPC / session contract** - length-prefixed pipes, epochs, safe points:
      [06](06-ipc-and-session-contract.md), [18](18-control-pipes.md).
    - **GPUI desktop** - screens, input, sessions: [05](05-gpui-desktop.md),
      [24](24-desktop.md).
    - **Driving LOTUS** - headless or windowed, one shared supervisor and MCP
      surface; primary sessions on persistent cards, disposable secondaries,
      sidebar and gauges: [30](30-sessions-and-interface.md).
    - **Multi-instance and storage** - one process per console, private roots:
      [10](10-multi-instance-and-storage.md).
    - **Debugging** - CPU/kernel/memory: [07](07-debugger-core.md); GPU capture
      and tracing: [08](08-gpu-and-trace.md); MCP and scenarios:
      [09](09-mcp-and-scenarios.md), [22](22-scenario-runner.md),
      [23](23-local-mcp.md).
    - Workspace layout: `crates/` (protocol, session, trace, debugger, runner,
      hardware, accuracy, mcp, cli, desktop), `workers/` (azahar, native, oracle),
      `vendor/azahar` (pinned source).
    
    ## Future plans
    
    - **Milestones M0-M6** - exit gates from reproducible sources to the first
      hardware-verified accuracy gain: [13](13-build-test-release.md).
    - **Tickets T00-T47 in four waves** - dependency-ordered plan with status:
      [15](15-implementation-tickets.md); delivered so far:
      [25 - wave status](25-wave-status.md).
    - **Wave 3 - comprehensive agentic debugger** - decisions, Azahar parity
      matrix and milestones 3.0-3.4: [29](29-wave-3-plan.md).
    - **Accuracy research path** - phases A-E, from cataloging Azahar's inherited
      assumptions to an independent PICA200 model and real firmware:
      [11](11-accuracy-research.md).
    - **Hardware validation** - physical Old 3DS microbenchmarks and evidence
      standards: [12](12-hardware-validation.md).
    - Remaining acceptance gaps (two-DPI interaction, audio playback, other
      platforms): [25](25-wave-status.md); visible rendering and input were checked
      by screenshot in [24](24-desktop.md).
    
    ## Building on Windows
    
    Primary toolchain: Rust 1.98.1 `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (GCC/MinGW-w64),
    CMake + Ninja. MSVC and other platforms are untested.
    
    Step-by-step instructions (tools, Rust, both native runtimes, portable ZIP, CI,
    release and recovery): **[27 - build and run](27-build-and-run.md)**. Pins live
    in `config/pins.toml`; each native source gets its own checkout, build directory
    and manifest. Background: [17](17-scaffold-and-pins.md), [13](13-build-test-release.md).
    Opt-in native tests: [21, reproduction](21-native-control.md).

    # Delivery retrospective: Waves 0-2 and v0.0.1
    
    Session record, 2026-11-15/16. Source: the agent session transcript
    ([chatlog01](chatlog01.md), reviewed by outline and by every failure/fix passage,
    not line by line). Evidence for results: [25](25-wave-status.md),
    [20](20-native-baseline.md), [26](26-portable-release.md). Build steps:
    [27](27-build-and-run.md). No hardware accuracy claim is made.
    
    ## What was done
    
    | Phase | Outcome |
    | --- | --- |
    | Native baseline (T01/T04) | Three worktrees at upstream `11eceda5e`; stock core built; bounded oracle driver booted `t03.3dsx` for 60 frames; default-off `ctr-worker` target |
    | Native worker (T05-T09) | Boot, BGRA frame ring with leases, input, muted audio ring, safe-point control, Windows job containment and root locks |
    | Rust (T02, T03, T10-T13) | Private-pipe protocol, supervisor, GPUI desktop, CLI scenarios, four-worker isolation, scoped local MCP |
    | Naming | LOTUS (app), AZAHAR (`integration`), CITnLO (`experimental`) applied across UI/docs/CLI |
    | Release | Portable ZIP + source ZIP + checksums; CI on GitHub; **v0.0.1 published** (run 43801752833) |
    
    ## What went well
    
    - Every native result is tied to an exact commit: `build-azahar.ps1` rejects a
      source that differs from `config/pins.toml`, is dirty, or has a foreign cache.
    - A stock-core oracle gave an independent reference: native screens matched stock
      byte for byte (after BGRA/RGBA), including two simultaneous guests.
    - Crash containment (job objects, root locks, epoch/lease invalidation) was tested
      by killing workers, not assumed.
    - Three CLI runs from fresh roots gave identical hashes.
    - CI built from clean checkouts and the packaged ZIP was tested relocated, with a
      Windows-only PATH.
    - Recovery without recompiling (`reuse_build_run`) turned a 45-minute rebuild into
      about 9 minutes.
    
    ## What went wrong and how it was resolved
    
    | Problem | Cause | Resolution |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Duplicate session IDs/paths in parallel tests | ID generator reused the same Windows clock tick | OS-random IDs plus a process-local counter |
    | Stock build failed on nested submodules | One submodule pass was not enough | Second recursive pass; CI uses `--init --recursive` |
    | Oracle died with `unordered_map::at` before load | Frontend never initialized `Settings::values.lle_modules` | Set every `service_module_map` entry to HLE in the driver; core unchanged |
    | Oracle/worker link errors | Missing Windows `crypt32` | Link `crypt32` on `WIN32` |
    | Workers failed to start from MCP | MinGW cannot open `\\?\` verbatim paths | Session adapter converts to ordinary Win32 paths |
    | Stock vs native screens differed | Fixture output depends on the launch path string (relative vs absolute); **root cause unresolved** | Use identical absolute paths; documented in [20](20-native-baseline.md); not treated as an accuracy regression |
    | Stale frames after a failed/second load | Leases survived content loads | Load-epoch invalidation on every load ([21](21-native-control.md)) |
    | Visible GPUI rendering and two-DPI interaction unverified | Computer Use was not approved for the apps; the user said to continue | Left **unverified** and labeled so everywhere; only geometry and controller tests exist |
    | Release build failed to compile shaders | GPUI needs `fxc.exe` | `setup-build-tools.py` fetches a hash-verified SDK package; `GPUI_FXC_PATH` |
    | Source archiver hung | Windows pipe stall on `git archive` padding | Drain output before waiting (`9b3123c`) |
    | ZIP creation failed on old timestamps | `zipfile` strict timestamps | `strict_timestamps=False` |
    | Package test failed in CI after all builds passed | Compared `RUNNER~1` vs `runneradmin` path strings | `samefile`/`resolve` comparison (`d2a09b0`) |
    | Rebuilding to fix a test would cost ~45 min | Packaging bug sat behind the build jobs | Added `reuse_build_run` plus `validate-build-reuse.py` (trusted main run, successful jobs, ancestor commit, path allowlist) |
    | Reuse run published nothing | `release` skipped transitively because `rust`/`native` were skipped | `always() && needs.package.result == 'success'` (`7f9dc3e`) |
    
    ## Lessons
    
    - Test the real CI path early; two of the last three defects were Windows
      runner-only.
    - A skipped job skips every dependent unless `always()` is used. Re-test
      conditions with the skip path, not just the green path.
    - Keep native tests visibly separate from ignored tests so a skip is never read as
      a pass.
    - Record deferred checks next to the claim, not in a separate list.
    
    ## Still open
    
    Visible GPUI rendering and input, actual two-DPI behavior, audible audio, title
    save formats beyond the drawbench CSV, accelerated renderers, other platforms,
    and the launch-path pixel sensitivity. Debugger and accuracy work (Waves 3-4) is
    not started; see [15](15-implementation-tickets.md).
    # 30 - Sessions, cards and the LOTUS interface
    
    How LOTUS is driven: **headless** (`lotus-mcp`) or **windowed**
    (`lotus-desktop`, optionally `--mcp`). Both drive one shared supervisor with
    one control model, so everything an agent can do headless it can do against a
    window a person is watching. Builds on [23](23-local-mcp.md) (MCP policy) and
    [24](24-desktop.md) (desktop plumbing); terms in the [glossary](glossary.md).
    
    ## Primary and secondary sessions
    
    | | Primary | Secondary |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Worker root | `<storage>/cards/<card>/` | `<storage>/scratch/<session>/` |
    | Guest SD/NAND | the card's own `sdmc/`, `nand/`, `sysdata/`; real reads/writes that persist | empty, or a point-in-time host copy of one card's guest directories |
    | On stop | card kept | root deleted; after a crash or failed stop only logs are kept |
    | Concurrency | one primary per card (registry check + the worker's `worker.lock`) | any number, limit permitting; several may copy one card |
    | Sidebar | top-level row | nested under the card it copied; a parentless secondary is top-level |
    
    A card is created on first use; names are 1-32 of `a-z 0-9 - _`. The guest
    directory names are Azahar's (`SDMC_DIR`, `NAND_DIR`, `SYSDATA_DIR` in
    `src/common/common_paths.h`), selected by `FileUtil::SetUserPath(root)` in
    `ctr_worker/frontend.h`. A copy is taken while the parent may be running and is
    **not** coordinated with its guest writes; copies over 4 GiB, symlinks and
    junctions are refused. On start, a host discards guest data in any unlocked
    `scratch/` root left by a previous process. This is a private-copy design, as
    [10](10-multi-instance-and-storage.md) prefers over unproven copy-on-write.
    
    ## Shared supervisor
    
    `session::supervisor::Supervisor` is thread-safe. Each session has its own async
    lock; the registry lock is never held across a worker exchange. A 600-frame
    `run_until` on one session therefore never delays another session's commands,
    status or preview. Creation reserves a slot (and the card) before the slow
    spawn, so concurrent creations respect `max_sessions` (default 4, the tested
    load; configurable to 16).
    
    The **pump** (every 100 ms in both frontends) polls each idle session's status,
    re-issues bounded `run` batches for sessions marked playing, and folds replies
    into telemetry. A session held by another command is skipped, not awaited. A
    batch that ended with `unsupported_applet` or `core_error` stops playback;
    `host_deadline` (slow batch) does not.
    
    ## Gauges
    
    Per session, from status replies (worker fields in [21](21-native-control.md)):
    
    | Gauge | Meaning |
    | --- | --- |
    | FPS + sparkline | presented guest frames per **host** second over � 500 ms windows |
    | Speed | FPS � 59.8312 Hz = `BASE_CLOCK_RATE_ARM11 / 4481136` (`core/core_timing.h:42`) |
    | Frame / epoch | presented frame counter; epoch increments on load/reset |
    | Audio | guest DSP samples per host second and cumulative drops (output stays muted) |
    | Worker | working set via the supervisor's own process handle (never by PID), PID, uptime |
    | Control | last mutating actor (`you`, `agent`, `host`), its operation, input owner |
    
    These are host-observed throughput figures, not guest-tick or hardware timing.
    
    ## MCP surface
    
    Headless and windowed servers expose the same tools; `lotus_status` reports
    `frontend: headless|windowed`. New or changed relative to [23](23-local-mcp.md):
    
    | Tool | Behaviour |
    | --- | --- |
    | `lotus_create_session` | `kind` `primary` (needs `card`) or `secondary` (default; optional `card` to copy); optional `asset` loads paused |
    | `lotus_load` | replace content in an owned session; paused |
    | `lotus_control` | `run` (continuous, returns at once), `pause`, `reset`, `stop` |
    | `lotus_run_until` | exactly 1-600 frames, then paused; ends continuous running |
    | `lotus_list_sessions` | ids, kind, card/parent, asset and gauges; never waits on a busy worker |
    | `lotus_list_cards` | cards and which session mounts each |
    | `lotus_registers` | r0-r15 and CPSR of one core at a safe point |
    | `lotus_focus_session` | windowed: show that session to the person; headless: no effect |
    
    Host configuration gains `asset_directories` (handle  directory; each `.3dsx`
    directly inside is approved as `<handle>/<file>`, re-listed on demand, so
    rebuilt patch variants can be loaded without a restart) and `max_sessions`.
    Existing configurations parse unchanged. A desktop user may also open any
    `.3dsx` with the file picker; it is approved as `local/<file>` for that process.
    MCP clients still cannot name paths.
    
    ## Window
    
    - **Sidebar** (Ctrl+B collapses to a rail of state chips): cards with their
      primary, secondaries nested beneath; square dot = primary, round =
      secondary, colour = state. Hover: `+` starts a secondary copying that card
      with the same content; `x` stops (primary data kept, secondary discarded).
      `+` beside SESSIONS opens an existing card, creates the next free card name,
      or starts an empty or copied secondary. Footer: MCP link and slot use.
      Icon buttons and rail chips carry tooltips (compiled; not yet seen on screen,
      since synthetic hover does not reach an inactive window).
    - **Toolbar**: name, PRIMARY/SECONDARY badge, card, state, content; Run/Pause,
      Step (one frame), Reset, Load (approved content or Open file.), Stop; Fit /
      1x / 2x zoom; stacked or side-by-side screens; Inspector.
    - **Gauge strip** under the screens; **Inspector** (Ctrl+I): session fields and
      core-0 registers, fetched only while paused and open.
    - Keys: Z/X A/B, A/S X/Y, Q/W L/R, arrows, Enter/Backspace Start/Select; Space
      run/pause; `.` step; Ctrl+O open file. Desktop loads start running; MCP loads
      stay paused.
    - Theme: Geist-derived dark neutrals with colour only for state
      (`desktop::theme`, after the workspace's `vercel.md`). Segoe UI and Consolas,
      since Geist is not assumed installed.
    
    Replaced frames are dropped from GPUI's sprite atlas immediately
    (`App::drop_image`) so streaming stays bounded.
    
    ## Evidence
    
    **Verified emulator** (Windows GNU, AZAHAR and CITnLO at the native pin in
    `config/pins.toml`, fixture `t03.3dsx`, 2026-11-16):
    
    - `session native_process`: four sessions created concurrently (two primaries,
      two secondaries), a fifth refused before launch, two advancing at once,
      secondaries' roots deleted and cards kept on stop.
    - `desktop native_controller`: primary streams and plays; a second primary on
      the same card is refused; a copied secondary sees the card's file, diverges
      without touching it, runs concurrently; an MCP server sharing the
      controller's supervisor lists both, advances the secondary and moves the
      window's selection; crash isolation; crashed secondary discarded with logs
      kept; primary card persists after stop.
    - `tests/test_windowed_mcp.py`: an MCP client launches `lotus-desktop --mcp`
      and drives primary + secondary concurrently, independently and
      asynchronously; no desktop or worker process remains afterwards.
    - Unchanged clients: `native_parity` and `tests/test_mcp_native.py` pass with
      their original create calls (kind defaults to secondary).
    
    **Checked by screenshot** (one 100%-scale display): see [24](24-desktop.md).
    Paused registers at frame 25 were identical across two separate runs.
    
    **Observed speed**: on this host the software-rendered worker runs `t03.3dsx`
    at about 7 guest fps alone (60 frames in 8.7 host s via `run_until`, without
    the pump, whose status polls skip a session held by a run) and about 4-5 fps
    each with three running. The speed gauge reports this (� 8 %). It is a property
    of the current software renderer, the motivation for ADR-009
    ([29](29-wave-3-plan.md)), not of this interface.
    
    Unit tests cover card names, copy/discard/sweep, reservations, asset
    directories, telemetry windows, tree building, fit scaling and formatting.
    Limits: no hardware claim; host audio stays muted; two-DPI and other
    platforms untested; no accessibility audit.

    session_tree, gauges, theme}`. Rollback: none of this changes the worker or its
    protocol; previous behaviour is a headless secondary-only use of the same tools.

    ? The interface work is in place: LOTUS can now be driven headless or windowed,
      and both drive the same sessions with the same MCP tools. I've left everything
      uncommitted (see the last section).
    
      How to run it
      - Headless: lotus-mcp host.json, for an agent alone.
      - Windowed: lotus-desktop host.json.
      - Windowed with MCP: lotus-desktop --mcp host.json. The agent launches the
        window as its MCP server and you watch and use the same sessions. The
        sidebar footer shows whether MCP is attached, the toolbar shows who last
        acted ("you" or "agent"), and lotus_focus_session lets an agent switch your
        view to a session.
    
      Sessions
      - Primary: mounts a named card at <storage>/cards/<name>/, with real SD/NAND
        reads and writes that persist. Only one primary per card can run at a time.
      - Secondary: gets a scratch folder that is empty or a copy of a card, taken
        while the primary may still be running. It's deleted when the session stops.
        After a crash, only its logs are kept.
      - Running several at once: each session has its own lock, so a long run on one
        never blocks another, and starting or stopping one doesn't wait on the
        others. Every session is addressed by its ID over MCP.
      - Limit: the default is 4 sessions, which is the load that has been tested.
        You can raise it to 16 with max_sessions in the host config.
      - Patch builds: a new asset_directories host-config field approves every .3dsx
        in a folder. Rebuilt patch variants show up without restarting LOTUS.
      - Naming: I called the persistent storage a "card" instead of "profile". Your
        uncommitted Wave-3 glossary already uses Profile for session settings (T24).
    
      Interface
      - The collapsible sidebar is the main navigation (Ctrl+B). Primaries are
        top-level entries, secondaries are nested under the card they copied, and a
        secondary with no parent card is top-level. When collapsed it becomes a
        strip of status icons.
      - The toolbar has Run/Pause, Step, Reset, Load (approved content or Open
        file.), Stop, zoom (Fit/1x/2x) and screen layout.
      - The gauges show fps with a small history graph, speed against the 59.83 Hz
        target, frame count, audio, worker memory, and who is in control.
      - The inspector (Ctrl+I) shows registers while a session is paused.
      - Colours follow vercel.md: dark neutrals, with colour only for state.
    
      Testing
      - On both AZAHAR and CITnLO, all the real-worker tests pass. That includes
        four sessions started at once, crash isolation, a card surviving a stop, and
        secondaries being deleted. Workspace tests, clippy with warnings denied,
        fmt and smoke.ps1 also pass.
      - Existing MCP clients still work unchanged.
      - New script tests/test_windowed_mcp.py has an MCP client drive the windowed
        LOTUS end to end. It passes.
      - I checked the window with screenshots. That closes the visible-rendering gap
        the previous session left open. Real frames render, keyboard and mouse both
        work, and Step advances the frame and refreshes the registers. Desktop
        memory stayed flat over 20 seconds of continuous screen updates.
    
      Things you should know
      - Speed: the emulator runs t03.3dsx at only about 7 fps on its own, roughly 8%
        speed. I timed this with nothing else running, so the new interface isn't
        causing it. Slow software rendering is what the Vulkan plan (ADR-009) is
        meant to fix, and the speed gauge reports it accurately.
      - Not verified:
        - Tooltips build, but I couldn't make one appear in screenshots.
        - Behaviour at two different display scalings is still untested.
        - Audio is still muted.
      - Portable launcher changes:
        - LOTUS.cmd no longer opens a file picker at startup; you pick content
          inside LOTUS with Open file..
        - The launcher has a new -Mode WindowedMCP for the window-plus-MCP setup.
