    # 11 - Path from an instrumented Azahar to hardware-accuracy research
    
    ## The critical distinction
    
    The bootstrap inherits Azahar's HLE assumptions, approximate scheduling and accelerated rendering. Even if the Rust front end is entirely original, it is **not a new hardware model yet**. Accuracy advances are only credited when an independently designed component or a measured correction reduces divergence from real 3DS behavior. Avoid the trap of equating 'different code' with 'more accurate emulation'.
    
    ## Target machine and long-term layers
    
    Original 2011 3DS: ARM11 MPCore (two cores), ARM9, DMP PICA200, audio DSP, VRAM/FCRAM/AXI memory, LCD controllers, DMA and peripherals. Old 3DS is a fixed default. New 3DS CPU core count/clock/L2 and extended memory are an explicit later profile, not an arbitrary speed slider. Some 3DS software uses ARM7 only in legacy DS/GBA modes; full legacy modes are outside phase 1. Hardware references: 3dbrew Memory layout, Hardware, FIRM and Coffeepot CTR index.
    
    ### Functional vs temporal vs firmware-system
    
    | Layer | Definition | Independent proof |
    |---|---|---|
    | Architectural CPU | ARM/Thumb/VFP instruction results, flags, exceptions, MMU behavior | hardware differential instruction tests |
    | PICA functional | register commands, vertex/geometry shading, texture/raster output | native framebuffer/reference renderer pixel comparisons |
    | Timing | completion times, interrupts, cache/bus effects | repeated physical tests under controlled workloads |
    | Firmware/system | real boot, actual ARM9/ARM11 kernels/services/peripherals | boots correctly from user-provided dumped components, passes known OS tests |
    
    Keep accuracy scores separate and per-subsystem. A timing approximation may be useful long before any cycle-accurate simulation is possible.
    
    ## Phase A: catalog inherited assumptions
    
    Before rewriting, build a table `assumptions.csv` with: subsystem, Azahar source location, behavior, evidence, affected workloads, confidence, verification test, owner and disposition. Examples from inspected source:
    
    - `Core::Timing::GenerateBaseTicks` can choose random initial ticks, affecting RNG-relevant game behavior. Test scenarios must pin a deterministic base.
    - `Core::Timing::ScheduleEvent` uses internal queues and, in a thread-safe mode, enforces a minimum scheduling delay related to slice size. These are HLE policies, not physical SoC properties.
    - `Core::System::RunLoop` steps ARM cores in virtual slices, with allowable small desynchronizations; not a cycle-by-cycle multicore processor simulator.
    - `GPU::DelayGenerator` estimates copy duration from fixed throughput tables.
    - `PicaCore::InitializeRegs` initializes some registers to compatibility defaults that may rely on earlier real firmware state (source comments explicitly acknowledge this).
    - HLE kernel/service results can differ from actual NATIVE_FIRM; test individual SVC/IPC semantics, not just whether a game boots.
    
    For each assumption, decide: preserve for fast mode; add observability; replace with a measured device model; or mark unknown.
    
    ## Phase B: CPU interpreter and cache model
    
    Develop a **separate Rust reference CPU** rather than porting Dynarmic. It should:
    
    1. Execute correct ARMv6K ARM/Thumb instruction semantics, banked registers, CPSR/SPSR, VFP operations, faults/privilege modes, MMU/TLB, atomic/exclusive monitor semantics.
    2. Offer instruction-step state snapshots and an architectural differential executor against real hardware and Azahar interpreter.
    3. Model instruction/data caches, write buffers, branch/pipeline effects, interrupt latency and inter-core coherence as separable timing components.
    4. Use physical memory requests with explicit delay/visibility results so memory contention isn't a constant cost per load.
    5. Keep JIT execution optional; a JIT would still submit memory/synchronization operations into the same model and cannot erase real stalls.
    
    **Dependency order:** first prove execution semantics; then attach calibrated timing; only after that optimize. An interpreter with guessed cycle counts is not cycle-accurate.
    
    ## Phase C: independent PICA200 reference model
    
    ### Initial component boundaries
    
    - external GPU engines: command submission, memory fills, display/texture transfers, busy/interrupt state;
    - command parser and register bank (reuse/reimplement facts from Azahar/3dbrew but separately test mask/group behavior);
    - programmable vertex/geometry shader interpreter with actual float24 arithmetic and swizzle/control-flow behavior;
    - vertex fetch, primitive assembly, clipping, culling and rasterization;
    - texture decoding and addressing, lookup tables, TEV combiners, alpha/depth/stencil/blending;
    - display-facing framebuffer/scanout behavior distinct from draw target;
    - independent timing pipeline, calibrated from Old 3DS experiments.
    
    A software reference renderer is appropriate even if too slow for real-time games. Retain accelerated Azahar backend for normal use. A GPU capture can be fed into both renderers **only if** it contains the real preconditions and input resource versions; validate equivalence rather than assume capture is self-contained.
    
    ### Explicit unknowns
    
    - Primitive Engine and variable-size primitive behavior: 3dbrew explicitly says full functionality is not understood, and specific enable behavior unknown.
    - Fine-grained shader throughput, cache replacement, co-issue/overlap among geometry, raster and fragment stages.
    - Cache capacities/latencies and exact bus arbitration under mixed CPU/GPU/DMA load.
    - Edge cases in hardware texture and framebuffer formats, fixed-point interpolation and subtle coverage rules.
    
    Treat these as research questions with falsifiable experiments, not commitments to implement undocumented details on guesswork.
    
    ## Phase D: memory and concurrency
    
    Model physical memory regions with visibility and arbitration:
    
    - FCRAM, VRAM banks and AXI WRAM; CPU cache and MMU mappings; device views may be noncoherent.
    - DMA/display transfer engines and PICA reads/writes can overlap CPU activity.
    - Hardware device requests should produce timestamped transactions with region/bank, size, service duration and completion/visibility behavior.
    - Start with a coarse deterministic scheduler and calibrate under isolated transfers; then mixed workloads where transfer engines compete.
    
    A fixed 'bytes / bandwidth' rule is a baseline only. Compare sequential/random, aligned/misaligned, read/write and mixed GPU traffic. Hardware architecture is not reducible to one shared RAM speed.
    
    ## Phase E: real firmware
    
    Eventually replace much of HLE with actual ARM9+ARM11 firmware/kernel execution. 3dbrew FIRM documents ARM9/ARM11 kernel sections and core system modules. A genuine firmware boot needs correct privileged CPU modes, reset/boot state, interrupt controllers, timers, memory maps, crypto/security peripherals and IPC. It also requires legally user-provided firmware/dumped device files; do not include these artifacts. Full boot ROM execution may remain out of reach for many iterations.
    
    Avoid attempting real firmware before the CPU/MMU/IRQ/memory foundations and the diagnostic harness can explain early boot failures. Treat `direct homebrew boot`, `FIRM boot` and `boot-ROM boot` as separate backend features with separate evidence grades.
    
    ## Hardware timing model methodology
    
    A timing model should predict **unseen** workload timing. For the GPU:
    
    1. Calibrate command parsing overhead using empty/no-op lists.
    2. Isolate vertex shader work with tiny pixel coverage and fixed state.
    3. Isolate raster/fragment work with few vertices and controlled screen coverage.
    4. Measure texture format/cache behavior by varying addresses, access locality and filter modes.
    5. Measure framebuffer/depth/blending pressure and display transfer separately.
    6. Run mixed workloads to observe pipeline overlap, contention and saturation.
    7. Compare predicted vs measured completion/interrupt times on a held-out set; report median and error distribution, not only average.
    
    'Fast host time x constant = simulated 3DS time' fails because different bottlenecks dominate different workloads. Also, emulate the **causal** completion events, not an isolated per-draw delay that cannot interact with subsequent commands.
    
    ## Unknown behavior policy
    
    Every uncertain device behavior must have:
    
    - status `measured / documented / inferred / approximated / unknown`;
    - source link or physical experiment ID;
    - allowed domain (Old 3DS hardware version, CFW/kernel state, input format);
    - counterexample or negative test when available;
    - fallbacks (`strict`, `compatible`, or `disabled`), with exact semantics.
    
    Never label compatibility workaround as a physical feature. Allow the debugger to highlight when a workload enters an approximated path.
    
    ## Evaluating "more accurate than Azahar"
    
    Produce a public table of cases where (a) physical output/timing is measured; (b) stock Azahar result is measured at pinned SHA; (c) experimental result is measured; (d) the new model reduces error, with error bars; (e) regressions are enumerated. A handful of wins does not imply globally highest accuracy, but it establishes verified improvements.
    
    ## Research references
    
    - 3dbrew physical map: https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/Memory_layout
    - 3dbrew GPU: https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/GPU/Internal_Registers
    - 3dbrew Primitive Engine unknowns: https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/GPU/Primitive_Engine
    - 3dbrew FIRM: https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/FIRM
    - ARM11 MPCore: https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ddi0360/latest/
    - Mikage Developer Edition: https://github.com/mikage-emu/mikage-dev
    - Coffeepot CPU/PICA/benchmarks: https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/tree/main/ctr
    # 12 - Physical 3DS validation, microbenchmarks and evidence
    
    ## Hardware test harness is a first-class subproject
    
    Create a tiny native 3DS executable test runner built with devkitPro, designed to emit repeatable state and timing reports, with test identifiers, firmware/CFW/model, toolchain revision and raw samples. Use Coffeepot's existing benchmark programs and documentation rather than inventing a fresh suite without reviewing it.
    
    Starting points:
    - https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/tree/main/ctr/benchmarks
    - https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/blob/main/ctr/engineering/testing-on-hardware.md
    - https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/blob/main/ctr/engineering/cpu-optimization.md
    - https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot/blob/main/ctr/engineering/PICA200/pica200-command-pipeline.md
    
    Coffeepot's source-version page already distinguishes *compiled*, *run on emulator*, and *run on hardware*, and records pinned devkitPro/libctru/citro3d/Luma3DS revisions. Preserve that standard and put code/tests and raw data together.
    
    ## Test record structure
    
    ```text
    experiment_id
    hypothesis, expected_observable, null_result, confounders
    binary_sha256, source_commit, compiler_flags, tool_versions
    console_model/region, firmware_version, Luma3DS_version, mode
    system_state: clocks, screens/3D, wifi, battery/charging, services
    input fixture, RNG seed, memory addresses/alignment, warmup
    raw timestamps/counters, units, calibration/overhead
    repeat_count, median/p95/p99/spread, error count
    raw frame/memory/GPU hashes, sample files
    result interpretation, limitations, next discriminating test
    ```
    
    Don't invent fields when the hardware cannot reveal them; use `unavailable` and explain. A successful no-error log is still not proof of exact rendering or timing.
    
    ## Measurement calibration
    
    - Measure clock timer read cost with empty loops and back-to-back reads. Control compiler optimization, unroll and dead-code elimination (emit observable checksum).
    - Use warmup/training iterations separately from measurement iterations; keep raw results.
    - Record counter frequency and overflow/wrap behavior; use sufficiently wide accumulators.
    - Randomize test order to reduce thermal/cache/time drift; report if the device's clocks or cache states cannot be fixed.
    - Repeat on separate hardware sessions, not merely a million measurements in one uninterrupted run.
    - For GPU completion, know precisely which IRQ/fence/busy flag constitutes completion. CPU submission time does not equal GPU completion time.
    - For framebuffer correctness, record native buffer bytes where possible, pixel format/orientation and when the capture was made. Screenshots taken later may miss transient state.
    
    ## Minimum initial test families
    
    ### CPU architecture and memory
    
    1. ARM/Thumb conditional execution, flag behavior, unusual shift operands, exclusive access, exceptions, privilege transitions, VFP arithmetic.
    2. Instruction vs data cache working sets, strides, dirty-line writeback, invalidate, instruction cache self-modification, page-table/TLB changes.
    3. Read/write latency by physical region and cacheable mapping, concurrent ARM11 core and DMA pressure where software permits.
    4. Branch/control-flow tests with same instruction count but different predictability; test VFP dependencies/throughput.
    
    ### GPU functional behavior
    
    1. Empty command lists, register masks/groups, immediate-mode vertices, indexed draw, primitive topology and restart.
    2. Shader operations (including float24 special values, swizzles, branches and loop control), shader output masks.
    3. Geometry/Primitive Engine cases, clipping limits, culling, interpolation, two-eye/rotation effects.
    4. Textures: swizzle/layout/format/ETC1, filtering, wrap, mip, procedurals, palettes if relevant.
    5. TEV, fragment lighting, LUT, fog, alpha/depth/stencil/blend operations; partial prior-buffer retention.
    6. Display transfers, fills, tiled/linear conversion, alignment and busy/IRQ behavior.
    7. CPU writes + cache flush before draw, GPU write then CPU read, CPU/GPU concurrent access.
    
    ### GPU timing isolation
    
    - Constant draw state; sweep vertex count x vertex shader operations at low coverage.
    - Constant geometry; sweep covered pixels x overdraw at fixed material/shader.
    - Sweep textures in VRAM vs FCRAM, formats, filter, locality and mip usage.
    - Busy flags/interrupt latency of `PSC0/PSC1`, PPF transfer and P3D command engine.
    - Mixed workloads designed to falsify additive cost assumptions: vertex-heavy plus pixel-heavy, transfer overlapping draw, repeated state changes.
    - Hardware hotspot counter experiments when registers are accessible; interpretation remains tentative until correlated with independent measurements.
    
    ### System behavior
    
    - VBlank, framebuffer swap and screen state; sleep/resume/HOME lifecycle.
    - HLE SVC vs real kernel scheduling/IPC/timeouts.
    - DSP sample timing and synchronization; DMA, underruns.
    - ARM9 storage/crypto behavior for firmware experiments in later phase.
    
    ## Per-experiment method
    
    Write each test as an empirical question:
    
    **Hypothesis:** moving identical vertex data from FCRAM to VRAM changes GPU completion latency by a measurable amount for workload X.
    
    **Controls:** identical vertices, commands, shader, raster coverage, render target, cache maintenance, warmup and measured start/stop boundaries. Verify both paths render pixel-identical outputs.
    
    **Independent variable:** data location only.
    
    **Recorded values:** command submission ticks, GPU completion/IRQ ticks, hotspot register readings if available, bytes/addresses and framebuffer hash.
    
    **Falsification:** distributions statistically overlap at the suite's observed noise level, or unexpected state changes explain the result. Conclude only for tested region/size, not universal memory hierarchy.
    
    ## Differential execution
    
    For each fixture:
    
    ```text
    hardware binary + initial data
            �� physical Old 3DS -> raw measured result
            �� Azahar upstream pinned -> emulated result
            �� integration branch -> emulated result
            �� experimental branch -> emulated result
                                    -> comparison report
    ```
    
    The hardware binary must make guest-observable checksums, not assume the host emulator can inspect inaccessible hardware internal registers. Normalize known capture differences, preserve raw samples and report mismatches by observable.
    
    ## Test prioritization
    
    Score candidate experiments by **uncertainty x likely impact x experimental observability**. Start with boundary behaviors for which Citra/Azahar source has explicit `TODO`, magic constants or compatibility defaults; prioritize commands executed by realistic homebrew. Unknown Primitive Engine behavior is interesting but shouldn't block basic software rendering. Track hardware evidence coverage of each accuracy-model assumption.
    
    ## Practical harness tooling
    
    - Use devkitPro/libctru to construct and load homebrew; when researching register semantics, minimize high-level library code where safe and documented.
    - Use `3dslink -s` for live logs, but avoid printing inside timed critical sections; buffer results and send after test.
    - Use Luma3DS Rosalina GDB for process/virtual/physical mapping, registers and SVC traps when applicable; recognize debug attachment perturbs timing.
    - Record failures with checksums and raw logs on SD, then retrieve from console.
    - Keep test programs small enough to audit, with build scripts and pinned deps. No kernel patch that would invalidate a measurement without recording it.
    
    ## Statistical reporting and falsifiability
    
    - Preserve all raw measurements and invalid samples with reason.
    - Report central tendency, spread, threshold definition, timer precision and confidence interval when possible.
    - Distinguish random measurement noise from deterministic emulator mismatch.
    - Hold out some workloads from calibration. A fitted model only tested against its training set is not validated.
    - When a timing model predicts observed hardware within 5%, that is a **test-specific finding**; document worst-case errors and scope.
    - Experiments that do not detect an effect still count as useful results when instrumented and reproducible.
    
    ## Acceptance for first empirical accuracy gain
    
    A pull request may claim improvement only with `before/after` test data on the **same stock Azahar source base** and independent physical 3DS samples, plus at least one held-out test and documented regressions. For purely architectural refactors or observability features, state no new accuracy claim.
    # 13 - Build system, CI, milestones, release and risk management
    
    ## Build philosophy
    
    Two technologies, two lockfiles and independent test pipelines:
    
    - Rust workspace: locked Rust toolchain, Cargo dependencies, pinned GPUI Git revision; builds desktop, CLI, session manager, trace/MCP libraries.
    - Azahar native worker: CMake/C++ with upstream submodules, pinned Azahar branch SHA, compiler, CMake options and dependency versions; builds worker executable and C++ tests.
    
    No requirement to compile GPUI and Azahar into one binary. IPC compatibility is tested with separate build outputs. Do not let the Rust build dynamically fetch Azahar's moving `master` during CI.
    
    ## Local development on Windows first
    
    > The commands below are the original plan. The working, verified commands are in
    > [27](27-build-and-run.md); `ctr-cli`/`ctr-worker` paths and flags there supersede these.
    
    Suggested prerequisites: Git, CMake, Ninja, C++ compiler/toolchain matching Azahar's supported build paths, Rust/Cargo, Python for small scripts where useful, Windows SDK/Vulkan tools for GPU backend. Use official Azahar build instructions for actual compiler versions; don't assume Microsoft/MSYS2/MXE settings from a past release remain valid. The source currently uses CMake >=3.25 and has platform-specific conditionals. On macOS/Linux, follow GPUI's platform prerequisites and Azahar's native build requirements separately.
    
    Suggested commands after implementation (not executable in untouched upstream):
    
    ```powershell
    cargo build --locked -p ctr-cli -p ctr-desktop -p ctr-supervisor
    cmake -S vendor/azahar -B build/native-integration -G Ninja -DENABLE_QT=OFF -DENABLE_LIBRETRO=OFF -DENABLE_CTR_WORKER=ON -DENABLE_SOFTWARE_RENDERER=ON
    cmake --build build/native-integration --target ctr-worker --config RelWithDebInfo
    cargo test --locked --workspace
    ctr-cli doctor --worker build/native-integration/src/ctr_worker/ctr-worker.exe
    ```
    
    **Do not cargo-build or invoke the worker from a post-build script that downloads copyrighted Nintendo files.** User firmware and game assets are external; fixtures can use self-authored homebrew programs.
    
    ## Continuous integration jobs
    
    | Job | Trigger | Gate |
    |---|---|---|
    | `rust-check` | every Rust PR | format, clippy, unit tests, no semver drift |
    | `gpui-compile` | GPUI/desktop PR | Windows build and smoke; Linux/macOS where runners available |
    | `azahar-integration-build` | integration PR/upstream sync | worker+stock Azahar compile, C++ tests, minimal native run |
    | `azahar-experimental-build` | experimental PR | same worker protocol, instrumentation tests |
    | `protocol-contract` | schema or worker PR | version negotiation, invalid inputs, CLI/MCP parity |
    | `worker-smoke` | worker or session PR | .3dsx launch, input, audio, two screens, stop/restart |
    | `multi-instance` | storage/supervisor PR | 4 sessions and fs isolation under fault injection |
    | `golden-corpus` | core/GPU PR | fixed binaries, GPU outputs and stable checkpoints |
    | `performance-regression` | selected nightly | baseline/diagnostic builds, median and p95 host cost, A/B |
    | `upstream-watch` | scheduled | latest upstream SHA, diff hotspots and license changes |
    | `hardware-data` | manual physical run | validates fixture metadata, units, hashes and statistics |
    
    GitHub CI cannot validate real 3DS hardware unless a controlled physical runner is built and explicitly maintained. Don't label emulator-only CI as hardware verification.
    
    ## Release profiles
    
    - `fast-play`: Azahar-compatible settings, accelerated renderer, low overhead, minimal tracing.
    - `debug`: breakpoint state, safe-point RPC, L1 event rings and artifacts, reasonable performance.
    - `capture`: selective L2/L3 GPU/CPU events, may pause guest or incur major slowdown.
    - `research`: experimental models with explicit version/config and measured uncertainty, not enabled by default without tests.
    
    A release manifest must record product version, worker source revision/branch, protocol, GPUI revision, compiler, dependencies, defaults, known unsupported functions, and license notices. Experimental builds must be visually distinguishable from integrated baseline in GUI and trace metadata.
    
    ## Exit gates, not arbitrary calendar deadlines
    
    ### Milestone M0 - reproducible sources
    
    - Pinned Azahar revision, GPL/license inventory, stock build works, two worktrees configured.
    - Minimal native worker target compiles with Qt/Libretro disabled where supported.
    - No feature claim yet.
    
    ### M1 - core boots headless
    
    - Program load and basic execution; emitted status and complete shutdown.
    - Software top/bottom frames and event ordering validated against stock Azahar in one known homebrew fixture.
    - Failing input/unsupported applet emits typed error, not hang.
    
    ### M2 - Rust supervisor and CLI
    
    - Native control IPC handshake and session state; pause/resume/reset/runs; isolated storage.
    - At least 2 workers; acceptance target 4 concurrent independent instances.
    - Repeatable scenario with fixed stop condition and output hash.
    
    ### M3 - GPUI usability
    
    - Both screens, touch mapping, controller input, live status and logs.
    - Dynamic frame content under synthetic and real worker; UI survives worker crash.
    - No required Qt windows or Libretro dependencies.
    
    ### M4 - developer debugging
    
    - CPU registers and disassembly, safe-point memory reads, breakpoints; kernel thread/process snapshots; consistent error semantics.
    - MCP and CLI command equivalence; agent reproduces a known crash through scenario runner.
    
    ### M5 - GPU captures
    
    - PICA command list, draw-at-state, texture versions, frame ID, output raw image and diff.
    - Instrumentation A/B test and missing/dropped event reporting.
    - Three representative rendering regressions diagnosed with captures.
    
    ### M6 - first hardware verified accuracy gain
    
    - Physical old-3DS fixture corpus exists; at least one meaningful independent behavior correction with before/after vs stock Azahar; held-out evidence.
    - No broad claim of perfect accuracy; known failures cataloged.
    
    ## Risk register
    
    | Risk | Probability/impact | Response |
    |---|---|---|
    | Azahar core relies on hidden frontend hooks | High/high | compile minimal worker early; write interface inventory before UI |
    | GPUI APIs change | High/medium | pin commit and isolate custom Elements |
    | Vulkan headless readback complicated | High/medium | software path first; benchmark readback |
    | Upstream and experimental branches drift | High/high | integration-first merge policy and nightly watch |
    | Snapshot semantics unreliable | Medium/high | scripted launch as fallback; validate async barriers |
    | Guest debugger reads race with core | High/high | queue to `ProcessPendingWork`, epoch/safe-point checks |
    | Trace destroys performance | High/medium | bounded levels and A/B measurements |
    | Multiple instances share writable files/ports | High/high | per-worker root, explicit locks, collision tests |
    | Hardware research open-ended | High/high | falsifiable short experiments with ROI prioritization |
    | GPL/third-party compatibility | Medium/high | per-file license audit, release source/notice compliance |
    | User game content/security | Medium/high | local-only, scoped paths, user-provided files |
    | Timing model overfits | High/high | held-out benchmarks; confidence bounds, no magic constants |
    
    ## Licensing and distribution
    
    The checked Azahar `LICENSE.txt` contains GPLv3, but individual files contain copyright notices such as GPLv2-or-later and GPLv3-or-later. **Verify all file-level licenses, linked dependencies, GPUI licensing, combined-work and source distribution obligations** when packaging. Different processes/IPC do not automatically settle legal characterization. Preserve copyright attribution, provide corresponding source and build information as required; do not bundle Nintendo firmware, games, console-unique data or keys. Consult competent legal guidance if commercial or restrictive distribution is planned.
    
    ## Publication criteria
    
    Before claiming a public release: install/uninstall cleanly; no external network listener; user-supplied files never leave machine by default; license notices and source provenance included; debugger features documented with limitations; crash reports scrub absolute user paths and private data by default; reproducibility run manifests generated. Publish an accuracy claims table with direct evidence rather than marketing adjectives.

    # 04 - Building the native Azahar worker (Option B)
    
    **Scope:** the actual native Azahar core. Explicitly **not** `src/citra_libretro`. The goal is a small, maintainable C++ executable with a portable IPC boundary, not an FFI binding of every C++ class into Rust.
    
    ## Source facts verified against current Azahar master (2026-11-15)
    
    - `src/core/core.cpp` declares `Core::System System::s_instance` and contains `System::RunLoop`, `Load`, `SingleStep`, `ProcessPendingWork`, `ProcessPendingWorkUntil` and `NotifyPendingWork`.
    - `src/core/core.h` exposes `Load(Frontend::EmuWindow&, filepath, secondary_window)`, `RunLoop(bool tight_loop=true)`, `SingleStep`, `RequestShutdown`, `Memory`, `Kernel`, `GPU`, `CoreTiming`.
    - `src/core/frontend/emu_window.h`: `WindowSystemType::Headless`; virtual `PollEvents`; `CreateSharedContext`; window info with `render_surface=nullptr`; touch methods; framebuffer layout and context lifecycle.
    - `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_platform.cpp` recognizes headless window type. **Does not guarantee end-to-end GPU screenshots or offscreen output**; test it.
    - `src/core/core_timing.cpp` schedules events and virtual CPU timers, with configurable tick base and CPU clock percentage.
    - `src/video_core/gpu.cpp`: `GPU::Execute` receives GSP requests, `SubmitCmdList` triggers the PICA command processor, VBlank events are registered, DMA/display transfers are handled.
    - `src/video_core/pica/pica_core.cpp`: `PicaCore` owns internal registers, shader engine, geometry pipeline, trigger-draw handling.
    - `src/core/rpc/rpc_server.cpp`: existing RPC includes memory access and screenshots; `src/core/rpc/udp_server.cpp` uses a fixed UDP port `45987` (unsuitable as-is for independent workers).
    - `src/CMakeLists.txt` adds core, video, audio, network and input libraries, then Qt/Libretro by options. `src/core/CMakeLists.txt` builds `citra_core`.
    
    These are integration leads, not claims that an `EmuWindow` subclass can be implemented without further missing interfaces.
    
    ## Native worker responsibilities
    
    1. Parse per-worker config from supervisor: root dir, file path, selected graphics backend, initial clock/3DS model, debug mode, IPC endpoint, requested test determinism, audio on/off.
    2. Create native file/path environment and register frontend applets, microphone/image callbacks, video and input bridges.
    3. Initialize `Core::System::GetInstance()`; `Load` selected executable; report structured error/status.
    4. Own the *single* emulation thread. Execute `RunLoop(true)` for running mode; `SingleStep()` only when correct CPU stepping semantics are confirmed.
    5. Drain only explicitly allowed control requests at `ProcessPendingWork` safe points; allow quiescent pause commands to be applied even when frame limiting is sleeping.
    6. Route screen/audio from backend to bounded shared-memory/output queues; never block the emulation thread indefinitely waiting on a slow GPUI client.
    7. On exit, flush/close storage, complete or reject pending control messages, stop video/audio threads, destroy renderer, then unload and report final state.
    
    ## First implementation spike: choose software renderer
    
    A software renderer avoids the GPU surface and Vulkan readback uncertainties during earliest UI bring-up. Disable Qt; compile worker target with video software backend and required dependencies. Once images+input+audio work, add offscreen Vulkan.
    
    **Build configuration sketch (must be validated on chosen source SHA):**
    
    ```bash
    cmake -S vendor/azahar -B build/azahar-worker \
      -DENABLE_QT=OFF \
      -DENABLE_LIBRETRO=OFF \
      -DENABLE_CTR_WORKER=ON \
      -DENABLE_SOFTWARE_RENDERER=ON \
      -DENABLE_VULKAN=ON \
      -DENABLE_SCRIPTING=OFF \
      -DENABLE_WEB_SERVICE=OFF \
      -DENABLE_ROOM=OFF \
      -DENABLE_ROOM_STANDALONE=OFF
    cmake --build build/azahar-worker --target ctr-worker --config RelWithDebInfo
    ```
    
    `ENABLE_CTR_WORKER` and `ctr-worker` are **new proposed names** and do not exist upstream yet. `RelWithDebInfo` handling and toolchain configuration depend on the chosen CMake generator. Some existing conditionals are tied to `ENABLE_QT`; inventory and remove accidental dependencies before declaring `Qt OFF` functional. Keep stock Azahar build independently testable.
    
    ## CMake changes (integration branch)
    
    Minimal, additive changes:
    
    - Root `CMakeLists.txt`: `option(ENABLE_CTR_WORKER "Build external emulation worker" OFF)`, set any mutual exclusions deliberately; don't repurpose Libretro flags.
    - `src/CMakeLists.txt`: `if(ENABLE_CTR_WORKER) add_subdirectory(ctr_worker) endif()` near other frontend targets.
    - `src/ctr_worker/CMakeLists.txt`: add executable with `worker_main.cpp`, `worker_frontend.cpp`, `worker_control.cpp`, `worker_capture.cpp`, `worker_input.cpp`, `worker_audio.cpp`, `worker_storage.cpp`. Link existing Azahar `citra_core`, `video_core`, `audio_core`, other dependencies verified by target graph. Do **not** duplicate core source compilation.
    - Explicitly choose a toolchain configuration and avoid linking existing Qt application objects. Keep native worker code in a small directory, with platform-specific socket/shared-memory code isolated.
    
    A hard requirement is that `ENABLE_CTR_WORKER=OFF` leaves upstream build behavior unchanged.
    
    ## Frontend construction
    
    Create `WorkerEmuWindow final : public Frontend::EmuWindow` with:
    - `WindowSystemInfo` set to `Headless` and null surface initially.
    - `PollEvents` forwards input/config messages gathered by the worker (no native GUI event loop).
    - `GetFramebufferLayout` uses an explicit top/bottom layout; touch coordinates are mapped from GPUI to bottom-screen pixel coordinates and forwarded to `TouchPressed/Moved/Released`.
    - `CreateSharedContext` initially returns null where supported; if renderer requires one, implement a renderer-specific offscreen context, not a fake pointer.
    - Configure min/layout sizes before `Core::System::Load` and keep their lifetime valid through shutdown.
    - Implement or register the frontend software keyboard, Mii selector and image/audio input services where games request them; don't silently treat all applets as successful. For headless tests, return a clear `NEEDS_UI_INTERACTION` event with timeout/fallback policy.
    
    Investigate the actual existing `citra_qt` and SDL-like frontend implementation for callbacks and ownership; `EmuWindow` alone doesn't cover every service.
    
    ## Initial running loop and command queue
    
    **Design pseudocode (not drop-in Azahar code):**
    
    ```cpp
    while (!shutdown_requested) {
        drain_nonblocking_control_messages();  // queues only
        switch (state) {
          case Running:
            result = system.RunLoop(true);
            break;
          case Paused:
            system.ProcessPendingWork();  // including debugger commands
            wait_on_control_condition_with_timeout();
            continue;
          case StepPending:
            result = run_step_for_selected_core_or_stop_with_error();
            state = Paused;
            break;
        }
        publish_run_result_if_needed(result);
        if (fatal(result)) break;
    }
    ```
    
    `SingleStep()` currently executes `RunLoop(false)`, which may interact with **all** CPU cores and scheduling. Do not label that 'step selected ARM11 core by exactly one instruction' until verified; add per-thread/per-core step semantics on experimental branch with tests. Never enter `RunLoop` recursively from a debugger callback. Add a safe-point queue to `ProcessPendingWork`, and use `NotifyPendingWork()` to wake the core on requests. Make pending requests cancellable on shutdown.
    
    ## Read/write semantics
    
    A memory read must specify `process_id`, `address_space`, `guest_address`, `length`, `consistency`. Validate range and permissions, avoid blindly copying virtual pointers into host buffers; use Azahar's `MemorySystem` facilities and return a typed fault, unmapped range or permission failure. GPU-backed pages may require a synchronized rasterizer flush to reflect what the CPU would observe; a pure inspector read should not secretly cause guest-visible writes or corrupt renderer caches.
    
    A write must also identify the process/space and note side effects: JIT invalidation if executable code changes, rasterizer cache invalidation for altered graphics resources, debugger-visible mutation provenance and a changed state epoch. Disable writes during uncommitted replay checkpoints.
    
    ## Frame emission
    
    - Software path: access the **final top/bottom screen images** after relevant display/layout transforms. Prefer raw native screen buffers over composited window captures; record geometry, pixel format, orientation, eye selection, crop and original guest framebuffer address.
    - Vulkan path: use an offscreen target supported by selected backend; wait for submission completion before readback or handoff; never assume `Headless` automatically presents usable images.
    - Ring buffer: at least 3 slots, slot generation/sequence, writer marks `WRITING` then `READY` with release/acquire synchronization; consumer owns a lease or copies before the writer reuses it.
    - Policy: UI may skip intermediate frames; capture/test mode must either reliably collect requested frames or return explicit dropped-frame counts. Do not silently switch the emulated game into a different clock speed to satisfy the UI.
    
    ## Audio and input
    
    - Input: make worker input atomic per emulated sampling boundary; external script has exclusive ownership, no simultaneous live controller events. Map native buttons and touch explicitly; normal gameplay can accept host timestamps but replay uses guest event boundaries.
    - Audio: start with existing Azahar audio stream to a per-worker ring; UI/supervisor mixes host playback streams or selects active one. Headless workers can discard playback but preserve emulated DSP execution and track underruns.
    - Microphone/camera/system keyboards: provide deterministic fixtures for tests; interactive mode can request user values. Do not pretend missing sensors exist.
    
    ## Storage and settings
    
    Azahar uses settings and utility globals, including `Settings::values` and file-path helpers. Before launching a worker, set its user directory **before initialization**, and explicitly override any application-global data/cache paths. Identify every file-writing path (logs, saves, shader cache, texture packs, archive caches, firmware, cheats, screenshots, temporary files). Reject two workers sharing writable roots by default.
    
    ## Existing RPC and GDB
    
    Existing Azahar RPC is an implementation reference, not a server to expose unchanged. It binds UDP `45987`, so multiple workers would collide and it may allow unsafe access without consistent synchronization. Initial worker build should disable it and use our authenticated local IPC. Retain GDB functionality through a per-worker configurable endpoint if needed; account for its core safe-point interactions. A direct internal debugger interface is better than layering MCP atop UDP packets.
    
    ## Technical risks and explicit tests
    
    | Risk | Test / mitigation |
    |---|---|
    | Qt-only code hidden in core path | Build `ENABLE_QT=OFF`, link native worker, launch homebrew |
    | `Headless` lacks Vulkan output capture | Software first, offscreen Vulkan spike, screenshots compared |
    | `ProcessPendingWork` reentrancy/races | Concurrent control storm, pause/resume while sleeping, TSAN where possible |
    | `SingleStep` semantics differ from request | Assert per-core PC/instruction behavior with two threads |
    | IPC call blocks emulation indefinitely | Deadlines and bounded queues, cancellation tests |
    | Audio or applet stalls headless | Synthetic fallback with explicit events; no silent green result |
    | Shader cache/shared paths corrupt | Two workers start/stop with separate roots and identical ROM |
    | Resource lifetime | Open/close/reload loop, multiple sessions, forced worker kill |
    | Performance effect of debug hooks | A/B uninstrumented vs inactive-hook vs active-trace runs |
    
    ## Invariants for merge into integration
    
    No new Rust UI dependency, no new default network listener, no changed GPU timing, no permanent trace allocations on the critical path, no change to stock Azahar frontend when worker option is OFF. All changes must have an explicit upstream behavior comparison.
    # 05 - GPUI desktop application: architecture, UX and rendering
    
    ## Framework contract
    
    Use Zed's **GPUI**, not Electron, a web shell or React Native. Build a Rust native app with entities/views/elements, action-driven keyboard shortcuts and async work. The `gpui_platform::application()` entrypoint chooses host platform; GPUI's own README reports Windows Win32/DirectWrite, macOS Metal (`font-kit` for glyphs), Linux Wayland/X11 options. **Pin the GPUI source commit**; the project is pre-1.0 and breaking changes are expected. Source: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/gpui/README.md
    
    ## Application entities and data ownership
    
    ```text
    AppModel
    �� WorkspaceModel             open docks, tabs, saved layouts
    �� SessionList                worker handles + health
    �  �� SessionViewModel        immutable latest snapshots and subscriptions
    �� CaptureStore               immutable capture/artifact metadata
    �� SymbolIndex                per-process ELF/symbol resolvers
    �� DebuggerModel              breakpoints, watches, focused thread, active frame
    �� Preferences                UI / input mapping / privacy
    ```
    
    The worker never calls into GPUI. A background task reads IPC, validates message ordering/epoch, stores immutable snapshots in a bounded cache and schedules UI model changes via GPUI's thread-safe executor/context mechanisms appropriate to pinned API. Never mutate a GPUI entity from an unmanaged worker thread. Coalesce high-frequency telemetry; don't re-render the entire debugger view for every GPU register change.
    
    ## Minimum viable layout
    
    - Central document area: 3DS top/bottom images; layout presets (stacked, side-by-side, single-screen, right-eye, native-resolution view); independently zoom and pan; pixel inspection mode with nearest-neighbor sampling.
    - Left dock: sessions + launch presets, process/thread tree, breakpoints/watchpoints.
    - Right dock: registers/disassembly, memory browser, PICA state/draw details; searchable, synchronized to selected snapshot.
    - Bottom dock: structured event log, tracing status/dropped counts, scripts/test results, audio underruns, worker errors.
    - Timeline: separate lanes for CPU execution, SVCs, kernel waits, GPU command lists/draws/transfers, DSP and presentation; show guest clock and host clock independently.
    - Header: active instance/build/backend, run/pause/step controls, determinism flag, Old/New 3DS mode, timing model label.
    
    **Avoid** expensive always-live visualizations until a user opens the pane. Closed panes should not trigger costly emulator reads.
    
    ## Layout and interaction discipline
    
    - Every panel has an independent stable ID. A GPUI entity maps to an instance and snapshot ID, never a raw C++ pointer.
    - Layout persistence is versioned; unknown panel types default to safe fallback rather than losing workspace configuration.
    - All numeric addresses appear with process/core/space qualifiers (e.g. CPU virtual `PID:VA`, physical VRAM, GPU register index). Switching current process should not silently reinterpret an old address.
    - Suspended/stale snapshots are visibly marked; the UI never shows the latest register contents as though they were captured at the selected old GPU draw.
    - Provide keyboard-first navigation and palette commands. Actions should be discoverable and localizable; avoid hardcoding shortcuts in individual panels.
    - Display failures/unsupported features explicitly, e.g. `renderer does not support GPU texture capture`, not empty black screenshots.
    
    ## Native image integration: do not prematurely force zero-copy
    
    `crates/gpui/src/elements/img.rs` has `ImageSource::Render(Arc<RenderImage>)`, `ImageSource::Image` and `ImageSource::Custom` in the currently inspected source. That supports a first CPU-pixel path with decoded/allocated images. Exact `RenderImage` constructors may change: compile a 2-screen pixel-demo pinned to your chosen GPUI commit before building the worker. Source: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/gpui/src/elements/img.rs
    
    ### Phase 1: CPU pixels
    
    1. Worker publishes normalized native-resolution RGB(A) screen images to shared-memory slots.
    2. Rust receiver validates descriptor/sequence/format and obtains or copies complete frames.
    3. Presenter creates a GPUI renderable image on demand and keeps only the newest displayable frame per active session.
    4. UI repaints at host display rate, independent of emulated frame timing; repeated frames should be permitted. Capture path uses raw frames and metadata independently of UI composition.
    5. Touch mapping uses *actual bottom-screen transform*: inverse translation/scale/rotation/zoom, clamp to native `320x240`, check pointer-down/move/release semantics, and capture the input device identity.
    
    ### Phase 2: GPU acceleration
    
    Azahar's accelerated renderer can produce Vulkan textures, while GPUI's native Windows rendering does not automatically consume them. Proof-of-concept options:
    
    - Vulkan image -> asynchronous GPU readback -> pinned CPU memory -> GPUI image. Simplest reliable progression.
    - Vulkan/D3D shared texture interop (Windows): export/import memory and synchronization objects where supported, match adapter/LUID and format, manage ownership/fences and lifetime. Needs native GPUI element/renderer extension, not just wrapping a texture handle in `img()`.
    - macOS: investigate Metal bridge/copy path separately; no assumption about Vulkan-to-Metal zero-copy.
    - Linux: investigate DMA-BUF/Vulkan interop and GPUI backend support separately.
    
    Every accelerated path must preserve a CPU fallback and report end-to-end display latency including synchronization stalls. Display throughput is not guest hardware timing.
    
    ## GPUI performance plan
    
    - Bound update rate of expensive inspectors; separate **display refresh** from **debugger state refresh**.
    - Use generation-indexed immutable snapshots and virtualized lists for instruction/event tables; never construct 100k UI rows every frame.
    - Asset lifetime: cache only bounded texture previews keyed by `(instance, frame_id, resource_id, epoch)`; evict LRU and invalidate on reset.
    - Avoid per-frame image decoding/allocations if a reusable buffer path works; benchmark the chosen GPUI image construction API.
    - Render high-cardinality timelines from compact downsampled event bins at the selected zoom; fetch full events only when selected.
    - Profile GPUI executor lag, IPC dequeue, image upload, paint time, UI stalls and presentation latency separately from native worker timings.
    
    ## Suggested app state transitions
    
    `NoSession -> Starting -> Ready -> Loading -> Running <-> Paused -> Stopping -> Stopped`. Other transitions: `Faulted`, `Disconnected`, `NeedsInput`, `Capturing`. UI action is disabled until legal. `Reset` invalidates old memory/resource generation and pending disassembly/capture requests.
    
    ## First compile-only spike
    
    1. Use pinned GPUI commit and official standalone app entrypoint.
    2. Show two dynamic generated test patterns, not a ROM.
    3. Sustain continuous frame replacement and interactive scaling for 10 minutes; check retained memory; measure CPU upload cost.
    4. Simulate 4 sessions with 2 screens each using synthetic changing frames; ensure inactive tabs don't consume similar UI resources as active ones.
    5. Draw a virtual 320x240 touch target overlay, click corners, verify inverse transform under zoom and DPI scaling.
    6. Suspend/restart frame production without dropping the UI; test worker-initiated format/size changes.
    
    This reduces risk before integrating Azahar's renderer and shows whether GPUI changes require custom Elements.
    
    ## Accessibility / quality
    
    Support keyboard navigation, visible focus, screen-reader labels where GPUI exposes them, colorblind-friendly state markers, actual selectable/copyable diagnostic text, accessible high-contrast mode. Debug panes should provide small exportable text artifacts as an alternative to screenshots.
    # 09 - MCP, programmatic debugging and scenario runner
    
    ## Architecture
    
    MCP is an **adapter to the Rust session supervisor**, not a second debugger implementation. Use the Rust MCP SDK (`rmcp`, pin version and check actual API). The same typed operations must be available through: GPUI actions, `ctr-cli`, test scripts and MCP. MCP tools return bounded structured records plus artifact handles; raw multi-megabyte traces/screenshots are resources/files, never giant tool response bodies.
    
    ## MCP tool taxonomy
    
    | Group | Suggested tools | Design constraints |
    |---|---|---|
    | Session | `session_create`, `session_load`, `session_status`, `session_stop`, `session_list` | explicit instance IDs; no accidental 'current' global |
    | Control | `run_until`, `pause`, `reset`, `step_instruction`, `step_frame` | guest and wall timeout, stop reason |
    | CPU | `cpu_state`, `disassemble`, `breakpoint_set`, `breakpoint_remove` | core/thread/process selectors |
    | Memory | `memory_map`, `memory_read`, `memory_write`, `memory_compare` | byte caps, explicit address space, write permission |
    | Kernel | `thread_list`, `ipc_trace`, `handle_lookup` | bounded lists, parsed + raw fallbacks |
    | GPU | `gpu_capture_frame`, `gpu_capture_draw`, `gpu_registers`, `texture_export` | state-at-draw, resource hashes, renderer sync |
    | Trace | `trace_configure`, `trace_start`, `trace_stop`, `artifact_list`, `artifact_open` | budgets, loss reporting, artifacts |
    | Tests | `scenario_run`, `scenario_cancel`, `scenario_result`, `comparison_run` | background jobs owned by supervisor, not open loops in tool call |
    
    Prefer fewer higher-value tools and a composable `scenario_run` over thousands of single-frame requests. Do not expose arbitrary `execute_shell`, arbitrary OS memory reads or unrestricted host filesystem access through MCP.
    
    ## Resources and metadata
    
    Resources can expose versioned immutable artifacts: screenshots, GPU command lists, memory dumps, trace summaries, reports. Use URI-like handles such as `ctr://session/<id>/artifact/<artifact-id>` if supported by the MCP SDK; access control must be validated on every resource read. Resource description includes content type, size, hash, epoch, lifetime and provenance. `artifact_open` should allow bounded ranges / paging for large traces.
    
    ## Example successful agent workflow
    
    **Question:** Why does a title-screen animation get choppy in the original 3DS-targeting program?
    
    1. Agent creates two sessions: baseline build and candidate build, each with private storage and identical emulator model/options.
    2. Runs a deterministic input script to a title-screen checkpoint, explicitly disables live input.
    3. Captures frame pacing, guest CPU samples, draw/transfer counts, rasterizer-cache events and host profiler metrics; selects 3 anomalous frames for L2 snapshots.
    4. Compares draw counts/command order and CPU SVC/thread waits. It may identify CPU-higher work or host-emulation stalls but **must not infer actual Old 3DS GPU milliseconds from host renderer timing**.
    5. If hardware performance prediction matters, requests the corresponding Coffeepot/physical-console benchmark or marks this question unresolved.
    6. Exports a small Markdown finding, commands/scripts, capture manifest, diff report and confidence labels.
    
    ## Scenarios: deterministic, bounded and repeatable
    
    A scenario is declarative data with a **start state**, **input ownership**, **actions/checkpoints**, **stop condition**, **capture policy**, and **assertions**. See `specs/scenario-example.yaml`.
    
    Requirements:
    - Every scenario must have a terminal condition and host timeout; `run forever` is invalid for automation.
    - `seed`, virtual-clock policy, initial save/NAND snapshot, game hash, model, graphics backend, worker SHA and build flags are recorded.
    - Inputs are sampled at explicit guest boundaries or frame IDs. If replay requires exact instruction tick timing, only claim it when supported; frame-anchored input is a weaker level.
    - Detect desync at checkpoints using targeted stable state (PC/thread, memory ranges, framebuffer hash, GPU state). Hashes must exclude volatile fields unless relevant.
    - For gameplay checks, show script coverage and which branch actually executed; a passing fixture for an unused fast path isn't evidence that optimization helped the game.
    - Assertions can be `equal`, `within_tolerance`, `monotonic`, `event_seen`, `no_event`, `frame_count`, `resource_limit`, `stop_reason`, etc., with explicit confidence of signal.
    
    ## Agent ergonomics
    
    A single `run_until` can return:
    
    ```json
    {
      "session_id":"<uuid>", "epoch":4, "stop_reason":"breakpoint",
      "guest_tick":123456789, "process_id":12, "thread_id":7,
      "artifacts":["ctr://session/.../trace/..."]
    }
    ```
    
    Never silently fall back from `step_cpu_instruction` to `step_frame`. Return `UNSUPPORTED` with `available_alternatives` when semantics cannot be met. Make tool schemas self-describing and prefer typed enums over stringly typed free-form commands.
    
    ## Concurrency
    
    - One **lease owner** for state-mutating control of a session at any time (UI or agent). Other clients may read immutable snapshots. Lease has timeout and revocation on disconnect.
    - Queue operations with priorities and explicit budgeting; `stop`/cancel remains available even when trace export is active.
    - A scenario runner owns its input channel; manual keyboard changes are suspended or require explicit takeover with scenario failure marker.
    - An agent should be able to spawn multiple sessions but supervisor enforces total CPU, RAM, GPU, disk and concurrent-run quotas.
    
    ## Failure modes
    
    - Agent asks for memory past mapped range -> partial read with typed holes or explicit error.
    - Agent uses stale epoch -> `STALE_EPOCH`, not accidental reads from another program.
    - GPU readback not supported -> `UNSUPPORTED`, no made-up capture.
    - Scenario times out -> partial artifact pack with `INCOMPLETE` and last stable checkpoint, not green result.
    - Worker crashes -> supervisor preserves per-run metadata and stdout/stderr while invalidating shared-memory handles.
    - Tool uses nonsensical clock time -> error with valid time domains.
    
    ## Security
    
    Local MCP stdio is a good initial transport. Refuse broad remote-listen defaults. Require per-session grants for writes, launch, attaching to user-provided firmware and reading captures. Validate every path under a managed run root and never let model-generated commands pass directly to shell execution. Allow explicit user approval for destructive file/restore operations.
    
    ## API versioning and tests
    
    Include tool compatibility matrix (`MCP tool version -> protocol -> worker capability`). Generate tool schemas from shared Rust types. Contract tests must run the *same* command through CLI and MCP and compare normalized result. Add fuzz tests for invalid addresses, malformed tool payloads, huge lists and expired artifact handles.
    # 10 - Multiple independent emulator instances and storage
    
    ## Why separate OS processes are mandatory at bootstrap
    
    Azahar's `Core::System` is implemented as a static singleton (`System::s_instance`) and other process-wide settings/file utilities exist. Running two 'systems' in one address space would require a broad refactor of global state, GDB/RPC ports, file paths, audio mixers and renderer lifetimes. Do not take that dependency before the rest of the product works. Multiple worker processes are isolated by address space, can be killed independently, and are easy for a Rust supervisor to manage.
    
    ## Session root layout
    
    ```text
    workspace/
      profiles/                         reusable read-only configurations
      base/                             user-supplied immutable NAND/SD/firmware base refs
      instances/
        <uuid>/
          config/                        instance settings and input mapping
          fs-overlay/                    writable NAND/SD/save changes
          shader-cache/                 per-instance unless verified safe shared cache
          captures/                      immutable trace/frame artifacts
          logs/                          worker stdout/stderr and structured log
          ipc/                           Unix socket or named-pipe metadata
          snapshots/                     backend-versioned save states
          manifest.json                  versions, paths (redacted in exports), lifecycle
      results/                           run reports, corpus
    ```
    
    Base files are referenced by a manifest/reader abstraction, not copied indiscriminately into each run. However, **read-only overlays are an implementation project**, not a guaranteed feature of Azahar's file abstractions. First implement separate full working directories and verify isolation; introduce copy-on-write only after proving every write path is intercepted. For reliability, a copied/private NAND/SD root is preferable to an incomplete COW implementation.
    
    ## Resource ownership
    
    - Each worker gets unique session UUID, IPC endpoint, logging destination, GDB port (if enabled), per-instance emulator config and saves.
    - Host input devices are mapped to explicit worker(s); duplicate broadcast input is opt-in and labeled.
    - Audio: route each worker's output independently; allow global mixer and per-worker mute/volume, but no shared guest DSP state.
    - GPU: separate Vulkan devices/queues/surfaces where driver behavior requires. Shared hardware means performance contention; four workers do *not* behave as four independent physical consoles in real time.
    - Files: no two workers write same physical path unless a proven safe shared cache with atomic/immutable file semantics.
    - Hardware console/network devices: exclusive resource leases; UDS/local wireless is a separate emulation problem.
    
    ## Scheduling and host interference
    
    Expose policies:
    
    - `interactive`: foreground display/audio at host refresh, others continue normally but may skip UI frames.
    - `benchmark`: throttle background activity or serialize independent timing measurements to eliminate noisy neighbors; record host load.
    - `batch`: headless unthrottled execution where supported, host CPU/GPU ceilings and disk cap.
    - `accuracy`: more expensive reference model if available, explicitly reduced emulation speed.
    
    **Never infer hardware cycle timing from host execution wall time**, especially under multi-instance contention. Separate the workload's emulated guest timestamps from host scheduler stalls.
    
    ## Instance lifecycle
    
    States: `CREATED`, `STARTING`, `READY`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSING`, `PAUSED`, `CAPTURING`, `STOPPING`, `STOPPED`, `FAILED`, `ORPHANED`.
    
    For each:
    1. Supervisor creates root with permissions and lock, validates user assets and quotas.
    2. Spawns child with only necessary arguments/environment and private endpoint capability.
    3. Handshake verifies protocol, worker SHA and available backend features.
    4. Worker loads content; reaches running/paused state; reports checkpoint.
    5. On stop, `RequestShutdown` is processed, files flushed, renderer/audio stopped, child exits and resources reaped.
    6. If timeout/crash, terminate process tree, mark captures partial, preserve logs; remove stale IPC and lock **only after verifying worker PID/liveness**.
    
    ## Clone and snapshots
    
    Initial cloning means **start new worker with same immutable ROM, profile, initial save data and input script**. It does not require cloning RAM/CPU state.
    
    Later `clone_checkpoint` may use Azahar save states, but must capture/verify:
    - Azahar worker commit and serialization schema version.
    - No pending unsupported async operations; Azahar's `RunLoop` already delays/fails saves when async kernel operations are pending.
    - Shader/cache/graphics resource state on restore, DSP and input state, epoch increment and rebind of debugging IDs.
    - Correct restoration of guest timer seeds and per-instance user data.
    - Whether saves are compatible between integration and experimental branches; default to **incompatible until tested**.
    
    For test automation, prefer a repeatable scripted boot to a known checkpoint if save-state correctness is uncertain.
    
    ## Stress/acceptance tests
    
    - Four workers boot test homebrew from a common immutable executable, each with isolated writable root; each finishes exact fixed-frame scenario.
    - Simultaneous saves yield four independent results; verify no shared writes or cache corruption via filesystem auditing.
    - Kill one worker mid-save; other three keep running; damaged overlay is detected/recovered or surfaced.
    - Start two GDB-enabled workers; ports never collide. Existing Azahar UDP RPC is disabled to avoid fixed-port collision.
    - Deliberately exhaust memory/disk quota in one instance; others remain operable, supervisor returns bounded error.
    - Restart same instance UUID after crash with new epoch; stale renderer shared-memory clients cannot access old slot handles.
    - Run same test in four processes and compare stable output hashes; document nondeterministic causes.
    
    ## Later optimization
    
    Only after profiling consider sharing read-only ROM mappings, shader compilation cache and immutable assets across processes. Shared writable GPU caches or HLE state are high risk. OS-level memory deduplication and copy-on-write file cloning may already provide sufficient benefit without dangerous in-process embedding.

    namespace CtrWorker {
    using Json = nlohmann::json;
    class Control {
    public:
        explicit Control(std::string root) : root(std::filesystem::absolute(root)) {}
        int Run() {
    #ifdef _WIN32
            _setmode(_fileno(stdout), _O_BINARY);
    #endif
            Initialize(system, root.string(), unsupported);
            RegisterInput(input);
            Settings::values.output_type = AudioCore::SinkType::Worker;
            Frontend::control_callback = [this] { Drain(true); };
            std::thread reader{[this] {
                while (!stopping) {
                    Json request;
                    if (!Receive(request, stopping))
                        break;
                    {
                        std::scoped_lock lock{mutex};
                        if (queue.size() >= 16)
                            break;
                        queue.push_back(std::move(request));
                    }
                    system.NotifyPendingWork();
                }
                disconnected = true;
                system.NotifyPendingWork();
            }};
            try {
                while (!stopping && !disconnected) {
                    Drain(false);
                    if (state == "running") {
                        const auto result = system.RunLoop();
                        if (result != Core::System::ResultStatus::Success || unsupported ||
                            window.frames >= target || std::chrono::steady_clock::now() >= deadline) {
                            state = "paused";
                            last_error = unsupported ? "unsupported_applet"
                                         : result != Core::System::ResultStatus::Success ? "core_error"
                                         : window.frames < target ? "host_deadline"
                                                                  : "";
                            if (pending_run) {
                                Reply(*pending_run,
                                      last_error.empty() ? "ok"
                                      : unsupported      ? "unsupported"
                                                         : "not_ready",
                                      Snapshot());
                                pending_run.reset();
                            }
                        }
                    } else {
                        system.ProcessPendingWorkUntil(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() +
                                                       std::chrono::milliseconds(10));
                    }
                }
            } catch (const std::exception& error) {
                std::cerr << "worker_control_error: " << error.what() << '\n';
                exit_code = 1;
            }
            stopping = true;
            reader.join();
            Frontend::control_callback = {};
            if (system.IsPoweredOn())
                system.Shutdown();
            Common::Log::Stop();
            return exit_code;
        }
    
    private:
        Json Snapshot() {
            const auto audio = AudioCore::WorkerSink::Drain();
            return {{"backend_name", CTR_BACKEND_NAME}, {"source", CTR_SOURCE_SHA}, {"frames", window.frames},
                    {"last_error", last_error},         {"input_owner", owner},
                    {"buttons", input.buttons},         {"touch_down", input.touch},
                    {"audio_samples", audio.samples},   {"audio_dropped", audio.dropped},
                    {"audio_hash_fnv1a64", audio.hash}, {"audio_buffered", audio.buffered}};
        }
        void Reply(const Json& request, const std::string& status, Json data = nullptr) {
            Send({{"version_major", 1},
                  {"version_minor", 0},
                  {"request_id", request.at("request_id")},
                  {"session", request.at("session")},
                  {"epoch", epoch},
                  {"status", status},
                  {"state", state},
                  {"backend", "azahar_native_software"},
                  {"data", std::move(data)}});
        }
        void Drain(bool nested) {
            // Never destroy/reinitialize a core while inside its RunLoop/frame limiter.
            for (unsigned count = 0; count < 16; ++count) {
                Json request;
                {
                    std::scoped_lock lock{mutex};
                    if (queue.empty())
                        return;
                    const auto method = queue.front().value("method", std::string{});
                    if (nested && method != "status" && method != "registers" &&
                        method != "read_memory")
                        return;
                    request = std::move(queue.front());
                    queue.pop_front();
                }
                Handle(request);
                if (stopping)
                    return;
            }
        }
        void Handle(const Json& request) {
            // Invalid envelopes end the connection: there may be no trustworthy reply identity.
            if (!request.is_object() || !request.contains("request_id") ||
                !request["request_id"].is_number_unsigned() || request["request_id"].get<u64>() == 0 ||
                !request.contains("session") || !request["session"].is_string() ||
                !request.contains("epoch") || !request["epoch"].is_number_unsigned() ||
                !request.contains("method") || !request["method"].is_string() ||
                !request.contains("version_major") || !request.contains("version_minor"))
                throw std::runtime_error("invalid request envelope");
            for (const auto& [key, value] : request.items())
                if (key != "version_major" && key != "version_minor" && key != "request_id" &&
                    key != "session" && key != "epoch" && key != "method" && key != "params")
                    throw std::runtime_error("unknown envelope field");
            const auto id = request["session"].get<std::string>();
            if (id.size() != 32 || id.find_first_not_of("0123456789abcdefABCDEF") != std::string::npos)
                throw std::runtime_error("invalid session");
            if (request["request_id"].get<u64>() <= last_request)
                throw std::runtime_error("request IDs must increase; retries are forbidden");
            last_request = request["request_id"].get<u64>();
            if (request["version_major"] != 1 || request["version_minor"] != 0) {
                Reply(request, "unsupported");
                return;
            }
            if (!session.empty() && session != id) {
                Reply(request, "permission_denied");
                return;
            }
            if (request["epoch"] != epoch) {
                Reply(request, "stale_epoch");
                return;
            }
            const auto method = request["method"].get<std::string>();
            if (method == "hello" && session.empty())
                session = id;
            if (session.empty()) {
                Reply(request, "not_ready");
                return;
            }
            try {
                const auto params = request.value("params", Json::object());
                if (method == "hello" || method == "status") {
                    Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                    return;
                }
                if (method == "stop") {
                    state = "stopped";
                    if (system.IsPoweredOn())
                        system.Shutdown();
                    Reply(request, "ok");
                    stopping = true;
                    return;
                }
                if (method == "load" || method == "reset") {
                    if (state == "running") {
                        Reply(request, "not_ready");
                        return;
                    }
                    const auto path = method == "load" ? params.at("path").get<std::string>() : content;
                    if (path.empty() || !std::filesystem::is_regular_file(path) ||
                        std::filesystem::path(path).extension() != ".3dsx") {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
                        return;
                    }
                    if (system.IsPoweredOn())
                        system.Shutdown();
                    unsupported = false;
                    input = {};
                    window.frames = 0;
                    last_error.clear();
                    owner = "live";
                    AudioCore::WorkerSink::Reset();
                    const auto result = system.Load(window, path);
                    if (result != Core::System::ResultStatus::Success) {
                        if (system.IsPoweredOn())
                            system.Shutdown();
                        state = "idle";
                        Reply(request, "not_ready", {{"load_result", static_cast<u32>(result)}});
                        return;
                    }
                    content = path;
                    state = "paused";
                    ++epoch;
                    Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                    return;
                }
                if (!system.IsPoweredOn()) {
                    Reply(request, "not_ready");
                    return;
                }
                if (method == "run" || method == "run_until") {
                    if (state != "paused" || pending_run) {
                        Reply(request, "not_ready");
                        return;
                    }
                    const auto frames = Unsigned(params, "frames", 600);
                    if (frames == 0 || frames > 600) {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
                        return;
                    }
                    target = window.frames + frames;
                    deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(20);
                    state = "running";
                    if (method == "run_until")
                        pending_run = request;
                    else
                        Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                } else if (method == "pause") {
                    state = "paused";
                    if (pending_run) {
                        Reply(*pending_run, "not_ready", {{"reason", "interrupted"}});
                        pending_run.reset();
                    }
                    Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                } else if (method == "capture") {
                    if (!window.frames) {
                        Reply(request, "not_ready");
                        return;
                    }
                    Reply(request, "ok",
                          {{"frames", Capture(system, root, epoch, ++capture_sequence)},
                           {"frame", window.frames}});
                } else if (method == "input") {
                    const auto requested_owner = params.at("owner").get<std::string>();
                    if (requested_owner != "live" && requested_owner != "scenario") {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
                        return;
                    }
                    if (owner == "scenario" && requested_owner != owner) {
                        Reply(request, "permission_denied");
                        return;
                    }
                    const auto buttons = static_cast<u32>(
                        Unsigned(params, "buttons", (1u << Settings::NativeButton::NumButtons) - 1));
                    const auto x = Unsigned(params, "x", 319), y = Unsigned(params, "y", 239);
                    if (buttons >= (1u << Settings::NativeButton::NumButtons) || x >= 320 || y >= 240) {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
                        return;
                    }
                    owner = requested_owner;
                    input = {buttons, x / 320.0f, y / 240.0f, params.value("touch", false)};
                    Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                } else if (method == "registers") {
                    const auto core = static_cast<u32>(Unsigned(params, "core", 3));
                    if (core >= system.GetNumCores()) {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
                        return;
                    }
                    Json registers = Json::array();
                    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
                        registers.push_back(system.GetCore(core).GetReg(i));
                    Reply(request, "ok",
                          {{"core", core},
                           {"registers", registers},
                           {"cpsr", system.GetCore(core).GetCPSR()},
                           {"safe_point", true}});
                } else if (method == "read_memory") {
                    const auto address = Unsigned(params, "address", 0xffffffffull),
                               length = Unsigned(params, "length", 4096);
                    const auto process = system.Kernel().GetCurrentProcess();
                    if (!process || length == 0 || length > 4096 || address + length > 0x100000000ull ||
                        address > 0xffffffffull) {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
                        return;
                    }
                    for (u64 i = 0; i < length; ++i)
                        if (!system.Memory().IsValidVirtualAddress(*process,
                                                                   static_cast<u32>(address + i))) {
                            Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
                            return;
                        }
                    std::vector<u8> bytes(length);
                    system.Memory().ReadBlock(*process, static_cast<u32>(address), bytes.data(),
                                              length);
                    Reply(request, "ok",
                          {{"address", address}, {"bytes", bytes}, {"safe_point", true}});
                } else
                    Reply(request, "unsupported");
            } catch (const std::invalid_argument&) {
                Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
            } catch (const Json::exception&) {
                Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
            } catch (const std::filesystem::filesystem_error&) {
                Reply(request, "invalid_argument");
            } catch (const std::runtime_error& error) {
                Reply(request, "unsupported", {{"reason", error.what()}});
            }
        }
        static u64 Unsigned(const Json& params, const char* key, u64 maximum) {
            if (!params.contains(key) || !params.at(key).is_number_unsigned() ||
                params.at(key).get<u64>() > maximum)
                throw std::invalid_argument("expected bounded unsigned integer");
            return params.at(key).get<u64>();
        }
        Core::System& system = Core::System::GetInstance();
        std::filesystem::path root;
        Window window;
        InputState input;
        std::string session, content, last_error, state = "idle", owner = "live";
        u64 epoch = 1, target = 0, capture_sequence = 0, last_request = 0;
        bool unsupported = false;
        int exit_code = 0;
        std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point deadline;
        std::optional<Json> pending_run;
        std::mutex mutex;
        std::deque<Json> queue;
        std::atomic_bool stopping = false, disconnected = false;
    };

            std::cout << "presented_frames=" << window.frames
                      << " result=" << static_cast<unsigned>(result)
                      << " unsupported_applet=" << unsupported << std::endl;
            if (window.frames >= 60)
                std::cout << CtrWorker::Capture(system, argv[3], 1, window.frames).dump() << std::endl;
            if (system.IsPoweredOn())
                system.Shutdown();
            Common::Log::Stop();
            return result == Core::System::ResultStatus::Success && window.frames >= 60 && !unsupported
                       ? 0
                       : 1;
        }
        std::cerr
            << "usage: ctr-worker --version | --probe-core | --boot <homebrew.3dsx> <private-root>\n";
        return 2;
    }

    //! Local host policy shared by the headless MCP server and the desktop.
    //!
    //! One `Supervisor` owns every session of a LOTUS process. Each session has its
    //! own async lock, so a long bounded run on one session never blocks commands,
    //! status or previews of another. The registry lock is never held across an
    //! await. Desktop and MCP call the same methods; there is one control model.

    //! scratch copy, discarded on end); see [`crate::card_store`].
