        pub worker: PathBuf,
        pub storage_root: PathBuf,

        #[serde(default)]
        pub assets: BTreeMap<String, PathBuf>,
        /// Approved directories: every `.3dsx` directly inside is `<handle>/<file>`.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub asset_directories: BTreeMap<String, PathBuf>,
        #[serde(default)]
        pub allow_control: bool,
        #[serde(default = "default_max_sessions")]

    fn default_max_sessions() -> usize {

    impl HostConfig {
        /// Configuration with no assets, control denied and the default session limit.
        pub fn new(worker: impl Into<PathBuf>, storage_root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
            Self {

                storage_root: storage_root.into(),
                assets: BTreeMap::new(),
                asset_directories: BTreeMap::new(),
                allow_control: false,

    /// Whether a session's guest writes persist.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]

        Primary { card: String },
        /// Private scratch root, empty or copied from `parent`; discarded on end.
        Secondary { parent: Option<String> },
    }
    
    /// Identity of a session as listed by every frontend.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
    pub struct SessionInfo {
        pub id: String,
        #[serde(flatten)]
        pub kind: SessionKind,

    impl SessionInfo {

    /// One session row: identity plus latest gauges.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]

        pub height: u32,
        pub bytes: usize,
        pub sha256: String,
    }
    
    /// A session's lock domain. Lock order: `native`, then `info` or `telemetry`.
    struct SessionHandle {
        info: Mutex<SessionInfo>,
        root: PathBuf,
        native: tokio::sync::Mutex<NativeSession>,
        telemetry: Mutex<Telemetry>,
        playing: AtomicBool,
    }
    
    impl SessionHandle {
        fn info(&self) -> SessionInfo {
            lock(&self.info).clone()
        }
        fn telemetry(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Telemetry> {
            lock(&self.telemetry)
        }
        fn record(&self, actor: Actor, operation: &str) {
            self.telemetry().record(actor, operation);
        }
        fn set_playing(&self, playing: bool) {
            self.playing.store(playing, Ordering::Release);
            self.telemetry().playing = playing;
        }
        fn is_playing(&self) -> bool {
            self.playing.load(Ordering::Acquire)
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Default)]
    struct Registry {
        sessions: BTreeMap<String, Arc<SessionHandle>>,
        /// Creations in progress, counted against the session limit.
        pending: usize,
        /// Card name to mounting session (or pending creation) ID.
        mounted: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    }
    
    /// No shell execution, arbitrary caller paths or remote listener.
    pub struct Supervisor {
        config: HostConfig,
        cards: CardStore,
        registry: Mutex<Registry>,
        artifacts: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, (Artifact, PathBuf)>>,
        /// Content approved interactively by the desktop user.
        local_assets: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, PathBuf>>,
        focus_request: Mutex<Option<String>>,
    }
    
    impl Supervisor {
        pub fn new(mut config: HostConfig) -> io::Result<Self> {
            if !(1..=MAX_SESSIONS_LIMIT).contains(&config.max_sessions) {
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                    format!("max_sessions must be in 1..={MAX_SESSIONS_LIMIT}"),
                ));
            }
            config.worker = config.worker.canonicalize()?;
            for path in config.assets.values_mut() {
                *path = path.canonicalize()?;
            }
            for (handle, path) in &mut config.asset_directories {
                if handle.is_empty() || handle.contains(['/', '\\']) {
                    return Err(io::Error::new(
                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                        "asset directory handles cannot be empty or contain separators",
                    ));
                }
                *path = path.canonicalize()?;
            }
            fs::create_dir_all(&config.storage_root)?;
            config.storage_root = config.storage_root.canonicalize()?;
            let cards = CardStore::open(&config.storage_root)?;
            Ok(Self {
                config,
                cards,
                registry: Mutex::default(),
                artifacts: Mutex::default(),
                local_assets: Mutex::default(),
                focus_request: Mutex::default(),
            })
        }
    
        #[must_use]
        pub fn max_sessions(&self) -> usize {
            self.config.max_sessions
        }
    
        #[must_use]
        pub fn allows_control(&self) -> bool {
            self.config.allow_control
        }
    
        pub fn require_control(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
            if self.config.allow_control {
                Ok(())

                    io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied,
                    "host has not enabled control for this client",

            }
        }
    
        /// Session IDs in creation-independent sorted order.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn sessions(&self) -> Vec<String> {
            lock(&self.registry).sessions.keys().cloned().collect()
        }
    
        /// Every session with its latest gauges; never waits on a worker.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn summaries(&self) -> Vec<SessionSummary> {
            self.handles()
                .iter()
                .map(|handle| SessionSummary {
                    info: handle.info(),
                    telemetry: handle.telemetry().clone(),
                })
                .collect()
        }
    
        pub fn summary(&self, id: &str) -> io::Result<SessionSummary> {
            let handle = self.handle(id)?;
            let telemetry = handle.telemetry().clone();
            Ok(SessionSummary {
                info: handle.info(),
                telemetry,
            })
        }
    
        /// Persistent card names.

        }
    
        /// Cards currently mounted by a primary session of this host.

        pub fn mounted_cards(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
            lock(&self.registry).mounted.clone()

        /// Approved content handles: configured, directory-listed and desktop-approved.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn assets(&self) -> Vec<String> {
            let mut handles: Vec<String> = self.config.assets.keys().cloned().collect();
            for (handle, directory) in &self.config.asset_directories {
                let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(directory) else {
                    continue;
                };
                for entry in entries.flatten() {
                    let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
                    if is_content_name(&name) && entry.path().is_file() {
                        handles.push(format!("{handle}/{name}"));
                    }
                }
            }
            handles.extend(lock(&self.local_assets).keys().cloned());
            handles.sort();

    //! Headless LOTUS: the MCP server over stdio, no window.
    //!
    //! Local only: no TCP listener is opened and no remote client can attach. When
    //! the client disconnects every session is stopped, so secondary data is
    //! discarded and primary cards are unlocked.
    
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use lotus_mcp::LotusServer;
    use lotus_session::supervisor::HostConfig;
    use rmcp::ServiceExt;
    
    #[tokio::main]
    async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        let server = if let Some(path) = std::env::args_os().nth(1) {
            let config: HostConfig = serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(path)?)?;
            LotusServer::configured(config, std::collections::BTreeMap::new())?
        } else {
            LotusServer::new()
        };
        let host = server.host().cloned();
        let pump = host.clone().map(|host| {
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                loop {
                    host.pump().await;
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
                }
            })
        });
        let service = server.serve(rmcp::transport::stdio()).await?;
        let result = service.waiting().await;
        if let Some(pump) = pump {
            pump.abort();
        }
        if let Some(host) = host {
            host.close().await;
        }
        result?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Which frontend hosts this server; reported to clients.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum Frontend {
        Headless,
        Windowed,
    }
    
    impl Frontend {
        fn name(self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                Frontend::Headless => "headless",
                Frontend::Windowed => "windowed",
            }
        }
    }
    
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct LotusServer {
        tool_router: ToolRouter<Self>,

        frontend: Frontend,
        scenarios: BTreeMap<String, PathBuf>,
    }
    
    impl Default for LotusServer {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self::new()
        }
    }
    
    impl LotusServer {
        /// Status-only server: cannot spawn workers or read files.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self {
                tool_router: Self::tool_router(),
                host: None,
                frontend: Frontend::Headless,
                scenarios: BTreeMap::new(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Headless server owning a new supervisor.
        pub fn configured(
            config: HostConfig,
            scenarios: BTreeMap<String, PathBuf>,
        ) -> io::Result<Self> {

                Frontend::Headless,
                scenarios,
            ))
        }
    
        /// Server over a supervisor another frontend also drives.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn shared(
            host: Arc<Supervisor>,
            frontend: Frontend,
            scenarios: BTreeMap<String, PathBuf>,
        ) -> Self {
            Self {
                tool_router: Self::tool_router(),
                host: Some(host),
                frontend,
                scenarios,
            }
        }

        pub fn host(&self) -> Option<&Arc<Supervisor>> {
            self.host.as_ref()
        }

            self.require_host()?.read_artifact(uri)
        }
    
        fn require_host(&self) -> io::Result<&Supervisor> {
            self.host.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| {

    fn tool_result(value: io::Result<Value>) -> CallToolResult {
        match value {
            Ok(value) => CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(value.to_string())]),
            Err(error) => CallToolResult::error(vec![ContentBlock::text(error.to_string())]),
        }
    }
    
    fn json<T: serde::Serialize>(value: &T) -> io::Result<Value> {
        serde_json::to_value(value).map_err(io::Error::other)
    }
    
    fn resource(artifact: &Artifact) -> Resource {
        Resource::new(&artifact.uri, &artifact.screen)
            .with_mime_type("application/octet-stream")
            .with_size(artifact.bytes as u64)
            .with_description(format!(
                "Native BGRA8 {}x{}, SHA-256 {}",
                artifact.width, artifact.height, artifact.sha256
            ))
    }

    //! Primary cards and secondary scratch roots below the host storage root.
    //!
    //! A primary session mounts `cards/<name>/` as its worker root, so Azahar's
    //! `sdmc/`, `nand/` and `sysdata/` (`common_paths.h`) persist between runs. A
    //! secondary session gets `scratch/<session>/`: empty, or a point-in-time host
    //! copy of one card's guest directories. The copy is not coordinated with a
    //! running parent's guest writes. Scratch guest data is deleted when the
    //! secondary ends; worker logs are kept only when it ended abnormally.
    use std::fs::{self, File};
    use std::io;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    
    /// Guest-visible directories copied into a secondary from its parent card.
    pub const GUEST_DIRS: [&str; 3] = ["sdmc", "nand", "sysdata"];
    /// Largest parent copy accepted for one secondary.
    pub const MAX_COPY_BYTES: u64 = 4 << 30;
    /// Host diagnostics retained after an abnormal end.
    const RETAINED: [&str; 3] = ["worker.stderr.log", "log", "native-manifest.json"];
    
    /// Owns the `cards/` and `scratch/` directories of one storage root.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub struct CardStore {
        cards: PathBuf,
        scratch: PathBuf,
    }
    
    impl CardStore {
        /// Create both directories and discard scratch data left by a previous host.
        pub fn open(storage_root: &Path) -> io::Result<Self> {
            let store = Self {
                cards: storage_root.join("cards"),
                scratch: storage_root.join("scratch"),
            };
            fs::create_dir_all(&store.cards)?;
            fs::create_dir_all(&store.scratch)?;
            store.sweep()?;
            Ok(store)
        }
    
        /// Card names in sorted order.
        pub fn list(&self) -> io::Result<Vec<String>> {
            let mut names = Vec::new();
            for entry in fs::read_dir(&self.cards)? {
                let entry = entry?;
                let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
                if entry.file_type()?.is_dir() && validate_name(&name).is_ok() {
                    names.push(name);
                }
            }
            names.sort();
            Ok(names)
        }
    
        /// Root of a primary card, created on first use.
        pub fn primary_root(&self, name: &str) -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
            validate_name(name)?;
            let root = self.cards.join(name);
            fs::create_dir_all(&root)?;
            if is_locked(&root)? {
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::ResourceBusy,
                    format!("card '{name}' is mounted by another LOTUS process"),
                ));
            }
            Ok(root)
        }
    
        /// Create a scratch root, optionally seeded from a card's guest directories.
        pub fn create_scratch(&self, session: &str, parent: Option<&str>) -> io::Result<PathBuf> {
            let root = self.scratch.join(session);
            fs::create_dir(&root)?;
            let Some(parent) = parent else {
                return Ok(root);
            };
            let result = (|| {
                validate_name(parent)?;
                let source = self.cards.join(parent);
                if !source.is_dir() {
                    return Err(io::Error::new(
                        io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
                        format!("unknown card '{parent}'"),
                    ));
                }
                let mut budget = MAX_COPY_BYTES;
                for name in GUEST_DIRS {
                    let from = source.join(name);
                    if from.is_dir() {
                        copy_tree(&from, &root.join(name), &mut budget)?;
                    }
                }
                Ok(())
            })();
            if let Err(error) = result {
                let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
                return Err(error);
            }
            Ok(root)
        }
    
        /// End a secondary. A clean end removes everything; otherwise logs remain.
        pub fn discard_scratch(&self, root: &Path, end: ScratchEnd) -> io::Result<()> {
            if root.parent() != Some(self.scratch.as_path()) {
                return Err(io::Error::other("refusing to discard a non-scratch root"));
            }
            match end {
                ScratchEnd::Clean => fs::remove_dir_all(root),
                ScratchEnd::Abnormal => discard_guest_data(root),
            }
        }
    
        /// Unlocked scratch roots belong to no live worker: drop their guest data.
        fn sweep(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
            for entry in fs::read_dir(&self.scratch)? {
                let root = entry?.path();
                if root.is_dir() && !is_locked(&root)? {
                    discard_guest_data(&root)?;
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    /// How a secondary ended, which decides whether its logs are kept.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub enum ScratchEnd {
        Clean,
        Abnormal,
    }
    
    /// Card names: 1-32 of `a-z 0-9 - _`, starting with a letter or digit.
    pub fn validate_name(name: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
        let valid = (1..=32).contains(&name.len())
            && name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit())
            && name
                .chars()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '-' || c == '_');
        if valid {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(io::Error::new(
                io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                "card name must be 1-32 of a-z, 0-9, '-', '_' and start with a letter or digit",
            ))
        }
    }
    
    /// Whether a live worker holds this root's lock. The worker's lock stays authoritative.
    fn is_locked(root: &Path) -> io::Result<bool> {
        let path = root.join("worker.lock");
        if !path.exists() {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let file = File::options().read(true).write(true).open(path)?;
        match file.try_lock() {
            Ok(()) => Ok(false),
            Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => Ok(true),
            Err(fs::TryLockError::Error(error)) => Err(error),
        }
    }
    
    fn discard_guest_data(root: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        for entry in fs::read_dir(root)? {
            let entry = entry?;
            if RETAINED.iter().any(|kept| entry.file_name() == *kept) {
                continue;
            }
            if entry.file_type()?.is_dir() {
                fs::remove_dir_all(entry.path())?;
            } else {
                fs::remove_file(entry.path())?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    /// Copy regular files and directories; links are refused rather than followed.
    fn copy_tree(from: &Path, to: &Path, budget: &mut u64) -> io::Result<()> {
        fs::create_dir_all(to)?;
        for entry in fs::read_dir(from)? {
            let entry = entry?;
            let kind = entry.file_type()?;
            let target = to.join(entry.file_name());
            if kind.is_dir() {
                copy_tree(&entry.path(), &target, budget)?;
            } else if kind.is_file() {
                let size = entry.metadata()?.len();
                *budget = budget.checked_sub(size).ok_or_else(|| {
                    io::Error::new(
                        io::ErrorKind::QuotaExceeded,
                        "parent card exceeds the 4 GiB secondary copy limit",
                    )
                })?;
                fs::copy(entry.path(), target)?;
            } else {
                return Err(io::Error::other(format!(
                    "refusing to copy link {}",
                    entry.path().display()
                )));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]

        fn store(name: &str) -> (PathBuf, CardStore) {

        #[test]
        fn names_reject_paths_and_uppercase() {
            for bad in ["", "..", "a/b", "a\\b", "Default", "-x", &"x".repeat(33)] {
                assert!(validate_name(bad).is_err(), "accepted {bad:?}");
            }
            for good in ["default", "hgss-dev", "p_2", "0"] {
                assert!(validate_name(good).is_ok(), "rejected {good:?}");
            }
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn secondary_copies_guest_dirs_and_writes_never_reach_parent() {
            let (base, store) = store("copy");
            let card = store.primary_root("dev").expect("card");
            fs::create_dir_all(card.join("sdmc/3ds")).expect("sdmc");
            fs::write(card.join("sdmc/3ds/save.bin"), b"parent").expect("seed");
            fs::write(card.join("worker.stderr.log"), b"not guest").expect("log");
    
            let scratch = store.create_scratch("s1", Some("dev")).expect("scratch");
            assert_eq!(
                fs::read(scratch.join("sdmc/3ds/save.bin")).expect("copied"),
                b"parent"
            );
            assert!(!scratch.join("worker.stderr.log").exists());
            fs::write(scratch.join("sdmc/3ds/save.bin"), b"child").expect("child write");
            assert_eq!(
                fs::read(card.join("sdmc/3ds/save.bin")).expect("parent"),
                b"parent"
            );
    
            store
                .discard_scratch(&scratch, ScratchEnd::Clean)
                .expect("discard");
            assert!(!scratch.exists());
            assert_eq!(store.list().expect("list"), vec!["dev".to_string()]);
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(base);
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn abnormal_end_keeps_logs_only_and_unknown_parent_fails_cleanly() {
            let (base, store) = store("abnormal");
            let scratch = store.create_scratch("s2", None).expect("empty scratch");
            fs::create_dir_all(scratch.join("sdmc")).expect("sdmc");
            fs::write(scratch.join("worker.stderr.log"), b"crash").expect("log");
            store
                .discard_scratch(&scratch, ScratchEnd::Abnormal)
                .expect("discard");
            assert!(!scratch.join("sdmc").exists());
            assert!(scratch.join("worker.stderr.log").exists());
    
            assert!(store.create_scratch("s3", Some("missing")).is_err());
            assert!(!base.join("scratch/s3").exists());
            assert!(store
                .discard_scratch(&base.join("cards"), ScratchEnd::Clean)
                .is_err());
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(base);
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn reopening_sweeps_unlocked_scratch_guest_data() {
            let (base, store) = store("sweep");
            let scratch = store.create_scratch("left", None).expect("scratch");
            fs::create_dir_all(scratch.join("nand")).expect("nand");
            drop(store);
            CardStore::open(&base).expect("reopen");
            assert!(!scratch.join("nand").exists());
            let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(base);
        }
    }

            ar & ncch_data;
        }
        friend class boost::serialization::access;
    };

    $dirty = & git -C $AzaharRoot status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal

    # Build and dependency pins
    
    LOTUS uses native process workers: **AZAHAR** (`integration`) and **CITnLO**
    (`experimental`). The future replacement backend is **LOTUS**. The two Azahar
    branches currently share integration code; no accuracy experiments exist yet.
    
    Immutable revisions live in [config/pins.toml](../config/pins.toml); Cargo.lock
    pins Rust dependencies and vendor/azahar pins native source. Upstream control:
    `11eceda5e0e682a1f44e396bf954a1b9137097ca`. GPUI/Zed:
    `6b720973027999bae402df23d469026f4cced988`. Rust:
    `1.98.1-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`.
    
    ## Build
    
    This Windows host uses GCC/MinGW-w64 16.2, CMake 4.4.3 and Ninja. MSVC and other
    host platforms are untested. GPUI links against Windows D3D import libraries.
    Its existing `.rsrc merge failure: multiple non-default manifests` warning remains
    visible; visual acceptance is deferred at the user's request.
    
    ```powershell
    scripts/bootstrap.ps1
    scripts/smoke.ps1
    scripts/build-azahar.ps1 -Branch integration
    scripts/build-azahar.ps1 -Branch experimental
    scripts/build-azahar.ps1 -Branch stock -Oracle -BuildDirectory build/azahar-stock
    ```
    
    Native builds require sibling worktrees `azahar-stock`, `azahar-integration`,
    `azahar-experimental`, or an explicit `-AzaharRoot`. Each must be clean at its
    manifest pin, with recursive submodules initialized. Existing worktrees were
    created from the supplied parent azahar clone; see [20](20-native-baseline.md).
    The script rejects moving/dirty inputs and a cache belonging to another tree.
    Each flavor has its own cache and `lotus-build-manifest.json` with SHA/flags/host.
    It builds native `ctr-worker` directly. `workers/azahar` is a retired scaffold
    stub and is not the runtime target. Local native commits must be published or
    transferred with their Git objects before a different machine can fetch the pins.
    
    The initial native matrix is Release, software renderer, Qt/SDL/Libretro off,
    host audio devices off, GDB compiled but disabled, LTO off. See script for every
    flag. There are no runtime dependency downloads and no bundled Nintendo assets.
    
    ## Run
    
    Create an ignored local host configuration as shown in [23](23-local-mcp.md).
    The desktop and MCP consume the same configuration and native session API:
    
    ```powershell
    cargo run -p lotus-desktop --bin lotus-desktop -- build/local-host.json
    cargo run -p lotus-mcp --bin lotus-mcp -- build/local-host.json
    cargo run -p lotus-cli --bin ctr-cli -- scenario run specs/native-smoke.yaml build/azahar-integration-native/bin/Release/ctr-worker.exe build/runs 3
    ```
    
    Both applications default to an empty host without configuration. Explicit
    approved asset handles avoid arbitrary-path MCP access. The desktop can create
    four sessions, select/dock screens, run/pause/reset/stop and route keyboard/touch.
    No real audio device is opened; the native DSP sink drains a bounded muted ring.
    
    ## Verification and source map
    
    `cargo test --workspace`, rustfmt and Clippy cover the Rust workspace. Asset
    tests are explicitly opt-in using `LOTUS_NATIVE_WORKER` and `LOTUS_FIXTURE`:
    
    ```powershell
    scripts/test-native.ps1 -Worker build/azahar-integration-native/bin/Release/ctr-worker.exe -Fixture ../t03.3dsx
    ```
    
    Current checks and acceptance gaps: [25](25-wave-status.md). Interfaces and
    primary source paths: [18](18-control-pipes.md), [21](21-native-control.md),
    [22](22-scenario-runner.md), [23](23-local-mcp.md), [24](24-desktop.md).
    The original FFI structs remain scaffold types; the implemented IPC is bounded
    JSON control plus file-ring BGRA frames. Neither implies hardware accuracy.
    
    Portable Windows packages and tagged GitHub releases:
    [26](26-portable-release.md). Optimized GPUI builds additionally require the
    pinned Microsoft FXC shader compiler; the portable runtime does not.
    # T03: inherited private control pipes
    
    Status: **verified compiled** on Windows GNU; process acceptance tests executed.
    No Azahar emulation is advertised by this spike. Source baseline:
    `11eceda5e0e682a1f44e396bf954a1b9137097ca`; no native files changed.
    This records the original T03 spike. The implemented native extension and current
    containment behavior are in [21](21-native-control.md).
    
    ## Decision
    
    The supervisor creates the worker with inherited stdin/stdout pipe ends. There
    is no socket name to guess, public listener, or reconnect operation. Possession
    of the inherited handles is the capability. This implements the local-pipe
    option without introducing a discoverable named-pipe server. A later attach
    feature must add explicit OS access control and secure authentication.
    
    Each message is a four-byte little-endian unsigned byte count followed by UTF-8
    JSON. The count must be in 1..=65536 before allocation. Schema:
    `specs/control-v1.schema.json`; executable types: `protocol::control`.
    The existing fixed C ABI structs are unchanged. The larger protocol draft is
    still proposed; the delivered native subset is documented in [21](21-native-control.md).
    
    The connection starts with hello, session identity and epoch 1; status and stop
    follow. Replies echo identity, request number and epoch. Unknown fields/methods,
    incompatible versions, malformed/truncated/oversized frames and unexpected
    reply identities are rejected. A mutable client owns the single outstanding
    exchange. Deadlines cover writes as well as reads. On transport failure or
    ambiguous timeout the child is killed/reaped; mutations are never retried.
    Stderr remains under the supplied private root. Clean stop requires both the
    completion reply and successful child exit.
    
    ## Reproduction
    
    ```powershell
    cargo test -p lotus-protocol -p lotus-session -p lotus-cli
    cargo build -p lotus-cli -p lotus-session
    .\target\debug\ctr-cli.exe mock .\target\debug\lotus-mock-worker.exe
    ```
    
    Tests cover clean exit and second launch, four simultaneous children, sibling
    failure, handshake crash/hang/stale epoch, crash after handshake and framing
    limits. The concurrent test exposed duplicate time-derived session UUIDs on
    Windows; an atomic counter now guarantees uniqueness within the process.
    Identifiers are not authentication secrets.
    
    ## Limits and rollback
    
    Linux/macOS are untested. The original T03 spike killed only the direct child;
    T09 has since added Windows descendant jobs, storage locks, native capabilities
    and emulation commands ([21](21-native-control.md)). The old scaffold
    WorkerProcess remains untouched. No guest output/performance claim applies;
    only host process/control behavior is exercised. Remove the CLI mock command
    and new modules to roll back without changing native behavior.
    # T02 native screen spike
    
    **Verified compiled**: Windows GNU, pinned GPUI
    `6b720973027999bae402df23d469026f4cced988`, Rust 1.98.1.
    Native Azahar baseline remains `11eceda5e0e682a1f44e396bf954a1b9137097ca`;
    this ticket does not link it or change native behavior.
    
    Run `cargo run -p lotus-desktop --bin lotus-screen-spike`.
    The separate executable continuously replaces eight native BGRA images for four
    synthetic sessions. It displays one session, changes selection every five host
    seconds and alternates 1x/1.5x display scale every twenty seconds. Hidden sessions
    have no image elements. Only the latest eight CPU images are retained; no native
    Vulkan interop or emulation claims are made. Arc is needed by GPUI's Render image
    source API. Source-inspected API: GPUI `assets.rs`, `RenderImage::new`, BGRA data.
    
    `cargo test -p lotus-desktop --lib` exercises native geometry, changing image
    contents, outside clicks, invalid transforms, four zoom levels, and physical
    coordinate inversion at 1.25x/2x DPI. These are simulated DPI tests, not evidence
    of two actual Windows display configurations. TouchTransform uses the actual
    bottom-image rectangle, excluding letterbox space, and never emits coordinates
    for outside presses.
    
    The process was launched for observation on this host. Initial samples were
    92,753,920 bytes working set / 66,912,256 private bytes / 872 handles; a later
    sample was 92,733,440 / 66,834,432 / 868. These are host resource observations,
    not guest timings or proof of visible presentation. Generation time is displayed
    in host microseconds. The computer-use tool rejected access to the executable;
    visual inspection and actual two-DPI interaction acceptance remain pending.
    At ten minutes (19:50:06-20:00:06 local, 2026-11-15), working set was
    93,011,968 bytes, private memory 66,850,816 bytes and handle count 868.
    CPU time was 332.8 host seconds. Live touch interaction and actual two-DPI
    presentation remain acceptance gaps. Existing .rsrc manifest linker warning remains visible.
    
    Visual and actual two-DPI interaction checks are deferred at the user's request
    to continue without Computer Use. Rollback: disable the separate spike executable;
    its geometry module is now also used by the native desktop. Linux/macOS remain untested.
    # Native branch worktrees and patch inventory
    
    Upstream base: `11eceda5e0e682a1f44e396bf954a1b9137097ca`.
    Local worktrees in the 3DS parent:
    
    | Source | Branch | Build cache | Purpose |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | azahar-stock | detached at upstream base | build/azahar-stock | unmodified core control |
    | azahar-integration | integration | build/azahar-integration-native | minimal native frontend |
    | azahar-experimental | experimental | build/azahar-experimental-native | future instrumentation |
    
    All three were created from the same base; no experimental model changes exist.
    The stock checkout stays detached and clean. Never use a branch name as a
    reproducible build input: the build script checks HEAD against config/pins.toml,
    rejects dirty sources and refuses caches configured for another source root.
    
    ## Matrix
    
    Windows GNU Release software-only is the initial tested configuration. Qt, SDL,
    Libretro, web service, scripting RPC, room servers, hardware graphics APIs and
    hardware audio sinks are off; software renderer is on; LTO and warnings-as-errors
    are off. GDB is compiled by upstream default but disabled in driver settings.
    The exact configuration is in build manifests and scripts/build-azahar.ps1.
    Linux/macOS, MSVC and accelerated renderers are untested. No hardware timing
    claim follows from the software baseline.
    
    Stock core: **verified compiled**. A standalone, bounded oracle driver is linked
    against the stock core via CMAKE_PROJECT_citra_INCLUDE; the source tree remains
    unchanged. Driver fallback applets are explicitly upstream compatibility mode,
    not a new implementation. This is not verification of the upstream Qt frontend.
    **Verified emulator**: the stock driver loaded the locally supplied `t03.3dsx`
    and presented 60 frames with load/run result 0 on 2026-11-15. Firmware was not
    needed in this HLE configuration. The first driver attempt exposed a missing
    frontend initialization of `Settings::values.lle_modules`; initializing every
    entry in `Service::service_module_map` to HLE resolved it without changing core.
    Differential image acceptance is recorded separately.

    | Ticket | Files | Rationale | Acceptance | Removal |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | T04 | root CMakeLists, src/CMakeLists, src/ctr_worker | opt-in process frontend | native link/probe, OFF remains stock | remove if upstream supplies equivalent target |

    ## Final differential and storage checks
    
    **Verified emulator**, final pin above, Release flags from the matrix. The fork
    also builds with `ENABLE_CTR_WORKER=OFF`: its oracle driver booted 60 frames and
    matched stock exactly. Using the same ordinary absolute `t03.3dsx` path in both

    # Native sessions, frames and containment
    
    LOTUS is the application. The upstream-tracking `integration` branch supplies
    the **AZAHAR** backend. The `experimental` branch supplies **CITnLO**, based on
    integration. The eventual replacement backend is **LOTUS**. These names do not
    change the existing wire protocol or executable names.
    
    The native frontend uses software rendering, Old 3DS, fixed initial ticks 0,
    fixed time 2000-01-01 UTC, HLE services/DSP and a muted audio sink. It never opens
    Qt/SDL windows. Unsupported keyboard/Mii callbacks pause with an explicit
    `unsupported_applet` reason. This does not implement arbitrary firmware applets.
    
    ## Implemented protocol
    
    The length-prefixed private pipe transport from document 18 now accepts `params`
    and returns `data`. Version remains 1.0; these are additive fields. The native
    backend identifier is `azahar_native_software`. Only one mutable Rust owner sends
    commands. IDs increase and are never retried after a transport failure.
    
    | Method | Parameters | Completion |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | hello/status | none | state, source SHA, presented frames, input/audio statistics |
    | load | path, local `.3dsx` | loaded and paused, epoch incremented, or typed error |
    | run | frames 1-600 | started; automatically pauses at budget or 20 host seconds |
    | run_until | frames 1-600 | paused after advancing, or explicit error/deadline |
    | pause | none | outer RunLoop returned; no nested teardown |
    | reset | none | same content reloaded, paused, epoch incremented |
    | capture | none | two native screen leases copied from latest software output |
    | input | owner live/scenario, buttons, x/y, touch | complete input state installed |
    | registers | core 0-3, also checked against active core count | 16 registers/CPSR at safe point |
    | read_memory | address u32, length 1-4096 | mapped current-process bytes at safe point |
    | stop | none | core shut down, then process exit required by supervisor |
    
    Queue capacity is 16 messages of at most 64 KiB. Only the reader thread touches
    the queue; all emulated state stays on the emulation thread. The existing
    `NotifyPendingWork` event wakes the frame limiter. The optional frontend callback
    in `ProcessPendingWork` services status/register/memory inspection there.
    Load/reset/stop and capture run outside nested RunLoop calls. No selected-core
    single-step precision is claimed.
    
    ## Ownership and budgets
    
    Frames use three reusable file slots per screen under the private root. Each
    has a 32-byte little-endian header: `LTRF`, version u32, epoch u64, sequence u64,
    width u32, height u32; then native BGRA8 pixels in top-left row order. Metadata
    also includes byte length, stride, slot and orientation. Rust validates all
    fields, bounds allocation, checks the header and returns owned pixels before
    another capture. There is no wait for UI acknowledgement. Old slot sequences,
    load/reset epochs and stopped/crashed sessions invalidate leases. Total pixel slot
    storage is bounded to 2,073,600 bytes plus six headers.
    
    Input factories expose one complete state to HID. Scenario ownership excludes
    live input until reload/reset. Sending all-zero state releases keys/touch after
    device disconnect. This version has no host audio device: the DSP submits to a
    16,384-stereo-sample muted ring, drops oldest samples on overflow, and reports
    sample/drop counts and FNV-1a checksum. Status drains the ring. The checksum is
    an emulator diagnostic, not an audio quality/hardware claim.
    
    On Windows, the supervisor starts the child suspended, assigns a kill-on-close
    job, then resumes its initial thread. Descendants inherit containment. Each
    root has an OS file lock held through process lifetime. Crashes retain stderr
    and native logs, invalidate leases, terminate the job and release the lock.
    Non-Windows builds currently retain direct-child termination only; descendant
    containment there is unimplemented and untested.
    
    ## Reproducible checks
    
    `cargo test -p lotus-session` includes five real mock process tests, including
    descendant termination and same-root exclusion. Native tests are opt-in, never
    silently counted as passing without assets:
    
    ```powershell
    $env:LOTUS_NATIVE_WORKER = (Resolve-Path build/azahar-integration-native/bin/Release/ctr-worker.exe).Path
    $env:LOTUS_FIXTURE = (Resolve-Path ../t03.3dsx).Path
    cargo test -p lotus-session --test native_process -- --ignored --nocapture
    ```

    workers, forced sibling failure, fifth-worker rejection and scoped artifacts
    retained after stop. Guest SD-write isolation is recorded in [20](20-native-baseline.md);
    save-game correctness for every title remains untested.
    No firmware was needed by this fixture; the supplied DSP dump remains external.
    Hardware verification: none. Other platforms/accelerated renderers: untested.

        /// Spawn a worker for `kind`, optionally loading approved content paused.
        pub async fn create(
            &self,
            kind: SessionKind,
            asset: Option<&str>,
            actor: Actor,
        ) -> io::Result<SessionInfo> {
            self.require_control()?;
            let content = asset.map(|handle| self.resolve_asset(handle)).transpose()?;
            let id = SessionUuid::generate().to_string();
            let reservation = self.reserve(&id, &kind)?;
            let root = match &kind {
                SessionKind::Primary { card } => self.cards.primary_root(card)?,
                SessionKind::Secondary { parent } => {
                    self.cards.create_scratch(&id, parent.as_deref())?
                }
            };
            let started = async {
                let mut native = NativeSession::spawn(&self.config.worker, &root).await?;
                if let Some(content) = &content {
                    if let Err(error) = native.load(content).await {
                        let _ = native.stop().await;
                        return Err(error);
                    }
                }
                Ok(native)
            }
            .await;
            let native = match started {
                Ok(native) => native,
                Err(error) => {
                    if matches!(kind, SessionKind::Secondary { .. }) {
                        let _ = self.cards.discard_scratch(&root, ScratchEnd::Abnormal);
                    }
                    return Err(error);
                }
            };
            let info = SessionInfo {
                id: id.clone(),
                kind,
                asset: asset.map(str::to_string),
                created_unix_ms: unix_ms(),
            };
            let mut telemetry = Telemetry::new();
            telemetry.state = native.state();
            telemetry.epoch = native.epoch();
            telemetry.pid = native.pid();
            telemetry.record(actor, "create");
            let handle = Arc::new(SessionHandle {
                info: Mutex::new(info.clone()),
                root,
                native: tokio::sync::Mutex::new(native),
                telemetry: Mutex::new(telemetry),
                playing: AtomicBool::new(false),
            });
            reservation.commit(handle);
            Ok(info)
        }
    
        /// Load approved content, replacing what was loaded. Leaves the session paused.
        pub async fn load(&self, id: &str, asset: &str, actor: Actor) -> io::Result<SessionInfo> {
            self.require_control()?;
            let content = self.resolve_asset(asset)?;
            let handle = self.handle(id)?;
            handle.set_playing(false);
            let mut native = handle.native.lock().await;
            pause_if_running(&mut native).await?;
            native.load(&content).await?;
            lock(&handle.info).asset = Some(asset.to_string());
            handle.record(actor, "load");
            Ok(handle.info())
        }
    
        /// Run continuously: the pump re-issues bounded runs until paused.
        pub async fn run(&self, id: &str, actor: Actor) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.require_control()?;
            let handle = self.handle(id)?;
            if handle.info().asset.is_none() {
                return Err(io::Error::other("load content before running"));
            }
            let mut native = handle.native.lock().await;
            if native.state() == SessionState::Paused {
                native.run().await?;
            }
            handle.set_playing(true);
            handle.record(actor, "run");
            Ok(())
        }

            self.require_control()?;
            let handle = self.handle(id)?;
            handle.set_playing(false);
            let mut native = handle.native.lock().await;
            handle.record(actor, "pause");
            native.pause().await
        }

        /// End a session. Secondary guest data is deleted; primary data persists.
        pub async fn stop(&self, id: &str, actor: Actor) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.require_control()?;
            let handle = {
                let mut registry = lock(&self.registry);
                let handle = registry
                    .sessions
                    .remove(id)
                    .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("unknown session"))?;
                registry.mounted.retain(|_, owner| owner != id);
                handle
            };
            handle.set_playing(false);
            handle.record(actor, "stop");
            let mut native = handle.native.lock().await;
            let result = if native.state().is_active() {
                native.stop().await
            } else {
                Ok(())
            };
            let end = if result.is_ok() && native.state() == SessionState::Stopped {
                ScratchEnd::Clean
            } else {
                ScratchEnd::Abnormal
            };
            drop(native);
            if matches!(lock(&handle.info).kind, SessionKind::Secondary { .. }) {
                self.cards.discard_scratch(&handle.root, end)?;
            }
            result
        }
    
        /// Failure injection and emergency termination, limited to this session's job.
        pub async fn abort(&self, id: &str, actor: Actor) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.require_control()?;
            let handle = self.handle(id)?;
            handle.set_playing(false);
            handle.record(actor, "abort");
            handle.native.lock().await.abort().await;
            Ok(())
        }

    //!
    //! All exchanges are serialized by mutable ownership. A failed or timed-out
    //! exchange destroys the connection: a possibly committed request is never retried.
    use std::fs::{self, File};
    use std::io;
    
    use std::process::Stdio;
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use lotus_protocol::control::{self, Method, Reply, Request, Status};

    /// Owns the child and its unshared pipe ends. Drop kills the direct child.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct ControlledWorker {
        child: Child,
        input: ChildStdin,
        output: ChildStdout,
        session: String,
        next_request: u64,
        epoch: u64,
        state: SessionState,
        timeout: Duration,
        root_lock: Option<File>,
        #[cfg(windows)]
        job: Option<crate::process_job::ProcessJob>,
    }
    
    impl ControlledWorker {
        /// Launch, retain stderr locally, and complete a bounded handshake.
        pub async fn spawn(spec: &WorkerSpec, timeout: Duration) -> io::Result<Self> {
            if timeout.is_zero() || timeout > Duration::from_secs(30) {
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                    "timeout must be in (0, 30s]",
                ));
            }
            fs::create_dir_all(&spec.storage_root)?;
            let root_lock = File::options()
                .create(true)
                .truncate(false)
                .read(true)
                .write(true)
                .open(spec.storage_root.join("worker.lock"))?;
            root_lock.try_lock().map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            let stderr = File::create(spec.storage_root.join("worker.stderr.log"))?;
            let mut command = Command::new(&spec.executable);
            command
                .args(&spec.args)
                .envs(spec.env.iter().cloned())
                .env("LOTUS_STORAGE_ROOT", &spec.storage_root)
                .stdin(Stdio::piped())
                .stdout(Stdio::piped())
                .stderr(stderr)
                .kill_on_drop(true);
            #[cfg(windows)]
            command.creation_flags(0x0800_0004);
            let mut child = command.spawn()?;
            #[cfg(windows)]
            let job = match crate::process_job::ProcessJob::attach_and_resume(
                child.id().expect("new child has PID"),
            ) {
                Ok(job) => job,
                Err(error) => {
                    let _ = child.kill().await;
                    return Err(error);
                }
            };
            let input = child
                .stdin
                .take()
                .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("missing child stdin"))?;
            let output = child
                .stdout
                .take()
                .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("missing child stdout"))?;
            let mut worker = Self {
                child,
                input,
                output,
                session: SessionUuid::generate().to_string(),
                next_request: 1,
                epoch: 1,
                state: SessionState::Created,
                timeout,
                root_lock: Some(root_lock),
                #[cfg(windows)]
                job: Some(job),
            };
            worker.request(Method::Hello).await?;
            worker.state = SessionState::Idle;
            Ok(worker)
        }

        #[must_use]
        pub fn state(&self) -> SessionState {
            self.state
        }
    
        #[must_use]
        pub fn epoch(&self) -> u64 {
            self.epoch
        }
    
        /// Child OS identifier, absent after reaping.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn pid(&self) -> Option<u32> {
            self.child.id()
        }
    
        /// Child working set in bytes, absent after reaping or on unsupported hosts.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn working_set(&self) -> Option<u64> {
            crate::process_memory::working_set(&self.child)
        }
    
        /// Query the worker without any GUI dependencies.
        pub async fn status(&mut self) -> io::Result<Reply> {
            self.request(Method::Status).await
        }
    
        /// Complete shutdown and reap; kill on any failed exchange or exit deadline.
        pub async fn stop(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.request(Method::Stop).await?;
            match tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, self.child.wait()).await {
                Ok(Ok(status)) if status.success() => {
                    self.state = SessionState::Stopped;
                    self.release_resources();
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => {
                    self.fail().await;
                    Err(io::Error::other("worker failed to exit cleanly"))
                }
            }
        }
    
        async fn fail(&mut self) {
            self.state = SessionState::Crashed;
            let _ = self.child.kill().await;
            let _ = self.child.wait().await;
            self.release_resources();
        }
    
        /// Terminate this worker and its contained descendants; retain logs.
        pub async fn abort(&mut self) {
            self.fail().await;
        }
    
        fn release_resources(&mut self) {
            #[cfg(windows)]
            {
                self.job.take();
            }
            self.root_lock.take();
        }
    
        pub async fn command(
            &mut self,
            method: Method,
            params: serde_json::Value,
        ) -> io::Result<Reply> {
            if matches!(self.state, SessionState::Stopped | SessionState::Crashed) {
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe,
                    "worker is no longer active",
                ));
            }
            let request = Request {
                version_major: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAJOR,
                version_minor: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MINOR,
                request_id: self.next_request,
                session: self.session.clone(),
                epoch: self.epoch,
                method,
                params,
            };
            self.next_request = self
                .next_request
                .checked_add(1)
                .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("request ID exhausted"))?;
            let result = tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, self.exchange(&request)).await;
            let reply = match result {
                Ok(Ok(reply)) => reply,
                Ok(Err(error)) => {
                    self.fail().await;
                    return Err(error);
                }
                Err(_) => {
                    self.fail().await;
                    return Err(io::Error::new(
                        io::ErrorKind::TimedOut,
                        "worker exchange deadline exceeded; result unknown",
                    ));
                }
            };
            if !lotus_protocol::is_compatible(reply.version_major, reply.version_minor)
                || reply.request_id != request.request_id
                || reply.session != self.session
                || reply.epoch
                    != self.epoch
                        + u64::from(
                            matches!(method, Method::Load | Method::Reset)
                                && reply.status == Status::Ok,
                        )
                || !matches!(
                    reply.state.as_str(),
                    "idle" | "running" | "paused" | "stopped"
                )
            {
                self.fail().await;
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
                    "invalid worker reply identity, epoch, status or state",
                ));
            }
            self.epoch = reply.epoch;
            self.state = match reply.state.as_str() {
                "running" => SessionState::Running,
                "paused" => SessionState::Paused,
                "stopped" => SessionState::Stopped,
                _ => SessionState::Idle,
            };
            Ok(reply)
        }
    
        async fn request(&mut self, method: Method) -> io::Result<Reply> {
            let reply = self.command(method, serde_json::Value::Null).await?;
            if reply.status != Status::Ok {
                return Err(io::Error::other(format!(
                    "worker rejected {method:?}: {:?}",
                    reply.status
                )));
            }
            Ok(reply)
        }
    
        async fn exchange(&mut self, request: &Request) -> io::Result<Reply> {
            self.input.write_all(&control::encode(request)?).await?;
            self.input.flush().await?;
            let length = self.output.read_u32_le().await?;
            control::validate_length(length)?;
            let mut payload = vec![0; length as usize];
            self.output.read_exact(&mut payload).await?;
            serde_json::from_slice(&payload).map_err(io::Error::other)
        }
    }
    
    impl Drop for ControlledWorker {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = self.child.start_kill();
            self.release_resources();
        }
    }

        let payload = serde_json::to_vec(value).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
        let length = u32::try_from(payload.len()).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
        validate_length(length)?;
        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(payload.len() + 4);
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&length.to_le_bytes());
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&payload);
        Ok(bytes)
    }

    Each run creates a fresh root. Inputs apply before the frame following their
    checkpoint; `press` releases one frame later. Touch uses native coordinates.
    Runs split at input/capture boundaries and advance at most 60 frames per request.
    Native requests have a 20-host-second deadline; each scenario also has its wall
    deadline. Limits: 100,000 frames, one hour, 4,096 input entries, 64 captures.
    Final native screens are always captured, bounding retained pixels below 45 MB
    per run. These limits describe host resources, not hardware cycles.
    
    `report.json` records source SHA, worker/content SHA-256, frame checkpoints,
    native BGRA8 hashes and host elapsed time. Failures retain `failure.json` and
    worker logs. Shutdown is attempted on all paths; the process job is the fallback.
    Repeat mode accepts 1-10 runs and rejects differing pixel hashes, retaining
    individual reports for investigation.

    # Local MCP adapter
    
    `lotus-mcp [host-config.json]` serves stdio only (headless). `lotus-desktop
    --mcp host-config.json` serves the same tools from the window over the same
    sessions; session kinds, cards and the full tool list are in
    [30](30-sessions-and-interface.md). Without configuration it can
    report status but cannot spawn workers or read files. Host configuration fixes
    the executable, root, approved asset handles and control permission:
    
    ```json
    {
      "worker": "C:/path/to/ctr-worker.exe",
      "storage_root": "C:/path/to/private-runs",
      "assets": {"demo": "C:/path/to/demo.3dsx"},
      "allow_control": true,
      "asset_directories": {"builds": "C:/path/to/build-output"},
      "max_sessions": 4
    }
    ```
    
    The last two fields are optional (defaults: none, 4; limit 16).
    
    Configuration is trusted local startup input, never a tool parameter. Each
    server process owns its sessions and artifact catalog. Client tools cannot
    select executables, roots or arbitrary content paths. Controls require
    `allow_control`; status/memory/capture operate only on owned sessions.
    `max_sessions` workers and 128 screen artifacts (at most 49,152,000 bytes)
    bound resources. On client disconnect every session is stopped.
    
    Tools: status/list (sessions, cards), create (primary/secondary), load an
    approved asset, run/run_until, pause/reset/stop, input, session status with
    gauges, registers, bounded mapped-memory reads, capture and focus. Scenario
    validation accepts only a handle registered by the embedding host; the standalone
    server currently registers none. Captures return `lotus://artifact/...` links.
    `resources/list` and `resources/read` expose only catalogued captures; read checks
    size/hash. No shell, arbitrary filesystem, network listener or Azahar UDP RPC.
    
    **Verified emulator**: the opt-in `native_parity` test compares MCP screen bytes
    with the shared native API at frame 60, and checks read-only permission, asset,
    session and resource restrictions. Windows GNU AZAHAR at native pin
    `05773bbb5380bc5094fcd8eacf189fdc5d6360bb`; the same acceptance passed on CITnLO.
    `tests/test_mcp_native.py` additionally exercises actual stdio initialization,
    tool calls, resource listing/reading and shutdown. No hardware verification.
    
    Source: `mcp::{server,tool_arguments}`, `session::{supervisor,native_session}`.
    MCP framing/types follow pinned `rmcp 3.10.0` source in Cargo.lock. Windows path
    normalization converts Rust verbatim canonical paths for MinGW std::filesystem;
    native manifest/logs remain in each private root. Rollback: launch without host
    configuration or set `allow_control` false.
    # LOTUS desktop
    
    The GPUI window renders snapshots and sends commands; it never touches a
    worker. Session model, layout, gauges and the shared MCP surface are in
    [30](30-sessions-and-interface.md); this document covers the plumbing.
    
    `desktop_controller` owns the shared `Supervisor` ([30](30-sessions-and-interface.md))
    on a background Tokio runtime. UI commands have a 32-entry bound and each runs
    as its own task, so a slow worker never stalls another session. Complete input
    states coalesce separately (8 ms flush), so key/touch releases never depend on
    command-queue space. Only the selected session is previewed; the latest screen
    pair replaces the previous one, and replaced images are dropped from GPUI's
    sprite atlas. There is no frame history. With `--mcp` the same runtime serves
    MCP on stdio over the same supervisor.
    
    Launch: `lotus-desktop [--mcp] host.json` ([23](23-local-mcp.md) host config).
    Without a configuration the window explains how to start one. Desktop loads
    start running; MCP loads stay paused. Click/drag the bottom screen for touch;
    focus loss, deactivation, selection and layout changes release input. Touch maps
    through the bottom image's actual layout rectangle; simulated 1.25x/2x DPI
    inversion tests cover native corners (`screen_geometry`).
    
    Worker failures clear displayed pixels and show a crashed state; other workers
    continue in their processes. Closing the window stops every session (3 s
    deadline each, job termination as fallback), discarding secondary data; an
    already pending native exchange can take up to its 30 s deadline.
    
    **Verified emulator**: `native_controller` (primary/secondary, concurrency,
    crash isolation, shared MCP, persistence; see [30](30-sessions-and-interface.md)).
    **Checked by screenshot** (Windows 11, one 100%-scale display, debug build,
    2026-11-16): native frames render; keyboard (Ctrl+I) and mouse (menu, collapse,
    rail selection, Step, Inspect, session rows) reach the window; working set held
    at ~96.6 MB over 20 s of continuous preview replacement. Actual two-DPI
    interaction, host audio and other platforms remain unverified.
    
    Source: `desktop::{desktop_controller, lotus_window, session_tree, gauges,
    theme, screen_geometry}`, `session::supervisor`. Primary GPUI APIs at its pinned
    source: `elements/{img,canvas,div}.rs`, `assets.rs` (`RenderImage` BGRA),
    `app.rs` (`drop_image`, `prompt_for_paths`), `app/context.rs` (activation/focus).
    Rollback: run headless (`lotus-mcp`, `ctr-cli`); no GUI is required.
    # Portable Windows release
    
    `LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64.zip` contains the desktop, CLI, MCP server and separate
    AZAHAR/CITnLO runtimes. Extract it into a writable folder. `LOTUS.cmd` selects
    homebrew using a Windows file dialog and launches CITnLO; `LOTUS-AZAHAR.cmd`
    selects AZAHAR. Both recreate absolute host configuration from the installation
    location, retaining sessions under `data/<backend>/sessions`. No installer,
    registry changes or developer tools are required. Windows 11 x64 / Direct3D 11
    is the initial target. The binaries are unsigned.
    
    **Verified compiled**, Windows GNU: optimized Rust applications and both native
    runtimes. **Verified emulator**: native evidence in [25](25-wave-status.md).
    Local release-profile workspace tests and portable ZIP relocation/startup tests
    passed, including Windows PowerShell 5.1 launcher configuration for both backends.
    
    The packager reads AMD64 PE imports, copies non-system DLLs recursively, and
    rejects missing dependencies or MSYS runtime dependencies. Windows system/API-set
    DLLs stay supplied by Windows. All payload files have SHA-256 entries in
    `release-manifest.json`; the release also supplies ZIP checksums, notices and a
    recursive LOTUS/native source ZIP. Guest assets and instance directories are
    excluded. Only the three production Rust executables are shipped.
    
    Build from a recursive Git checkout of the release tag. `scripts/setup-build-tools.py`
    downloads hash-verified WinLibs GCC 16.2.0 r2 (including CMake/Ninja) and Windows
    SDK 10.0.28000.2705 shader tools into a private build directory. Add
    `<tools>/winlibs/mingw64/bin` to PATH and set `GPUI_FXC_PATH` to
    `<tools>/sdk/c/bin/10.0.28000.0/x64/fxc.exe`. GPUI's pinned
    `crates/gpui_windows/build.rs` requires FXC for optimized shader compilation.
    The SDK is a build dependency, not part of the runtime ZIP.
    
    The exact build, staging and packaging commands are in
    [windows.yml](../.github/workflows/windows.yml). CI runs on pushes to main,
    pull requests, tags and manual dispatch: Rust formatting/Clippy/release tests;
    independent pinned native builds; native framing/self-tests; package assembly;
    relocation to a path containing spaces with a Windows-only PATH; DLL/hash,
    launcher, CLI, MCP and native startup checks. No supplied private fixture runs
    on GitHub. Tag `v<version>` must match Cargo's workspace version and publishes
    only after all build and package jobs pass. Actions and build-tool downloads are
    pinned; per-runtime manifests record source/flags/compiler. GitHub's Windows
    runner image is maintained externally, so byte-identical rebuilds are not promised.
    Manual dispatch with `publish_release=true` instead creates the version tag and
    release from the tested workflow SHA after the same checks. It never overwrites
    an existing release. Only the release job receives repository write permission.
    For packaging-only recovery, `reuse_build_run` accepts a completed main run whose
    Rust and both native build jobs passed. CI rejects changed binary inputs and
    cross-repository/PR builds, then reruns package tests against those immutable
    artifacts. Compiler flags and source pins remain recorded in the reused manifests.
    
    Local native fixture results and stock comparisons remain in
    [25](25-wave-status.md). Visible GPUI/input and actual two-DPI checks are still
    deferred at the user's instruction. Audio playback and hardware accuracy are not
    claimed. Rollback is extracting an earlier ZIP; preserve `data/` when upgrading.
    
    Corresponding source: the tag's LOTUS tree, pinned fork commits and recursive
    submodules, plus Cargo.lock's exact Rust sources. The source ZIP excludes Git
    metadata; use `git clone --branch v0.0.1 --recurse-submodules
    https://github.com/estyseesghosts/lotus.git` for the Git-based build scripts.
    # Build, test, package and release (Windows x64)
    
    Authoritative commands. CI ([windows.yml](../.github/workflows/windows.yml)) runs
    the same steps; **verified compiled** there (run 43795955719, 2026-11-16). The
    local-checkout variant below differs only in paths. MSVC, Linux and macOS are
    untested. Rationale and release contents: [26](26-portable-release.md).
    
    ## 0. Just run it
    
    Extract `LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64.zip` from the GitHub release into a writable
    folder (spaces are fine). Run `LOTUS.cmd` (CITnLO) or `LOTUS-AZAHAR.cmd`; pick
    your own `.3dsx`. No installer, registry or toolchain. Data stays in `data/`;
    keep it when upgrading. Verify the download against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Binaries
    are unsigned, so SmartScreen may warn.
    
    ## 1. Prerequisites
    
    | Tool | Version | Notes |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Windows | 11 x64 | Direct3D 11 |
    | Git | any recent | submodule support |
    | Python | 3.11+ (CI: 3.14) | `tomllib`, `hashlib.file_digest` |
    | rustup | any | installs the pin in `rust-toolchain.toml` (`1.98.1-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`) automatically |
    | `gh` | optional | CI dispatch and logs |
    
    GCC, CMake, Ninja and the FXC shader compiler are **not** taken from the system.
    The next step downloads hash-verified copies into a private directory.
    
    ## 2. Checkout and tools
    
    ```powershell
    git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/estyseesghosts/lotus.git
    cd lotus
    python scripts/setup-build-tools.py build/tools    # WinLibs GCC 16.2.0 r2 (+CMake/Ninja), SDK 10.0.28000.2705 fxc
    $env:PATH = "$PWD\build\tools\winlibs\mingw64\bin;$env:PATH"
    $env:GPUI_FXC_PATH = "$PWD\build\tools\sdk\c\bin\10.0.28000.0\x64\fxc.exe"
    scripts/bootstrap.ps1      # pinned toolchain, submodules, Cargo fetch, pin check (idempotent)
    ```
    
    Do this in every new shell: PATH and `GPUI_FXC_PATH` are not persisted. The
    submodule fetch is large. Without FXC, GPUI's `build.rs` fails in `--release`.
    Pins: `config/pins.toml`; check with `scripts/verify-pins.ps1`.
    
    ## 3. Rust (desktop, CLI, MCP)
    
    ```powershell
    scripts/smoke.ps1                                   # fast: build, tests, fmt, clippy, CLI, pins; no ROM/GPU/display
    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo build --locked --release --bins               # target/release: lotus-desktop, ctr-cli, lotus-mcp
    cargo test --locked --release --workspace
    ```
    
    Always pass `--locked`. Native tests are `#[ignore]` by default; an ignored run
    is not a pass (see 5).
    
    Run headless with `lotus-mcp host.json`, windowed with `lotus-desktop host.json`,
    or windowed and agent-driven with `lotus-desktop --mcp host.json` (host config:
    [23](23-local-mcp.md); sessions: [30](30-sessions-and-interface.md)).
    
    ## 4. Native runtimes (AZAHAR and CITnLO)
    
    `build-azahar.ps1` refuses a source whose `HEAD` differs from `config/pins.toml`
    or that is dirty, and refuses a CMake cache configured for another source root.
    Use **one source checkout and one build directory per branch**; never share a
    cache. Mirror CI so the `vendor/azahar` submodule stays untouched:
    
    ```powershell
    Import-Module ./scripts/Pins.psm1
    $pins = Read-Pins config/pins.toml
    foreach ($branch in 'integration','experimental') {
        $src = "build/native-source-$branch"; $out = "build/native-$branch"
        git clone --no-checkout $pins['azahar']['fork'] $src
        git -C $src checkout --detach $pins['azahar']["${branch}_commit"]
        git -C $src submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1
        ./scripts/build-azahar.ps1 -Branch $branch -AzaharRoot $src -BuildDirectory $out -Parallel 2
        & "./$out/bin/Release/ctr-worker.exe" --self-test
        python tests/test_native_protocol.py "$out/bin/Release/ctr-worker.exe"
    }
    ```
    
    `integration` is AZAHAR, `experimental` is CITnLO. At the v0.0.1 pins both point
    to the same commit, so they differ only by `-DCTR_BACKEND_NAME`. Flags (software
    renderer, Qt/SDL/Libretro/Vulkan/OpenGL off, LTO off) are fixed in the script and
    recorded in `lotus-build-manifest.json`. First clean build: about 35-45 min on a
    GitHub runner. `-Branch stock -Oracle` builds the unmodified-core oracle used for
    screen comparison ([20](20-native-baseline.md)).
    
    ## 5. Native acceptance (needs your own homebrew)
    
    ```powershell
    scripts/test-native.ps1 -Worker build/native-integration/bin/Release/ctr-worker.exe -Fixture C:\abs\path\t03.3dsx
    python tests/test_mcp_native.py <lotus-mcp.exe> <host-config> <asset-handle>   # see 21/23
    python tests/test_windowed_mcp.py <lotus-desktop.exe> <host-config> <asset-handle> [hold-seconds]   # see 30
    ```
    
    Use absolute fixture paths. When comparing against stock, use the *same* absolute
    path in both; launch-path changes the pixels ([20](20-native-baseline.md)). No
    ROMs, firmware or captures are committed or uploaded.
    
    ## 6. Portable ZIP
    
    ```powershell
    python scripts/package-windows.py rust --binary-dir target/release --metadata build/metadata.json --output build/rust-artifact --dll-dir build/tools/winlibs/mingw64/bin
    python scripts/package-windows.py runtime --build build/native-integration --output build/azahar-artifact --dll-dir build/tools/winlibs/mingw64/bin
    python scripts/package-windows.py runtime --build build/native-experimental --output build/citnlo-artifact --dll-dir build/tools/winlibs/mingw64/bin
    python scripts/package-windows.py assemble --rust build/rust-artifact --azahar build/azahar-artifact --citnlo build/citnlo-artifact --output build/dist --version 0.0.1
    python tests/test_portable.py build/dist/LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64.zip
    python scripts/archive-source.py build/dist/LOTUS-v0.0.1-source.zip
    ```
    
    `build/metadata.json` is `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 --filter-platform x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`.
    `assemble` fails on unresolved non-system DLLs or MSYS runtime imports.
    `test_portable.py` relocates the ZIP to a path with spaces, with a Windows-only
    PATH, and checks hashes, DLL closure, launchers, CLI, MCP and native startup.
    `--version` must equal the workspace version in `Cargo.toml`.
    
    ## 7. CI and release
    
    Workflow `Windows portable`: jobs `rust`, `native (integration|experimental)`
    (parallel, 90 min cap), then `package`, then `release`.
    
    | Trigger | Effect |
    | --- | --- |
    | push to `main`, PR | build and test; no release |
    | tag `v*` | full run, then release from the tag; tag must equal `v<Cargo version>` |
    | manual dispatch, `publish_release=true` | full run, then creates tag and release `v<Cargo version>` at the tested SHA |
    
    ```powershell
    gh workflow run windows.yml --ref main -f publish_release=true
    gh run watch <id> --exit-status
    gh release view v<version> --json assets
    ```
    
    A release is never overwritten; to redo one, bump the version or delete it by
    hand first. Only the `release` job has `contents: write`. A new push to a ref
    cancels its in-progress run (concurrency group); tag runs are not cancelled.
    
    **Packaging-only recovery** (no recompile, about 10 min): add
    `-f reuse_build_run=<run-id>` to the dispatch. `scripts/validate-build-reuse.py`
    requires that run to be a completed `windows.yml` run on `main` of this repo, with
    `rust` and both native jobs green, an ancestor of the current commit, and no
    changes outside `tests/test_portable.py`, the workflow, `scripts/package-windows.py`,
    `scripts/archive-source.py`, `scripts/validate-build-reuse.py`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`,
    `packaging/` and `docs/`. Anything else means rebuild. Artifacts expire after 7
    days, so a reuse run must be recent.
    
    ## 8. Troubleshooting
    
    | Symptom | Cause / fix |
    | --- | --- |
    | `GPUI_FXC_PATH`/shader error in `--release` | set it (2) |
    | `Source pin mismatch` / `Build inputs must be committed and clean` | checkout the pinned commit; do not edit the source tree |
    | `Cache belongs to a different source tree` | use a separate `-BuildDirectory` per source |
    | Missing/odd DLL at package time | build with the WinLibs GCC on PATH, not MSYS2 |
    | Worker fails to start on a `\\?\` path | already normalized by the session adapter; pass ordinary absolute paths |
    | Tests "pass" with nothing run | native tests are opt-in; use `scripts/test-native.ps1` |
    | Release job skipped after green `package` | fixed in `7f9dc3e`; `release` needs `always()` when build jobs are skipped |
    | Linker warning about duplicate manifest/resource | GPUI's, known and harmless on GNU |

    //! Real child-process acceptance, not an in-memory transport simulation.
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use lotus_session::controlled_worker::ControlledWorker;
    use lotus_session::{SessionState, WorkerSpec};
    
    fn spec(mode: &str) -> WorkerSpec {
        let id = lotus_protocol::envelope::SessionUuid::generate();
        WorkerSpec::new(
            env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_lotus-mock-worker"),
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lotus-control-{id}")),
        )
        .arg(mode)
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn handshake_query_clean_shutdown_and_second_launch() {
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let spec = spec("");
            let mut worker = ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_secs(3))
                .await
                .expect("mock handshake");
            let reply = worker.status().await.expect("status over pipes");
            assert_eq!(reply.backend, "mock");
            worker.stop().await.expect("graceful exit");
            assert_eq!(worker.state(), SessionState::Stopped);
            assert!(
                worker.status().await.is_err(),
                "stopped connection cannot be reused"
            );
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("remove test storage");
        }
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn failed_handshakes_are_reaped_and_logs_retained() {
        for mode in ["crash", "stale", "hang"] {
            let spec = spec(mode);
            assert!(
                ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_millis(500))
                    .await
                    .is_err(),
                "{mode} must fail"
            );
            assert!(spec.storage_root.join("worker.stderr.log").is_file());
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("child has released its files");
        }
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn four_private_connections_survive_a_sibling_failure() {
        let mut workers = Vec::new();
        let mut specs = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..4 {
            let spec = spec("");
            workers.push(
                ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_secs(3))
                    .await
                    .expect("spawn isolated child"),
            );
            specs.push(spec);
        }
        assert!(
            ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec("crash"), Duration::from_secs(3))
                .await
                .is_err()
        );
        for (mut worker, spec) in workers.into_iter().zip(specs) {
            worker.status().await.expect("sibling remains responsive");
            worker.stop().await.expect("sibling exits");
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("remove test storage");
        }
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn running_child_crash_transitions_to_crashed() {
        let spec = spec("crash_status");
        let mut worker = ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_secs(3))
            .await
            .expect("handshake before crash");
        assert!(worker.status().await.is_err());
        assert_eq!(worker.state(), SessionState::Crashed);
        assert!(
            worker.status().await.is_err(),
            "failed commands cannot be retried"
        );
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("reaped child releases log");
    }
