    class DelayGenerator {
    private:
        DelayGenerator() = default;
    
        // Average transfer speed based on measurements taken from real
        // hardware. 4 different modes have been taken into consideration:
        // RAM -> RAM, RAM -> VRAM, VRAM -> RAM and VRAM -> VRAM.
        // Furthermore, measurements are split into DMA transfers and tex
        // copies. For simplicity, we will assume fills are as fast as
        // texture copies.
    
        static constexpr double mibps_to_ns_per_byte(double mib_per_sec) {
            return 1'000'000'000.0 / (mib_per_sec * 1024.0 * 1024.0);
        }
    
        static constexpr std::array<std::array<double, 4>, 2> speed_mibps = {
            {{
                 190.0, // DMA RAMTORAM
                 310.0, // DMA RAMTOVRAM
                 380.0, // DMA VRAMTORAM
                 380.0, // DMA VRAMTOVRAM
             },
             {
                 450.0,  // TEX RAMTORAM
                 3100.0, // TEX RAMTOVRAM
                 5400.0, // TEX VRAMTORAM
                 5400.0, // TEX VRAMTOVRAM
             }}};
    
    public:
        enum class CopyMode {
            RAMTORAM,
            RAMTOVRAM,
            VRAMTORAM,
            VRAMTOVRAM,
        };
    
        static CopyMode GetCopyMode(bool input_vram, bool output_vram) {
            if (!input_vram && !output_vram) {
                return CopyMode::RAMTORAM;
            } else if (!input_vram && output_vram) {
                return CopyMode::RAMTOVRAM;
            } else if (input_vram && !output_vram) {
                return CopyMode::VRAMTORAM;
            } else {
                return CopyMode::VRAMTOVRAM;
            }
        }
    
        static u64 CalculateDelayNanoseconds(CopyMode mode, bool is_textre, size_t size) {
            double base_ns_per_byte =
                mibps_to_ns_per_byte(speed_mibps[is_textre][static_cast<u32>(mode)]);
    
            return static_cast<u64>(size * base_ns_per_byte);
        }
    };

            LOG_ERROR(Kernel, "No request is associated with the thread");

        auto& record = *record_map[thread_id];

        record.translated_reply_cmdbuf = std::move(translated_cmdbuf);
        InvokeCallbacks(record);
    
        record_map.erase(thread_id);

            // This is possible when the recorder is enabled after application started
            LOG_ERROR(Kernel, "No request is associated with the thread");
            return;
        }
    
        auto& record = *record_map[thread_id];
        record.status = RequestStatus::HLEUnimplemented;

    //! Owned ELF/DWARF data from an explicitly approved build artifact.
    use std::{collections::BTreeMap, io, sync::Arc};
    use object::{Object, ObjectSection, ObjectSymbol};
    use serde::Serialize;
    
    type Reader = gimli::EndianArcSlice<gimli::RunTimeEndian>;
    pub struct Symbols {
        context: addr2line::Context<Reader>,
        symbols: BTreeMap<u64, (String, u64)>,
    }
    #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
    pub struct Location {
        pub address: u32,
        pub symbol: Option<String>,
        pub offset: Option<u64>,
        pub file: Option<String>,
        pub line: Option<u32>,
        pub column: Option<u32>,
    }
    impl Symbols {
        pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Self> {
            if bytes.len() > 128 << 20 { return Err(io::Error::other("ELF exceeds 128 MiB")); }
            let file = object::File::parse(bytes).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            if file.format() != object::BinaryFormat::Elf || file.architecture() != object::Architecture::Arm || !file.is_little_endian() {
                return Err(io::Error::other("expected a little-endian ARM ELF build artifact"));
            }
            let dwarf = gimli::Dwarf::load(|section| -> io::Result<Reader> {
                let data = file.section_by_name(section.name()).map(|s| s.uncompressed_data())
                    .transpose().map_err(io::Error::other)?.unwrap_or_default();
                if data.len()>64<<20 { return Err(io::Error::other("DWARF section exceeds budget")); }
                Ok(Reader::new(Arc::from(data.as_ref()), gimli::RunTimeEndian::Little))
            })?;
            let context = addr2line::Context::from_dwarf(dwarf).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            let mut symbols = BTreeMap::new();
            for symbol in file.symbols().filter(|s| s.is_definition() && s.address()<=u64::from(u32::MAX)) {
                if let Ok(name) = symbol.name() {
                    if !name.is_empty() && !name.starts_with('$') {
                        symbols.insert(symbol.address() & !1, (name.to_string(), symbol.size()));
                    }
                }
            }
            Ok(Self { context, symbols })
        }
        pub fn locate(&self, address: u32) -> io::Result<Location> {
            let pc = u64::from(address & !1);
            let symbol = self.symbols.range(..=pc).next_back()
                .filter(|(base, (_,size))| *size == 0 || pc < **base+size);
            let location = self.context.find_location(pc).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            Ok(Location { address, symbol: symbol.map(|(_, (name,_))| name.clone()),
                offset: symbol.map(|(base,_)| pc-base),
                file: location.as_ref().and_then(|l| l.file.map(str::to_string)),
                line: location.as_ref().and_then(|l| l.line), column: location.and_then(|l| l.column) })
        }
        pub fn resolve(&self, query: &str) -> io::Result<Vec<u32>> {
            if query.is_empty() || query.len()>1024 { return Err(io::Error::other("invalid symbol query")); }
            if let Some((path,line)) = query.rsplit_once(':').filter(|(_,s)| s.parse::<u32>().is_ok()) {
                let line = line.parse::<u32>().map_err(io::Error::other)?;
                let mut result = Vec::new();
                for (address,_,location) in self.context.find_location_range(0,1u64<<32).map_err(io::Error::other)?.take(1_000_000) {
                    if location.line == Some(line) && location.file.is_some_and(|file| file.replace('\\',"/").ends_with(&path.replace('\\',"/"))) {
                        result.push(address as u32);
                        if result.len()==128 { break; }
                    }
                }
                return Ok(result);
            }
            Ok(self.symbols.iter().filter(|(_, (name,_))| name==query).take(128).map(|(address,_)| *address as u32).collect())
        }
        pub fn count(&self) -> usize { self.symbols.len() }
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
        #[test] fn rejects_non_elf_and_host_elf() {
            assert!(Symbols::parse(b"not an ELF").is_err());
            assert!(Symbols::parse(&[0;52]).is_err());
        }
    }

    //! Mock worker for process/transport acceptance; this never emulates a console.
    use std::io;
    
    use lotus_protocol::control::{self, Method, Reply, Request, Status};
    
    fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
        let mode = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_default();
        if mode == "descendant" {
            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60));
            return Ok(());
        }
        if mode == "spawn_descendant" {
            let mut command = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe()?);
            command.arg("descendant");
            #[cfg(windows)]
            {
                use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
                command.creation_flags(0x0800_0000);
            }
            let descendant = command.spawn()?;
            let root = std::env::var_os("LOTUS_STORAGE_ROOT").expect("supervisor supplies root");
            std::fs::write(
                std::path::Path::new(&root).join("descendant.pid"),
                descendant.id().to_string(),
            )?;
        }
        let mut input = io::stdin().lock();
        let mut output = io::stdout().lock();
        let mut identity: Option<String> = None;
        loop {
            let request: Request = control::read(&mut input)?;
            if mode == "crash" || (mode == "crash_status" && request.method == Method::Status) {
                std::process::exit(23);
            }
            if mode == "hang" {
                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60));
                continue;
            }
            let status = if !lotus_protocol::is_compatible(request.version_major, request.version_minor)
            {
                Status::Unsupported
            } else if request.session.len() != 32
                || !request.session.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit())
                || request.request_id == 0
            {
                Status::InvalidArgument
            } else if identity.as_ref().is_some_and(|id| id != &request.session) {
                Status::PermissionDenied
            } else if request.method != Method::Hello && identity.is_none() {
                Status::NotReady
            } else if request.epoch != 1 {
                Status::StaleEpoch
            } else if !matches!(
                request.method,
                Method::Hello | Method::Status | Method::Stop
            ) {
                Status::Unsupported
            } else {
                if request.method == Method::Hello {
                    identity = Some(request.session.clone());
                }
                Status::Ok
            };
            let stopped = status == Status::Ok && request.method == Method::Stop;
            let reply = Reply {
                version_major: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAJOR,
                version_minor: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MINOR,
                request_id: request.request_id,
                session: request.session,
                epoch: if mode == "stale" { 0 } else { 1 },
                status,
                state: if stopped { "stopped" } else { "idle" }.into(),
                backend: "mock".into(),
                data: serde_json::Value::Null,
            };
            control::write(&mut output, &reply)?;
            if stopped {
                return Ok(());
            }
        }
    }

            .await
            .expect("native handshake");
        assert!(
            NativeSession::spawn(&executable, &root).await.is_err(),

            .input(InputState::default(), "scenario")
            .await
            .expect("release buttons");

        assert_eq!(status["frames"], 60);

        assert_eq!(frames[0].bgra.len(), 400 * 240 * 4);
        assert_eq!(frames[1].bgra.len(), 320 * 240 * 4);
        let lease = frames[0].lease.clone();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            session.capture().await.expect("replace ring slots");
        }
        assert!(
            session.read_lease(&lease).is_err(),
            "slot sequence invalidates lease"
        );

        for _ in 0..10 {

            session
                .memory(pc, 4)
                .await
                .expect("mapped instruction memory");
            assert!(session.memory(pc, 4097).await.is_err(), "bounded read");
        }
        session.pause().await.expect("pause outside nested loop");
        let current = session.capture().await.expect("capture after pause");
        session.reset().await.expect("new epoch");
        assert!(
            session.read_lease(&current[0].lease).is_err(),
            "reset invalidates leases"
        );
        session.advance(2).await.expect("run after reset");
        let before_load = session.capture().await.expect("frame before reload");
        session.load(&fixture).await.expect("reload content");
        assert!(
            session.read_lease(&before_load[0].lease).is_err(),

    // Poll inherited stdin so stopping can join the reader without orphan threads.
    inline bool ReadExact(char* data, size_t size, const std::atomic_bool& stop) {
        while (size && !stop) {
    #ifdef _WIN32
            DWORD available = 0;
            const auto handle = GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE);
            if (!PeekNamedPipe(handle, nullptr, 0, nullptr, &available, nullptr))
                return false;
            if (!available) {
                std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
                continue;
            }
            DWORD received = 0;
            if (!ReadFile(handle, data, static_cast<DWORD>(std::min<size_t>(size, available)),
                          &received, nullptr) ||
                !received)
                return false;
    #else
            pollfd descriptor{STDIN_FILENO, POLLIN, 0};
            if (poll(&descriptor, 1, 10) <= 0)
                continue;
            const auto received = read(STDIN_FILENO, data, size);
            if (received <= 0)
                return false;
    #endif
            data += received;
            size -= received;
        }
        return size == 0;
    }
    inline bool Receive(nlohmann::json& request, const std::atomic_bool& stop) {
        unsigned char prefix[4];
        if (!ReadExact(reinterpret_cast<char*>(prefix), 4, stop))
            return false;
        const u32 size =
            u32{prefix[0]} | (u32{prefix[1]} << 8) | (u32{prefix[2]} << 16) | (u32{prefix[3]} << 24);
        if (!size || size > 65536)
            return false;
        std::string payload(size, '\0');
        if (!ReadExact(payload.data(), size, stop))
            return false;
        request = nlohmann::json::parse(payload, nullptr, false);
        return !request.is_discarded();
    }
    inline void Send(const nlohmann::json& reply) {
        const auto payload = reply.dump();
        if (payload.size() > 65536)
            throw std::runtime_error("reply exceeds control bound");
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
            std::cout.put(static_cast<char>(payload.size() >> (i * 8)));
        std::cout.write(payload.data(), payload.size());
        std::cout.flush();
        if (!std::cout)
            throw std::runtime_error("control pipe disconnected");
    }

    Common::Vec4<u8> LookupTexture(const u8* source, unsigned int x, unsigned int y,
                                   const TextureInfo& info, bool disable_alpha) {
        // Coordinate in tiles
        const unsigned int coarse_x = x / 8;
        const unsigned int coarse_y = y / 8;
    
        // Coordinate inside the tile
        const unsigned int fine_x = x % 8;
        const unsigned int fine_y = y % 8;
    
        const u8* line = source + coarse_y * info.stride;
        const u8* tile = line + coarse_x * CalculateTileSize(info.format);
        return LookupTexelInTile(tile, fine_x, fine_y, info, disable_alpha);
    }

        auto& page_table = *process.vm_manager.page_table;
    
        VAddr current = addr;
        VAddr end = addr + size;
    
        while (current < end) {
            const VAddr page_base = (current & ~CITRA_PAGE_MASK);
            const VAddr page_index = page_base >> CITRA_PAGE_BITS;
    
            auto it = page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.find(page_index);
            if (it != page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.end()) {
                // Nothing to do, only increment count.
                it->second.watchpoint_count++;
            } else {
                MemoryRef mem;
                PageType& type = page_table.attributes[page_index];
    
                switch (type) {
                case PageType::Memory:
                    mem = page_table.pointers.Ref(page_index);
                    type = PageType::MemoryWatchpoint;
                    page_table.pointers[page_index] = nullptr;
                    break;
                case PageType::RasterizerCachedMemory:
                    mem = GetPointerForRasterizerCache(page_base);
                    type = PageType::RasterizerCachedMemoryWatchpoint;
                    break;
                default:
                    LOG_ERROR(HW_Memory, "Cannot get pointer to register watchpoint for page 0x{:08X}",
                              page_base);
                    continue;
                }
    
                page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.insert(
                    {page_index,
                     PageTable::WatchpointPageInfo{.watchpoint_count = 1, .memory = std::move(mem)}});
            }
    
            current = page_base + CITRA_PAGE_SIZE;
        }
    }
    
    void MemorySystem::UnregisterWatchpoint(const Kernel::Process& process, VAddr addr, u32 size) {
        auto& page_table = *process.vm_manager.page_table;
    
        VAddr current = addr;
        VAddr end = addr + size;
    
        while (current < end) {
            const VAddr page_base = (current & ~CITRA_PAGE_MASK);
            const VAddr page_index = page_base >> CITRA_PAGE_BITS;
    
            auto it = page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.find(page_index);
            if (it != page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.end()) {
                if (--it->second.watchpoint_count == 0) {
    
                    PageType& type = page_table.attributes[page_index];
    
                    switch (type) {
                    case PageType::MemoryWatchpoint:
                        type = PageType::Memory;
                        page_table.pointers[page_index] = it->second.memory;
                        break;
                    case PageType::RasterizerCachedMemoryWatchpoint:
                        type = PageType::RasterizerCachedMemory;
                        break;
                    default:
                        LOG_ERROR(HW_Memory, "Invalid watchpoint page type for page 0x{:08X}: {}",
                                  page_base, static_cast<u8>(type));
                    }
    
                    page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.erase(page_index);
                }
            } else {
                LOG_ERROR(HW_Memory, "No watchpoint found on page 0x{:08X}", page_base);
            }
    
            current = page_base + CITRA_PAGE_SIZE;
        }
    }

    u32 MemorySystem::GetFCRAMOffset(const u8* pointer) const {
        ASSERT(pointer >= impl->fcram.get() && pointer <= impl->fcram.get() + Memory::FCRAM_N3DS_SIZE);
        return static_cast<u32>(pointer - impl->fcram.get());
    }
    
    u8* MemorySystem::GetFCRAMPointer(std::size_t offset) {
        ASSERT(offset <= Memory::FCRAM_N3DS_SIZE);
        return impl->fcram.get() + offset;
    }
    
    const u8* MemorySystem::GetFCRAMPointer(std::size_t offset) const {
        ASSERT(offset <= Memory::FCRAM_N3DS_SIZE);
        return impl->fcram.get() + offset;
    }
    
    MemoryRef MemorySystem::GetFCRAMRef(std::size_t offset) const {
        ASSERT(offset <= Memory::FCRAM_N3DS_SIZE);
        return MemoryRef(impl->fcram_mem, offset);
    }
    
    u8* MemorySystem::GetDspMemory(std::size_t offset) const {
        ASSERT(offset <= Memory::DSP_RAM_SIZE);
        return impl->dsp_ram.get() + offset;
    }

## Assistant

I found two more native edge cases worth fixing before broader tests: an unmapped watchpoint could enter an existing non-advancing loop, and large log pages could exceed the control-message limit. Watchpoint setup now checks the mapping first, and log pages stop at a byte budget and return a cursor.

    void Recorder::Finish(const std::string& filename) {
        // Setup CiTrace header
        CTHeader header;
        std::memcpy(header.magic, CTHeader::ExpectedMagicWord(), 4);
        header.version = CTHeader::ExpectedVersion();
        header.header_size = sizeof(CTHeader);
    
        // Calculate file offsets
        auto& initial = header.initial_state_offsets;
    
        initial.pica_registers_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.pica_registers.size());
        initial.lcd_registers_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.lcd_registers.size());
        initial.default_attributes_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.default_attributes.size());
        initial.vs_program_binary_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.vs_program_binary.size());
        initial.vs_swizzle_data_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.vs_swizzle_data.size());
        initial.vs_float_uniforms_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.vs_float_uniforms.size());
        initial.gs_program_binary_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.gs_program_binary.size());
        initial.gs_swizzle_data_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.gs_swizzle_data.size());
        initial.gs_float_uniforms_size = static_cast<u32>(initial_state.gs_float_uniforms.size());
        header.stream_size = static_cast<u32>(stream.size());
    
        initial.gpu_registers = sizeof(header);
        initial.lcd_registers = initial.gpu_registers + initial.gpu_registers_size * sizeof(u32);
        initial.pica_registers = initial.lcd_registers + initial.lcd_registers_size * sizeof(u32);
        ;
        initial.default_attributes = initial.pica_registers + initial.pica_registers_size * sizeof(u32);
        initial.vs_program_binary =
            initial.default_attributes + initial.default_attributes_size * sizeof(u32);
        initial.vs_swizzle_data =
            initial.vs_program_binary + initial.vs_program_binary_size * sizeof(u32);
        initial.vs_float_uniforms =
            initial.vs_swizzle_data + initial.vs_swizzle_data_size * sizeof(u32);
        initial.gs_program_binary =
            initial.vs_float_uniforms + initial.vs_float_uniforms_size * sizeof(u32);
        initial.gs_swizzle_data =
            initial.gs_program_binary + initial.gs_program_binary_size * sizeof(u32);
        initial.gs_float_uniforms =

        header.stream_offset = initial.gs_float_uniforms + initial.gs_float_uniforms_size * sizeof(u32);
    
        // Iterate through stream elements, update relevant stream element data
        for (auto& stream_element : stream) {
            switch (stream_element.data.type) {
            case MemoryLoad: {
                auto& file_offset = memory_regions[stream_element.hash];
                if (!stream_element.uses_existing_data) {
                    file_offset = header.stream_offset;
                }
                stream_element.data.memory_load.file_offset = file_offset;
                break;
            }
    
            default:
                // Other commands don't use any extra data
                DEBUG_ASSERT(stream_element.extra_data.size() == 0);
                break;
            }
            header.stream_offset += static_cast<u32>(stream_element.extra_data.size());
        }
    
        try {
            // Open file and write header
            FileUtil::IOFile file(filename, "wb");
            std::size_t written = file.WriteObject(header);
            if (written != 1 || file.Tell() != initial.gpu_registers)
                throw "Failed to write header";

    void Swapchain::Destroy() {
        vk::Device device = instance.GetDevice();
        if (swapchain) {
            device.destroySwapchainKHR(swapchain);
            swapchain = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
        }
        for (const auto semaphore : image_acquired) device.destroySemaphore(semaphore);
        for (const auto semaphore : present_ready) device.destroySemaphore(semaphore);
        image_acquired.clear();
        present_ready.clear();
    }

    void GPU::WriteReg(VAddr addr, u32 data) {
        switch (addr & 0xFFFFF000) {
        case VADDR_LCD: {
            const u32 offset = addr - VADDR_LCD;
            const u32 index = offset / sizeof(u32);
            ASSERT(addr % sizeof(u32) == 0);
            ASSERT(index < Pica::RegsLcd::NumIds());
            impl->pica.regs_lcd[index] = data;
            break;
        }
        case VADDR_GPU:
        case VADDR_GPU + 0x1000: {
            const u32 offset = addr - VADDR_GPU;
            const u32 index = offset / sizeof(u32);
    
            ASSERT(addr % sizeof(u32) == 0);
            ASSERT(index < Pica::PicaCore::Regs::NUM_REGS);
            impl->pica.regs.reg_array[index] = data;
    
            // Handle registers that trigger GPU actions
            switch (index) {
            case GPU_REG_INDEX(memory_fill_config[0].trigger):
                MemoryFill(0, 0);
                break;
            case GPU_REG_INDEX(memory_fill_config[1].trigger):
                MemoryFill(1, 1);
                break;
            case GPU_REG_INDEX(display_transfer_config.trigger):
                MemoryTransfer();
                break;
            case GPU_REG_INDEX(internal.pipeline.command_buffer.trigger[0]):
                SubmitCmdList(0);
        }
    
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.bool_uniforms):
            gs_setup.WriteUniformBoolReg(regs.internal.gs.bool_uniforms.Value());
            break;
    
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.int_uniforms[0]):
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.int_uniforms[1]):
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.int_uniforms[2]):
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.int_uniforms[3]): {
            const u32 index = (id - PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.int_uniforms[0]));
            gs_setup.WriteUniformIntReg(index, regs.internal.gs.GetIntUniform(index));
            break;
        }
    
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.uniform_setup.set_value[0]):
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.uniform_setup.set_value[1]):
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.uniform_setup.set_value[2]):
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.uniform_setup.set_value[3]):
        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.uniform_setup.set_value[4]):

        case PICA_REG_INDEX(gs.uniform_setup.set_value[6]):
    void PicaCore::WriteInternalReg(u32 id, u32 value, u32 mask, bool& stop_requested) {
        if (id >= RegsInternal::NUM_REGS) [[unlikely]] {
            // Writes to OOB registers are no-op.
            LOG_DEBUG(
                HW_GPU,
                "Commandlist tried to write to invalid register 0x{:03X} (value: {:08X}, mask: {:X})",
                id, value, mask);
            return;
        }
    
        delay_generator.AddCommands(1);
    
        // TODO: Figure out how register masking acts on e.g. vs.uniform_setup.set_value
        const u32 old_value = regs.internal.reg_array[id];
        const u32 write_mask = ExpandBitsToBytes[mask];
        regs.internal.reg_array[id] = (old_value & ~write_mask) | (value & write_mask);
    
        if (debug_context) [[unlikely]] {
            // Track register write.
            DebugUtils::OnPicaRegWrite(id, mask, regs.internal.reg_array[id]);
            // Track events.
            debug_context->OnEvent(DebugContext::Event::PicaCommandLoaded, &id);
        }
    
        if (reg_impl_flags_lut[id].NeedsSpecialHandling()) {
            HandleSpecialReg(id, value, stop_requested);
        }
    
        dirty_regs.Set(id);
    
        if (debug_context) [[unlikely]] {
            debug_context->OnEvent(DebugContext::Event::PicaCommandProcessed, &id);
        }
    }

    struct InputParameters {

    class Input {
    public:
        Input() = default;
    
        virtual ~Input() = default;
    
        /// Starts the microphone. Called by Core
        virtual void StartSampling(const InputParameters& params) = 0;
    
        /// Stops the microphone. Called by Core
        virtual void StopSampling() = 0;
    
        /// Checks whether the microphone is currently sampling.
        virtual bool IsSampling() = 0;
    
        /**
         * Adjusts the Parameters. Implementations should update the parameters field in addition to
         * changing the mic to sample according to the new parameters. Called by Core
         */
        virtual void AdjustSampleRate(u32 sample_rate) = 0;
    
        /**
         * Called from the actual event timing at a constant period under a given sample rate.
         * When sampling is enabled this function is expected to return a buffer of 16 samples in ideal
         * conditions, but can be lax if the data is coming in from another source like a real mic.
         */
        virtual Samples Read() = 0;
    
    protected:
        InputParameters parameters;
    };

    class StaticInput final : public Input {
    public:
        StaticInput();
        ~StaticInput() = default;
    
        void StartSampling(const InputParameters& params) {
            parameters = params;
            is_sampling = true;
        }
    
        void StopSampling() {
            is_sampling = false;
        }
    
        bool IsSampling() {
            return is_sampling;
        }
    
        void AdjustSampleRate(u32 sample_rate) {}
    
        Samples Read() {
            return (parameters.sample_size == 8) ? CACHE_8_BIT : CACHE_16_BIT;
        }
    
    private:

    };

    namespace Loader {
    
    /*
     * File layout:
     * - File header
     * - Code, rodata and data relocation table headers
     * - Code segment
     * - Rodata segment
     * - Loadable (non-BSS) part of the data segment
     * - Code relocation table
     * - Rodata relocation table
     * - Data relocation table
     *
     * Memory layout before relocations are applied:
     * [0..codeSegSize)             -> code segment
     * [codeSegSize..rodataSegSize) -> rodata segment
     * [rodataSegSize..dataSegSize) -> data segment
     *
     * Memory layout after relocations are applied: well, however the loader sets it up :)
     * The entrypoint is always the start of the code segment.
     * The BSS section must be cleared manually by the application.
     */
    
    enum THREEDSX_Error { ERROR_NONE = 0, ERROR_READ = 1, ERROR_FILE = 2, ERROR_ALLOC = 3 };
    
    static const u32 RELOCBUFSIZE = 512;
    static const unsigned int NUM_SEGMENTS = 3;
    
    // File header
    #pragma pack(1)
    struct THREEDSX_Header {
        u32 magic;
        u16 header_size, reloc_hdr_size;
        u32 format_ver;
        u32 flags;
    
        // Sizes of the code, rodata and data segments +
        // size of the BSS section (uninitialized latter half of the data segment)
        u32 code_seg_size, rodata_seg_size, data_seg_size, bss_size;
        // offset and size of smdh
        u32 smdh_offset, smdh_size;
        // offset to filesystem
        u32 fs_offset;
    };
    
    // Relocation header: all fields (even extra unknown fields) are guaranteed to be relocation counts.
    struct THREEDSX_RelocHdr {
        // # of absolute relocations (that is, fix address to post-relocation memory layout)
        u32 cross_segment_absolute;
        // # of cross-segment relative relocations (that is, 32bit signed offsets that need to be
        // patched)
        u32 cross_segment_relative;
        // more?
    
        // Relocations are written in this order:
        // - Absolute relocations
        // - Relative relocations
    };
    
    // Relocation entry: from the current pointer, skip X words and patch Y words
    struct THREEDSX_Reloc {
        u16 skip, patch;
    };
    #pragma pack()
    
    struct THREEloadinfo {
        u8* seg_ptrs[3]; // code, rodata & data
        u32 seg_addrs[3];
        u32 seg_sizes[3];
    };
    
    static u32 TranslateAddr(u32 addr, const THREEloadinfo* loadinfo, u32* offsets) {
        if (addr < offsets[0])
            return loadinfo->seg_addrs[0] + addr;
        if (addr < offsets[1])
            return loadinfo->seg_addrs[1] + addr - offsets[0];
        return loadinfo->seg_addrs[2] + addr - offsets[1];
    }
    
    using Kernel::CodeSet;
    
    static THREEDSX_Error Load3DSXFile(Core::System& system, FileUtil::IOFileBase* file, u32 base_addr,
                                       std::shared_ptr<CodeSet>* out_codeset) {
        if (!file->IsOpen())
            return ERROR_FILE;
    
        // Reset read pointer in case this file has been read before.
        file->Seek(0, SEEK_SET);
    
        THREEDSX_Header hdr;
        if (file->ReadBytes(&hdr, sizeof(hdr)) != sizeof(hdr))
            return ERROR_READ;
    
        THREEloadinfo loadinfo;
        // loadinfo segments must be a multiple of 0x1000
        loadinfo.seg_sizes[0] = (hdr.code_seg_size + 0xFFF) & ~0xFFF;
        loadinfo.seg_sizes[1] = (hdr.rodata_seg_size + 0xFFF) & ~0xFFF;
        loadinfo.seg_sizes[2] = (hdr.data_seg_size + 0xFFF) & ~0xFFF;
        // prevent integer overflow leading to heap-buffer-overflow
        if (loadinfo.seg_sizes[0] < hdr.code_seg_size || loadinfo.seg_sizes[1] < hdr.rodata_seg_size ||
            loadinfo.seg_sizes[2] < hdr.data_seg_size) {
            return ERROR_READ;
        }
        u32 offsets[2] = {loadinfo.seg_sizes[0], loadinfo.seg_sizes[0] + loadinfo.seg_sizes[1]};
        u32 n_reloc_tables = hdr.reloc_hdr_size / sizeof(u32);
        std::vector<u8> program_image(loadinfo.seg_sizes[0] + loadinfo.seg_sizes[1] +
                                      loadinfo.seg_sizes[2]);
    
        loadinfo.seg_addrs[0] = base_addr;
        loadinfo.seg_addrs[1] = loadinfo.seg_addrs[0] + loadinfo.seg_sizes[0];
        loadinfo.seg_addrs[2] = loadinfo.seg_addrs[1] + loadinfo.seg_sizes[1];
        loadinfo.seg_ptrs[0] = program_image.data();
        loadinfo.seg_ptrs[1] = loadinfo.seg_ptrs[0] + loadinfo.seg_sizes[0];
        loadinfo.seg_ptrs[2] = loadinfo.seg_ptrs[1] + loadinfo.seg_sizes[1];
    
        // Skip header for future compatibility
        file->Seek(hdr.header_size, SEEK_SET);
    
        // Read the relocation headers
        std::vector<u32> relocs(n_reloc_tables * NUM_SEGMENTS);
        for (unsigned int current_segment = 0; current_segment < NUM_SEGMENTS; ++current_segment) {
            std::size_t size = n_reloc_tables * sizeof(u32);
            if (file->ReadBytes(&relocs[current_segment * n_reloc_tables], size) != size)
                return ERROR_READ;
        }
    
        // Read the segments
        if (file->ReadBytes(loadinfo.seg_ptrs[0], hdr.code_seg_size) != hdr.code_seg_size)
            return ERROR_READ;
        if (file->ReadBytes(loadinfo.seg_ptrs[1], hdr.rodata_seg_size) != hdr.rodata_seg_size)
            return ERROR_READ;
        if (file->ReadBytes(loadinfo.seg_ptrs[2], hdr.data_seg_size - hdr.bss_size) !=
            hdr.data_seg_size - hdr.bss_size)
            return ERROR_READ;
    
        // BSS clear

    //! Native worker process handling.
    //!
    //! The worker is a separate OS process running a modified Azahar core. This
    //! module owns starting it, handing it its private storage and stopping it
    //! without leaving orphans behind.
    
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::process::{Child, Command, Stdio};
    use thiserror::Error;
    
    /// Azahar branch flavour a worker was built from.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    pub enum WorkerFlavor {
        /// `integration` branch: upstream minimal worker hooks.
        Integration,
        /// `experimental` branch: tracing, debugger and accuracy work.
        Experimental,
    }
    
    impl WorkerFlavor {
        /// Branch name on the Azahar fork.
        pub fn branch(&self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                WorkerFlavor::Integration => "integration",
                WorkerFlavor::Experimental => "experimental",
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// Errors raised while launching or supervising a worker.
    #[derive(Debug, Error)]
    pub enum WorkerLaunchError {
        /// The worker executable was not found.
        #[error("worker executable not found: {0}")]
        NotFound(PathBuf),
        /// The worker could not be started.
        #[error("failed to launch worker: {0}")]
        Launch(#[source] std::io::Error),
    }
    
    /// How a worker process should be started.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct WorkerSpec {
        /// Path of the worker executable.
        pub executable: PathBuf,
        /// Private storage root handed to the worker.
        pub storage_root: PathBuf,
        /// Additional command line arguments.
        pub args: Vec<String>,
        /// Environment variables added to the worker environment.
        pub env: Vec<(String, String)>,
    }
    
    impl WorkerSpec {
        /// A worker that runs against `storage_root`.
        pub fn new(executable: impl Into<PathBuf>, storage_root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
            Self {
                executable: executable.into(),
                storage_root: storage_root.into(),
                args: Vec::new(),
                env: Vec::new(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Add a command line argument.
        pub fn arg(mut self, arg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
            self.args.push(arg.into());
            self
        }
    
        /// Add an environment variable.
        pub fn env(mut self, key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
            self.env.push((key.into(), value.into()));
            self
        }
    }
    
    /// A running worker process.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct WorkerProcess {
        child: Child,
        executable: PathBuf,
    }

        template <bool UNSAFE>
        void ReadBlockImpl(const Kernel::Process& process, const VAddr src_addr, void* dest_buffer,
                           const std::size_t size) {
            auto& page_table = *process.vm_manager.page_table;
    
            std::size_t remaining_size = size;
            std::size_t page_index = src_addr >> CITRA_PAGE_BITS;
            std::size_t page_offset = src_addr & CITRA_PAGE_MASK;
    
            while (remaining_size > 0) {
                const std::size_t copy_amount = std::min(CITRA_PAGE_SIZE - page_offset, remaining_size);
                const VAddr current_vaddr =
                    static_cast<VAddr>((page_index << CITRA_PAGE_BITS) + page_offset);
    
                switch (page_table.attributes[page_index]) {
                case PageType::Unmapped: {
                    LOG_ERROR(
                        HW_Memory,
                        "unmapped ReadBlock @ 0x{:08X} (start address = 0x{:08X}, size = {}) at PC "
                        "0x{:08X}",
                        current_vaddr, src_addr, size, GetPC());
                    std::memset(dest_buffer, 0, copy_amount);
                    break;
                }
                case PageType::Memory: {
                    DEBUG_ASSERT(page_table.pointers[page_index]);
    
                    const u8* src_ptr = page_table.pointers[page_index] + page_offset;
                    std::memcpy(dest_buffer, src_ptr, copy_amount);
                    break;
                }
                case PageType::MemoryWatchpoint: {
                    auto it = page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.find(page_index);
                    ASSERT_MSG(it != page_table.watchpoint_pages_map.end(),
                               "Missing memory for watchpoint page");
    
                    const u8* src_ptr = it->second.memory.GetPtr() + page_offset;
                    std::memcpy(dest_buffer, src_ptr, copy_amount);
                    break;
                }
                case PageType::RasterizerCachedMemory:
                case PageType::RasterizerCachedMemoryWatchpoint: {
                    if constexpr (!UNSAFE) {
                        RasterizerFlushVirtualRegion(current_vaddr, static_cast<u32>(copy_amount),
                                                     FlushMode::Flush);
                    }
                    std::memcpy(dest_buffer, GetPointerForRasterizerCache(current_vaddr), copy_amount);
                    break;
                }
            if (memory != nullptr && memory.GetSize() > CITRA_PAGE_SIZE)
                memory += CITRA_PAGE_SIZE;
        }
    }
    
    void MemorySystem::MapMemoryRegion(PageTable& page_table, VAddr base, u32 size, MemoryRef target) {

        ASSERT_MSG((base & CITRA_PAGE_MASK) == 0, "non-page aligned base: {:08X}", base);
        MapPages(page_table, base / CITRA_PAGE_SIZE, size / CITRA_PAGE_SIZE, target, PageType::Memory);
    }
    
    void MemorySystem::UnmapRegion(PageTable& page_table, VAddr base, u32 size) {
        ASSERT_MSG((size & CITRA_PAGE_MASK) == 0, "non-page aligned size: {:08X}", size);
        ASSERT_MSG((base & CITRA_PAGE_MASK) == 0, "non-page aligned base: {:08X}", base);
        MapPages(page_table, base / CITRA_PAGE_SIZE, size / CITRA_PAGE_SIZE, nullptr,

    }

    std::vector<InputDetails> ListInputs() {
        return {input_details.begin(), input_details.end()};
    }
    
    const InputDetails& GetInputDetails(InputType input_type) {
        auto iter = std::find_if(
            input_details.begin(), input_details.end(),
            [input_type](const auto& input_detail) { return input_detail.type == input_type; });
    
        if (input_type == InputType::Auto || iter == input_details.end()) {
            if (input_type != InputType::Auto) {
                LOG_ERROR(Audio, "AudioCore::GetInputDetails given invalid input_type {}", input_type);
            }
            // Auto-select.
            // input_details is ordered in terms of desirability, with the best choice at the front.
            iter = input_details.begin();
        }
    
        return *iter;
    }

    void GMainWindow::LoadAmiibo(const QString& filename) {
        Service::SM::ServiceManager& sm = system.ServiceManager();
        auto nfc = sm.GetService<Service::NFC::Module::Interface>("nfc:u");
        if (!nfc) [[unlikely]] {
            return;
        }
    
        std::scoped_lock lock{system.Kernel().GetHLELock()};
        if (!nfc->LoadAmiibo(filename.toStdString())) {
            QMessageBox::warning(this, tr("Error opening amiibo data file"),
                                 tr("Unable to open amiibo file \"%1\" for reading.").arg(filename));
            return;
        }
    
        ui->action_Remove_Amiibo->setEnabled(true);
    }

    typedef unsigned int u32;

    volatile u32 counter = 1;
    volatile u32 canary[2] = {0xcafebabe, 0xdeadbeef};
    
    __attribute__((noinline)) static void output(const char* text, u32 length) {
        register const char* r0 __asm__("r0") = text;
        register u32 r1 __asm__("r1") = length;
        __asm__ volatile("svc 0x3d" : "+r"(r0), "+r"(r1) :: "r2", "r3", "memory");
    }
    
    __attribute__((noinline)) void tick(void) {
        watched = ++counter;
        if (mode == 1) watched = *(volatile u32*)0;
        if (mode == 2) canary[1] = 0xbad;
        if (mode == 3) {
            register u32 r0 __asm__("r0") = 0;
            __asm__ volatile("svc 0x3c" : "+r"(r0) :: "r1", "r2", "r3", "memory");

    }

    """Build the owned freestanding ARM fixture with clang, or devkitARM GCC.
    The 3DSX segment container follows native loader/3dsx.cpp. Absolute link addresses
    match the worker's homebrew base; relocation tables are intentionally empty.
    """
    from pathlib import Path
    import argparse
    import hashlib
    import json
    import shutil
    import struct
    import subprocess
    
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--gcc", help="devkitARM arm-none-eabi-gcc executable (uses matching objcopy)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    out = args.output.resolve()
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    source = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures/debugger"
    compiler = args.gcc or shutil.which("clang")
    if not compiler:
        raise SystemExit("clang or --gcc <devkitARM GCC> is required")
    objcopy = str(Path(compiler).with_name("arm-none-eabi-objcopy.exe")) if args.gcc else shutil.which("llvm-objcopy")
    elf = out / "debugger.elf"
    command = [compiler, "-mcpu=mpcore", "-marm", "-mfloat-abi=soft", "-O1", "-g", "-gdwarf-4",
               "-ffreestanding", "-fno-builtin", "-fno-omit-frame-pointer", "-fno-unwind-tables",
               "-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables", "-nostdlib", "-Wl,--build-id=none",
               "-Wl,-T,"+str(source / "link.ld"), str(source / "fixture.c"), "-o", str(elf)]
    if not args.gcc:
        command[1:1] = ["--target=armv6k-none-eabi", "-fuse-ld=lld"]
    subprocess.run(command, check=True)
    segments = []
    for section in ("text", "rodata", "data"):
        path = out / (section + ".bin")
        subprocess.run([objcopy, "--dump-section", "."+section+"="+str(path), str(elf)], check=True)
        segments.append(path.read_bytes())
    header = struct.pack("<IHHIIIIIIIII", 0x58534433, 44, 8, 0, 0,
                         *(len(s) for s in segments), 0, 0, 0, 0)
    rom = header + bytes(24) + b"".join(segments)
    (out / "debugger.3dsx").write_bytes(rom)
    (out / "build.json").write_text(json.dumps(dict(compiler=subprocess.check_output([compiler,"--version"],text=True).splitlines()[0],
        command=command, sha256=hashlib.sha256(rom).hexdigest(), elf_sha256=hashlib.sha256(elf.read_bytes()).hexdigest()),indent=2))
    print(out / "debugger.3dsx")

    //! Bounded ARM/Thumb decoding through the host's LLVM tools; no guest code runs.
    use std::{io, path::Path};
    use tokio::process::Command;
    
    /// A tiny ELF object lets llvm-objdump decode arbitrary captured bytes faithfully.
    fn elf(address: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out=vec![0u8;52];
        out[..7].copy_from_slice(b"\x7fELF\x01\x01\x01");
        out[16..18].copy_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
        out[18..20].copy_from_slice(&40u16.to_le_bytes());
        out[20..24].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        out[36..40].copy_from_slice(&0x05000000u32.to_le_bytes());
        out[40..42].copy_from_slice(&52u16.to_le_bytes());
        out[46..48].copy_from_slice(&40u16.to_le_bytes());
        out[48..50].copy_from_slice(&3u16.to_le_bytes());
        out[50..52].copy_from_slice(&2u16.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(bytes);
        let names_offset=out.len() as u32;
        let names=b"\x00.text\x00.shstrtab\x00";
        out.extend_from_slice(names);
        while out.len()%4!=0 { out.push(0); }
        let table=out.len() as u32;
        out[32..36].copy_from_slice(&table.to_le_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(&[0;40]);
        for fields in [[1,1,6,address,52,bytes.len() as u32,0,0,4,0],
                       [7,3,0,0,names_offset,names.len() as u32,0,0,1,0]] {
            for word in fields {out.extend_from_slice(&word.to_le_bytes());}
        }
        out
    }
    
    pub async fn decode(root: &Path,address:u32,bytes:&[u8],thumb:bool) -> io::Result<String> {
        if bytes.is_empty() || bytes.len()>4096 { return Err(io::Error::other("decode budget 1..4096 bytes")); }
        let path=root.join(format!("decode-{}.o",lotus_protocol::envelope::SessionUuid::generate()));
        std::fs::write(&path,elf(address,bytes))?;
        let mut command=Command::new("llvm-objdump");
        command.args(["--disassemble",if thumb {"--triple=thumbv6k-none-eabi"}else{"--triple=armv6k-none-eabi"},"--mcpu=mpcore"])
            .arg(&path).kill_on_drop(true);
        #[cfg(windows)] command.creation_flags(0x0800_0000);
        let result=tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3),command.output()).await;
        let _=std::fs::remove_file(path);
        let output=result.map_err(|_|io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::TimedOut,"LLVM decode deadline"))??;
        if !output.status.success() || output.stdout.len()>131072 {
            return Err(io::Error::other("LLVM ARM disassembler failed; install llvm-objdump on the host PATH"));
        }
        Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).lines().filter(|line| {
            line.trim_start().split_once(':').is_some_and(|(address,_)|u32::from_str_radix(address,16).is_ok())
        }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n"))
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
        #[tokio::test] async fn arm_and_thumb_decode_the_actual_bytes() {
            if Command::new("llvm-objdump").arg("--version").output().await.is_err() { return; }
            let root=std::env::temp_dir();
            let arm=decode(&root,0x100000,&[0xfe,0xff,0xff,0xea],false).await.unwrap();
            assert!(arm.contains("100000:")&&arm.contains("b\t"),"{arm}");
            let thumb=decode(&root,0x100000,&[0xfe,0xe7],true).await.unwrap();
            assert!(thumb.contains("100000:")&&thumb.contains("b\t"),"{thumb}");
        }
    }

        #[tool(
            description = "Start a session in its own worker process. Handles expire when this server exits; primary cards retain guest storage across restarts. kind=primary mounts a persistent card (one primary per card); kind=secondary (default) is disposable: empty, or a point-in-time copy of `card`, deleted on stop. Optional asset loads paused. Requires host control permission."
        )]
        pub async fn lotus_create_session(
            &self,
            Parameters(args): Parameters<CreateArgs>,
        ) -> CallToolResult {
            let result = async {
                let host = self.require_host()?;
                let kind = match (args.kind, args.card) {
                    (KindArg::Primary, Some(card)) => SessionKind::Primary { card },
                    (KindArg::Primary, None) => {
                        return Err(io::Error::new(
                            io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                            "a primary session needs a card",
                        ))
                    }
                    (KindArg::Secondary, parent) => SessionKind::Secondary { parent },
                };
                let info = host.create(kind, args.asset.as_deref(), Actor::Mcp).await?;
                Ok(serde_json::json!({"session": info.id, "info": info}))
            }
            .await;
            tool_result(result)
        }
    
        #[tool(
            description = "Load an approved asset into an owned session, replacing its content; leaves it paused. Requires control permission."
        )]
        pub async fn lotus_load(&self, Parameters(args): Parameters<LoadArgs>) -> CallToolResult {
            let result = async {
                let host = self.require_host()?;
                json(&host.load(&args.session, &args.asset, Actor::Mcp).await?)
            }
            .await;
            tool_result(result)

        ) -> CallToolResult {
            let result = async {
                let host = self.require_host()?;
                host.advance(&args.session, args.frames, Actor::Mcp).await
            }
            .await;
            tool_result(result)
        }
    
        #[tool(
            description = "run (continuous, returns immediately), pause, reset or stop an owned session. Requires host control permission."
        )]
        pub async fn lotus_control(&self, Parameters(args): Parameters<ControlArgs>) -> CallToolResult {
            let result = async {
                let host = self.require_host()?;
                let id = &args.session;
                match args.operation {
                    ControlOperation::Run => {
                        host.run(id, Actor::Mcp).await?;
                        Ok(serde_json::json!({"playing": true}))
                    }
                    ControlOperation::Pause => host.pause(id, Actor::Mcp).await,
                    ControlOperation::Reset => host.reset(id, Actor::Mcp).await,

                        host.stop(id, Actor::Mcp).await?;

                    }
                }
            }
            .await;
            tool_result(result)
        }

    # Implementer rules — read before touching code
    
    ## Order of authority
    
    1. Measured physical-hardware behavior > independent hardware trace > documented specification > existing emulator behavior > hypothesis.
    2. User's explicit decisions: native Azahar integration (**not Libretro**), Rust + GPUI, multiple isolated workers, two Azahar branches (`integration`, `experimental`).
    3. Preserve compatibility and successful baselines before speculative accuracy changes.
    
    ## Attribution
    
    Agents never insert their own branding as a commit attribution or co-attribution. All commits are authored solely by the git identity already set on the authors computer. For example, the project owner's git identity should always be `terezi <jules@foxtails.me>`.
    
    ## Documentation
    
    Agents should keep documentation and comments as brief as possible. This does not mean spare on technical details. Explain what it is, what it's doing, how it works, what it isn't, and the relevant necessary information.
    
    Agents must keep documentation consistent.
    
    Agents must always be able to refer back to primary sources (such as 3DBrew, the citra wiki, source code citations from azahar) to justify changes or decisions. Agents are encouraged to use secondary sources, such as Coffeepot, for easy lookup of information - coffeepot, however, should not be your citation.
    
    ## Branch discipline
    
    - `integration`: only smallest viable native worker/front-end hooks, configurable build target, deterministic control queue, frame/audio/input adapters, and proven bug fixes required for integration. No GPU timing redesign or pervasive tracing. Regular upstream merges.
    - `experimental`: based on `integration`; structured tracing, debugger controls, snapshot experiments, timing models, hardware-fidelity experiments. Never merge `experimental` wholesale into `integration`.
    - Any item that seems essential to integration but introduces accuracy behavior changes needs an ADR and separate two-step PR.
    - Freeze upstream baseline SHA and CMake options in each test report. One independent worktree/build directory per branch. Never build both using one configured CMake cache.
    
    ## Evidence and debugging
    
    - Never confuse host milliseconds, virtual 3DS ticks, and empirically inferred hardware cycles.
    - Never claim a new accuracy feature without a hardware witness, an independent reference, and a counterexample where the old behavior differed.
    - Any cross-thread mutable emulated-state read MUST run at a defined safe point or return a labeled approximate telemetry snapshot.
    - Instrument with bounded buffers, severity filters and loss counters. Avoid `printf` in hot paths. Measure instrumentation-on/off overhead.
    - A GPU draw capture must describe the actual command/state at the draw, not a post-frame memory reconstruction. Pre-draw hashes must be computed by the draw or use frozen memory snapshots; never hash unrelated time-dependent registers as image identity.
    - Label examples explicitly: **verified compiled**, **verified hardware**, **verified emulator**, **source inspected**, or **proposed**. No unverifiable green check marks.
    
    ## Implementation quality
    
    - Prefer a narrow PR with a runnable acceptance test over a broad refactor.
    - Keep the C++ worker free of GPUI, MCP, and agent concepts.
    - Keep FFI structs plain, fixed-width and versioned; do not expose `std::string`, `std::vector`, `Core::System*` or internal layouts across IPC.
    - No unsandboxed remote RPC listener by default. MCP/control access local-only and scoped to explicitly created workers.
    - Treat ROMs, firmware, save data, logs and captures as sensitive user assets. Do not upload them, bundle them, or include them in bug reports without consent.
    - On worker crash, retain logs and metadata, invalidate frame-buffer leases, terminate child descendants and release per-instance locks.
    - Do not implement experimental multi-instance support by embedding two Azahar `Core::System`s in one process: globals and lifetime assumptions are not cleared.
    - Avoid speculative architectural abstractions that lack a second backend or a concrete test.
    
    ## Definition of done for every PR
    
    1. Explain touched subsystem, expected change, and branch rationale.
    2. Enumerate upstream source revision and build flags; tests and known untested platforms.
    3. Include a test that would fail without the change (or justify an instrumentation-only PR).
    4. Record guest output hash/checkpoints and host overhead for performance-relevant changes.
    5. Confirm clean shutdown, second launch, and two parallel workers if shared process/storage infrastructure changed.
    6. Update docs/source-map and protocol schema for altered interfaces.
    7. Make limitations explicit; retain rollback flag for risk-bearing work.
    # 29 — Wave 3 plan: comprehensive agentic debugger
    
    Status: **proposed**, 2026-11-15. Tickets and their Deliver/Check/Avoid terms
    are in [15](15-implementation-tickets.md); this document holds the goal,
    decisions, Azahar parity matrix and milestone order. No item here is
    implemented; source facts below are **source inspected** at the native pin in
    `config/pins.toml`.
    
    ## Goal
    
    LOTUS + CITnLO must meet or exceed every debugging, configuration and
    inspection capability of Azahar, exposed uniformly through the worker
    protocol, CLI, MCP and desktop, so that an agent can find and explain guest
    bugs without the Qt frontend. "Exceed" means capabilities Azahar lacks:
    rewind, session forking, predicate stops, symbol-aware debugging, matrix
    runs, and a single arbitrated control model across GDB, MCP and desktop.
    
    ## Decisions (owner, 2026-11-15)
    
    | ADR | Decision | Consequence |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | ADR-008 | **GDB server is written in Rust** (`crates/gdb`) on top of the Lotus debug API; Azahar's stub is not used | CITnLO workers build with `ENABLE_GDBSTUB=OFF`; HIO is rerouted to the worker debug channel. Multi-session, non-stop and reverse execution become possible |
    | ADR-009 | **Offscreen Vulkan worker from the start of Wave 3**; software renderer stays as default-safe fallback and oracle | New headless presentation path; `graphics_api`, `resolution_factor`, `physical_device` and hardware-renderer GPU debugging become real |
    | ADR-006 (unchanged) | **Old 3DS is the default profile**; New 3DS is a fully supported, explicitly labeled profile | Every test that touches CPU, scheduling or memory layout runs on both profiles |
    | ADR-010 | **Settings schema and transport live in `integration`**; debugger and accuracy toggles that change behavior are exposed but not altered there | Both AZAHAR and CITnLO accept profiles; default profile reproduces today's behavior byte for byte (proven by T24 check) |
    | ADR-011 | **Audio is in Wave 3**: audible output, capture, HLE/LLE DSP and mic injection | Supersedes the muted-only profile in [25](25-wave-status.md) |
    
    ADR-010 rationale: a settings channel is a frontend adapter (allowed in
    `integration` by [03](03-azahar-branches.md)); keeping it there means the
    AZAHAR backend can serve as a control in matrix runs (T41) with identical
    profiles. Any setting whose *default* would differ from stock still needs its
    own ADR.
    
    ## Source facts that constrain the design
    
    | Fact | Source | Effect |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Azahar GDB stub binds `INADDR_ANY` | `src/core/gdbstub/gdbstub.cpp:2125` | Violates local-only rule; another reason for ADR-008. Build-flag test must prove the stub is absent |
    | HIO request enters via `svcBreak`-family path into `GDBStub::SetHioRequest` | `src/core/hle/kernel/svc.cpp:1178`, `gdbstub/hio.h` (152-byte `PackedGdbHioRequest`, libctru layout) | CITnLO patch forwards the request address to the debug channel; Rust server implements the `F` reply |
    | Worker forces software renderer, Old 3DS, stub off | `src/ctr_worker/frontend.h:61-64` | Defaults move into the T24 default profile instead of hard-coded writes |
    | `is_new_3ds` read at boot (memory mode, cores) | `src/core/core.cpp:401,461` | Apply class `boot` |
    | `cpu_clock_percentage` applied live | `System::ApplySettings`, `core.cpp:876` | Apply class `live` |
    | Vulkan instance accepts `WindowSystemType::Headless`, but `PresentWindow` always creates a surface | `vk_instance.cpp:136`, `vk_present_window.cpp:104` | T45 adds an offscreen presenter with readback into the frame ring |
    | LLE DSP selected from `audio_emulation` at system init | `core.cpp:661-662` | Apply class `boot`; firmware is a user asset in the session root, never bundled |
    | CFG values (username, birthday, language, country, sound mode, play coins) live in CFG save data, not `Settings::values` | `configure_system.ui`, `hle/service/cfg` | Apply class `cfg-savedata`; written through the CFG module before boot |
    
    Every other setting's apply class is determined in T24 by reading where it is
    consumed; none is assumed.
    
    ## Parity matrix
    
    Azahar column names its frontend action, setting or interface. Each row must
    be reachable from worker protocol, CLI and MCP (T44 enforces this);
    desktop coverage follows in T17.

    | GDB `Z2/Z3/Z4` watchpoints | Read/write/access watchpoints with cost estimate and cap | T14b |

    ## Milestones

    """Bounded wire-level acceptance probe; private roots, no uploaded user assets."""
    import argparse
    import hashlib
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    import queue
    import struct
    import subprocess
    import threading
    import time
    import uuid
    
    
    class Peer:
        def __init__(self, worker, root):
            root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
            self.root = root
            self.stderr = (root / "probe.stderr.log").open("wb")
            self.process = subprocess.Popen([str(worker)], env={**os.environ, "LOTUS_STORAGE_ROOT": str(root)}, stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=self.stderr)
            self.session = uuid.uuid4().hex
            self.epoch = 1
            self.sequence = 0
            self.notifications = []
            self.output = queue.Queue(32)
            self.reader = threading.Thread(target=self.read, daemon=True)
            self.reader.start()
    
        def read(self):
            try:
                while True:
                    header = self.process.stdout.read(4)
                    if len(header) != 4:
                        raise EOFError("worker closed stdout")
                    length, = struct.unpack("<I", header)
                    assert 0 < length <= 65536
                    self.output.put(json.loads(self.process.stdout.read(length)))
            except Exception as error:
                self.output.put(error)
    
        def call(self, method, params=None, expected="ok"):
            self.sequence += 1
            data = json.dumps(dict(version_major=1, version_minor=0, request_id=self.sequence,
                                   session=self.session, epoch=self.epoch, method=method, params=params)).encode()
            self.process.stdin.write(struct.pack("<I", len(data)) + data)
            self.process.stdin.flush()
            while True:
                reply = self.output.get(timeout=35)
                if isinstance(reply, Exception):
                    raise reply
                assert reply["session"] == self.session
                if reply.get("notification"):
                    self.notifications.append(reply)
                    continue
                assert reply["request_id"] == self.sequence, reply
                self.epoch = reply["epoch"]
                assert reply["status"] == expected, reply
                return reply["data"]
    
        def debug(self, operation, **params):
            return self.call("debug", dict(operation=operation, **params))
    
        def close(self):
            try:
                if self.process.poll() is None:
                    self.call("stop")
                self.process.wait(timeout=5)
            finally:
                if self.process.poll() is None:
                    self.process.kill()
                    self.process.wait()
                self.stderr.close()
    
    
    def probe(worker, asset, root, experimental, new, vulkan, frames=60):
        peer = Peer(worker, root)
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            peer.call("hello")  # Regression: omitted notification negotiation remains legal.
            peer.call("hello", {"notifications": True})
            settings = []
            offset = 0
            while True:
                page = peer.debug("settings_list", offset=offset, limit=32)
                settings.extend(page["settings"])
                offset = page["next"]
                if offset is None:
                    break
            assert len(settings) >= 125
            peer.debug("settings_set", name="is_new_3ds", value=new)
            peer.debug("settings_set", name="graphics_api", value=2 if vulkan else 0)
            peer.call("load", {"path": str(asset)})
            peer.call("debug", {"operation": "settings_set", "name": "is_new_3ds", "value": not new}, "invalid_argument")
            result = peer.call("run_until", {"frames": frames})
            capture = peer.call("capture")
            hashes = {}
            for lease in capture["frames"]:
                data = (root / lease["path"]).read_bytes()
                assert data[:4] == b"LTRF" and len(data) == lease["bytes"] + 32
                hashes[lease["screen"]] = hashlib.sha256(data[32:]).hexdigest()
            registers = peer.debug("registers", core=0)
            assert len(registers["registers"]) == 16 and len(registers["vfp"]) == 64
            threads = peer.debug("threads")
            if experimental:
                peer.call("pause")
                pc = registers["registers"][15]
                # A one-instruction self-loop makes breakpoint/skip semantics independent of app scheduling.
                peer.debug("write_memory", address=pc & ~3, bytes=[254, 255, 255, 234])
                peer.debug("write_register", core=0, register=15, value=pc & ~3)
                bp = peer.debug("breakpoint_set", address=pc & ~3, kind="execute", length=4)
                stopped = peer.call("run_until", {"frames": 1})
                assert stopped["stop"]["reason"] == "breakpoint", stopped
                assert stopped["stop"]["breakpoint"] == bp["id"]
                peer.debug("breakpoint_remove", id=bp["id"])
                step = peer.debug("step", core=0, count=1)
                assert step["instructions"] == 1 and step["stop"]["reason"] == "step", step
            return dict(new_3ds=new, renderer="vulkan" if vulkan else "software", source=result["source"],
                        hashes=hashes, threads=len(threads["threads"]), seconds=time.monotonic()-start,
                        notifications=len(peer.notifications), root=str(root))
        finally:
            peer.close()
            assert "Failed to find title id for ROM (Error 0)" not in (root / "probe.stderr.log").read_text(errors="replace")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("worker", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("asset", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("--experimental", action="store_true")
        parser.add_argument("--vulkan", action="store_true")
        args = parser.parse_args()
        reports = []
        for new in (False, True):
            report = probe(args.worker.resolve(), args.asset.resolve(),
                           args.output.resolve() / ("new" if new else "old"),
                           args.experimental, new, args.vulkan)
            reports.append(report)
            print(json.dumps(report), flush=True)
        (args.output / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(reports, indent=2))
    //! Owned ELF/DWARF data from an explicitly approved build artifact.
    use std::{collections::BTreeMap, io, sync::Arc};
    use object::{Object, ObjectSection, ObjectSymbol};
    use serde::Serialize;
    
    type Reader = gimli::EndianArcSlice<gimli::RunTimeEndian>;
    pub struct Symbols {
        context: addr2line::Context<Reader>,
        symbols: BTreeMap<u64, (String, u64)>,
    }
    #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
    pub struct Location {
        pub address: u32,
        pub symbol: Option<String>,
        pub offset: Option<u64>,
        pub file: Option<String>,
        pub line: Option<u32>,
        pub column: Option<u32>,
    }
    impl Symbols {
        pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Self> {
            if bytes.len() > 128 << 20 { return Err(io::Error::other("ELF exceeds 128 MiB")); }
            let file = object::File::parse(bytes).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            if file.format() != object::BinaryFormat::Elf || file.architecture() != object::Architecture::Arm || !file.is_little_endian() {
                return Err(io::Error::other("expected a little-endian ARM ELF build artifact"));
            }
            let dwarf = gimli::Dwarf::load(|section| -> io::Result<Reader> {
                let data = file.section_by_name(section.name()).map(|s| s.uncompressed_data())
                    .transpose().map_err(io::Error::other)?.unwrap_or_default();
                if data.len()>64<<20 { return Err(io::Error::other("DWARF section exceeds budget")); }
                Ok(Reader::new(Arc::from(data.as_ref()), gimli::RunTimeEndian::Little))
            })?;
            let context = addr2line::Context::from_dwarf(dwarf).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            let mut symbols = BTreeMap::new();
            for symbol in file.symbols().filter(|s| s.is_definition() && s.address()<=u64::from(u32::MAX)) {
                if let Ok(name) = symbol.name() {
                    if !name.is_empty() && !name.starts_with('$') {
                        symbols.insert(symbol.address() & !1, (name.to_string(), symbol.size()));
                    }
                }
            }
            Ok(Self { context, symbols })
        }
        pub fn locate(&self, address: u32) -> io::Result<Location> {
            let pc = u64::from(address & !1);
            let symbol = self.symbols.range(..=pc).next_back()
                .filter(|(base, (_,size))| *size == 0 || pc < **base+size);
            let location = self.context.find_location(pc).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            Ok(Location { address, symbol: symbol.map(|(_, (name,_))| name.clone()),
                offset: symbol.map(|(base,_)| pc-base),
                file: location.as_ref().and_then(|l| l.file.map(str::to_string)),
                line: location.as_ref().and_then(|l| l.line), column: location.and_then(|l| l.column) })
        }
        pub fn resolve(&self, query: &str) -> io::Result<Vec<u32>> {
            if query.is_empty() || query.len()>1024 { return Err(io::Error::other("invalid symbol query")); }
            if let Some((path,line)) = query.rsplit_once(':').filter(|(_,s)| s.parse::<u32>().is_ok()) {
                let line = line.parse::<u32>().map_err(io::Error::other)?;
                let mut result = Vec::new();
                for (address,_,location) in self.context.find_location_range(0,1u64<<32).map_err(io::Error::other)?.take(1_000_000) {
                    if location.line == Some(line) && location.file.is_some_and(|file| file.replace('\\',"/").ends_with(&path.replace('\\',"/"))) {
                        result.push(address as u32);
                        if result.len()==128 { break; }
                    }
                }
                return Ok(result);
            }
            Ok(self.symbols.iter().filter(|(_, (name,_))| name==query).take(128).map(|(address,_)| *address as u32).collect())
        }
        pub fn count(&self) -> usize { self.symbols.len() }
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
        #[test] fn rejects_non_elf_and_host_elf() {
            assert!(Symbols::parse(b"not an ELF").is_err());
            assert!(Symbols::parse(&[0;52]).is_err());
        }
    }
    /* Freestanding ARM11 fixture: no firmware, commercial content or host libraries. */
    typedef unsigned int u32;
    typedef unsigned long long u64;
    volatile u32 mode = 0;
    volatile u32 watched = 0x11223344;
    volatile u32 counter = 1;
    volatile u32 canary[2] = {0xcafebabe, 0xdeadbeef};
    
    __attribute__((noinline)) static void output(const char* text, u32 length) {
        register const char* r0 __asm__("r0") = text;
        register u32 r1 __asm__("r1") = length;
        __asm__ volatile("svc 0x3d" : "+r"(r0), "+r"(r1) :: "r2", "r3", "memory");
    }
    
    __attribute__((noinline)) void tick(void) {
        watched = ++counter;
        if (mode == 1) watched = *(volatile u32*)0;
        if (mode == 2) canary[1] = 0xbad;
        if (mode == 3) {
            register u32 r0 __asm__("r0") = 0;
            __asm__ volatile("svc 0x3c" : "+r"(r0) :: "r1", "r2", "r3", "memory");
        }
        if (mode == 4) __asm__ volatile(".word 0xe7f000f0");
    }
    
    __attribute__((noinline)) int main(void) {
        static const char ready[] = "lotus-fixture:ready\n";
        output(ready, sizeof(ready)-1);
        for (;;) tick();
    }
    
    __attribute__((naked, section(".text.start"), used)) void _start(void) {
        __asm__ volatile("bl main\n1: b 1b");
    }

    class DebugTools {

        explicit DebugTools(Core::System& system, const std::filesystem::path& root)
            : system(system), root(root), bindings(SettingsBindings()) {}
    
    #ifdef CTR_EXPERIMENTAL

                [this](const char* reason,Json data){Stop(reason,std::move(data));});

                if (stopped) return true;
                if (stepping) return false;

                    if (bp.kind != "execute" || bp.address != core.GetPC()) continue;
                    if (skip_core == core.GetID() && skip_pc == core.GetPC()) {
                        skip_core = 0xffffffff;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if (bp.process && (!process || *bp.process != process->process_id)) continue;
                    ++bp.hits;
                    if (bp.hits < bp.hit_after || !Matches(bp.condition, core)) continue;
                    if (!bp.log.empty()) { Record("logpoint", {{"breakpoint", id}, {"text", bp.log}, {"pc", core.GetPC()}}); continue; }
                    Stop("breakpoint", {{"breakpoint", id}, {"address", bp.address}, {"core", core.GetID()},
                                       {"thread", thread->thread_id}, {"process", process ? process->process_id : 0}});

            }
